Now, in this coupled system, artificial intelligence and machine learning have driven progress toward the understanding of the nonlinear composition–process–property relationships. But their predictive reliability is limited by patchy data and low reproducibility in manual experiments. Therefore, controlling lab environments and generating reproducible data with help from autonomous laboratories is paramount to accelerate predictive design. This review highlights recent progress in data driven materials discovery and closed loop experiments in perovskite research. We also report that AI guided process optimization is capable of identifying reproducible manufacturing windows. In parallel, robotic manipulation, high throughput synthesis with in situ monitoring and autonomous characterization are enabling systematic exploration of the multi‐dimensional process space.
nb35f188243a6: Advancing free‐form‐factor electronics is essential to broaden their applicability of electronics. In this regard, the development of stretchable semiconductors and their systems that offer both excellent stretchability with outstanding optoelectronic properties is imperative. Among various optoelectronic material candidates, metal‐halide perovskite has emerged as the most promising semiconductors owing to their high charge mobility, long exciton diffusion length and tunable bandgap. However, compared to stretchable organic‐based devices, stretchable perovskite devices have been rarely investigated because of perovskites’ inherently low mechanical stretchability. In this regard, to develop stretchable perovskite optoelectronics, identifying the fundamental determinants of their low mechanical deformability and establishing of strategies to overcome these limitations are crucial. In this context, this paper presents the first in‐depth overview of stretchability characteristics of perovskite‐based optoelectronic device, highlighting key strategies for realizing next‐generation stretchable platforms from material and geometric perspectives. In detail, background on mechanical deformation behaviors of stretchable devices is provided. Subsequently, we examine reported studies on stretchable perovskite optoelectronic devices according to their materials and device structures. Finally, current challenges and important issues that remain unresolved but must be addressed to enable meaningful progress are discussed.
nc4e6a538c75a: Aqueous supercapacitors (SCs) are attractive energy storage devices owing to their high power density and operational safety; however, their practical deployment is constrained by the limited operating voltage window imposed by water electrolysis, which restricts the attainable energy density. Herein, we report a lead (Pb) single‐atom anchored on nitrogen‐doped carbon (SA‐Pb/NC), where Pb, as a p‐block metal, modulates the adsorption strength of H*/H2O species at Pb‐N4 sites. Such modulation effectively suppresses water‐electrolysis reactions, thereby expanding the electrochemical operational voltage window and enhancing energy storage performance. SA‐Pb/NC delivers a specific capacitance of 530.07 F g−1, nearly twice that of bare NC. A symmetric SA‐Pb/NC device further achieves an energy density of 38.67 Wh kg−1 within an ultrawide voltage window of 1.50 V. Remarkably, no detectable H2 evolution is observed for the SA‐Pb/NC device even after 48 h of continuous operation, whereas the NC‐based device generates 0.09 µmol of H2 within only 12 h. Theoretical calculations further reveal that SA‐Pb sites optimize K+ adsorption–desorption kinetics while weakening the affinity for H2O‐derived intermediates, thereby enabling efficient charge storage and effective suppression of water electrolysis. This work provides a general strategy for designing high‐energy‐density aqueous supercapacitors through voltage‐window expansion enabled by lead single‐atom sites.
nef2a074feae5: Aqueous Supercapacitors The cover contrasts conventional nitrogen‐doped carbon (left) with Pb single‐atom decorated nitrogen‐doped carbon (right). While the pristine electrode suffers from water electrolysis accompanied by hydrogen and oxygen bubble generation, Pb single atoms suppress parasitic gas evolution, enabling efficient charge storage and transport. This atomic‐scale design delivers stable, high‐energy‐density aqueous supercapacitors. More in article number e70900, Min‐Cheol Kim, Jung Kyu Kim, and co‐workers.
n13e2017a31a4: The conjugated ionic additive MeQAPyBF4 synergistically combines interfacial engineering and bulk passivation for PTAA-based n-i-p PSCs. Its cationic π-conjugated moiety localizes at grain boundaries and the perovskite/PTAA interface, tuning energy levels, passivating defects, and improving hole extraction, while the anion targets the buried perovskite/SnO2 interface. This enables PSCs with 26.17% PCE and enhanced stability. Abstract Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) based on poly[bis(4-phenyl) (2,4,6-trimethylphenyl) amine] (PTAA) as the hole transport material offer excellent thermal stability but still suffer from open-circuit voltage (V OC) losses that limit their power conversion efficiency (PCE). These losses are primarily attributed to interfacial defects, energy level mismatches, and suboptimal contact with charge transport layers, which induce non-radiative recombination. Here, a conjugated ionic additive designed to synergistically integrate interfacial engineering and bulk passivation is reported. The cationic π-conjugated moiety localizes at grain boundaries and the perovskite/PTAA interface, enabling energy level tuning, defect passivation, and enhanced hole extraction, while the anionic counterpart preferentially resides at the buried perovskite/SnO2 interface, passivating interfacial defects and improving film quality. This dual-site modulation yields high-quality perovskite films with suppressed energetic disorder and improved charge extraction. As a result, n-i-p structured PSCs employing PTAA achieve PCEs of (25.73 ± 0.35)%, alongside a 15.17 cm2 mini-module delivering (22.96 ± 0.61)% efficiencies. The devices exhibit outstanding stability, retaining 86% of the original PCE following 960 h of thermal aging at 85 °C in nitrogen. This work demonstrates that rationally designed conjugated ionic additives can simultaneously optimize bulk and interfacial properties, offering a viable route toward high-efficiency, stable PSCs compatible with scalable manufacturing.
n86900a58ed8c: The accelerated adoption of thermoplastic elastomers (TPEs) is driving a critical shift toward wearable electronics and highly durable energy technologies that are both mechanically durable and high‐performing. This feature‐article systematically examines the rapidly expanding role of TPEs across key device platforms, specifically organic photovoltaics and thermoelectrics, and explores how TPEs enable their synergistic integration with other crucial functionalities such as light‐emitting diodes, thin‐film transistors, photodetectors, and electrochemical transistors within advanced flexible energy systems. The integration of TPEs in various devices enables unprecedented improvements in both mechanical robustness and electronic functionality critical for sustained energy performance. The distinctive two‐phase microstructure of TPEs, which combines dynamically reversible physical crosslinks with flexible soft segments, enables tunable mechanical behavior and superior interfacial compatibility. This architecture allows TPEs to serve multiple critical functions, as flexible substrates, encapsulation layers, adhesion promoters, and toughening agents, significantly improving stretchability, structural adaptability, and performance retention under mechanical deformation for energy conversion and storage applications. By critically analyzing recent breakthroughs, this review formulates essential design guidelines and persistent challenges for optimizing TPE‐incorporated devices. Collectively, this work underscores the transformative and practical potential of TPEs in realizing advanced, intelligent, and highly durable energy‐harvesting and power‐supply systems for next‐generation wearable applications.
n518ae2568f13: Introducing tributylsulfonium iodide (TBSI) into the trimming solvent induces tilted 2D perovskite orientation, which passivates grain boundaries, enhances conductivity, and preserves the optimized 3D FAPbI3 layer. As a result, the devices achieved 26.6% efficiency (certified 26.3%) and maintained 90% of their initial efficiency after continuous operation for 1100 h at the maximum power point. Abstract Despite the high stability of 2D perovskites, high‐efficiency perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have predominantly been fabricated using pure 3D perovskites as the light‐absorbing layer. Introducing 2D perovskites into the 3D perovskite bulk typically leads to the formation of insulating spacer layers between conductive inorganic slabs, limiting the conductivity and charge transport of the 3D perovskite, thereby reducing device efficiency. This study demonstrates that these disadvantages associated with introducing 2D perovskites can be eliminated by tilting the 2D perovskite orientation. The thermodynamically stable tilted 2D perovskite orientation enhances the conductivity of 3D perovskites, improves film uniformity, and reduces defect concentration through grain boundary passivation. Additionally, the method used to induce this tilted 2D perovskite orientation does not influence the crystallization process of the highly optimized 3D perovskite. As a result, the best‐performing PSCs exhibit an efficiency of 26.6% (certified efficiency of 26.3%) under simulated solar illumination. Furthermore, encapsulated devices retain ≈90% of their initial efficiency even after 1100 h of operation under maximum power point tracking. These findings provide critical insights into overcoming the inherent limitations of conventional 2D perovskites, offering a pathway toward high‐efficiency and stable PSCs.
n50ba4ad0c726: The molecular design strategy that integrates both side chain and backbone engineering in diketopyrrolopyrrole‐based conjugated polymers to identify the optimal balance between doping efficiency and microstructural order is demonstrated. Comprehensive spectroscopic, electrochemical, morphological, and structural characterizations reveal that the polymer incorporating an asymmetric oligo(ethylene glycol) side chain and a single thiophene donor unit achieves efficient doping without disrupting molecular order, resulting in an exceptional power factor of 561.9 µW m−1 K−2. Abstract Achieving high thermoelectric performance in conjugated polymers is challenging because chemical doping perturbs the microstructure and induces electronic disorder, limiting the simultaneous enhancement of electrical conductivity (σ) and the Seebeck coefficient (S). Herein, a rational molecular design strategy is proposed for diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)‐based conjugated polymers that combines an asymmetric side‐chain configuration—a branched alkyl group on one side and a polar oligo(ethylene glycol) (OEG) group on the other—with electron‐rich donor units (thiophene, thienothiophene, and bithiophene). These structural modifications modulate energy levels, dopant miscibility, and interchain interactions, facilitating higher doping levels and favorable molecular packing for charge transport. However, doped microstructures exhibit pronounced sensitivity to the specific combination of oxygenated side chains and donor units, with increasing doping levels leading to molecular disorder or abnormal doping behavior. Among the series, PODEGT—comprising a monothiophene donor and an asymmetric OEG side chain—achieved an optimal balance between doping efficiency and structural order, thereby enabling concurrent improvements in σ and S and yielding an exceptional power factor of 561.9 µW m−1 K−2, the highest reported for DPP‐based conjugated polymers. These results establish a generalizable molecular design strategy that reconciles doping efficiency with microstructural robustness, providing a breakthrough toward high‐performance organic thermoelectrics.
nbb8ca4f9cd35: On‐skin power sources require ultrathin form factors, safety, and mechanical robustness, but few battery platforms simultaneously satisfy these requirements. Here, we report the thinnest Al–air batteries to date (<270 µm) enabled by hygroscopic hydrogel electrolytes. Operating in a water‐in‐salt regime with highly concentrated ionic species, strong ion–water interactions suppress electrolyte dehydration and Al self‐corrosion, while enabling high‐capacity operation of 2479 mAh g‒1 at 10 mA cm‒2 in ultrathin architectures. The cells withstand over 3000 bending cycles at a bending radius of 1 mm and remain functional under severe deformation, including crumpling, cutting, and perforation. Stable operation over more than 1000 cycles of repeated anode replacement suggests an operational lifespan exceeding 8000 h. When integrated with organic electrochemical transistor‐based biosensors, the system enables continuous, real‐time physiological signal monitoring with a signal fidelity of up to 31.1 dB, providing a viable route toward continuous operation of conformal epidermal electronic systems.
n2fd4246266ea: Aluminum–Air Batteries In article number e71309, Seung Joon Yoo, Woo‐Jin Song, Sungjun Park, and co‐workers present an ultrathin aluminum–air battery enabled by hygroscopic hydrogel electrolytes for imperceptible on‐skin electronics. Although reducing battery thickness typically limits the electrolyte reservoir and energy capacity, the hygroscopic electrolyte continuously captures ambient moisture while the air cathode utilizes oxygen from the surrounding air. This air‐breathing and moisture‐harvesting design sustains electrochemical energy conversion in an on‐skin platform, offering a route to high‐capacity power sources for skin‐conformal electronics.
n7f358e3e1015: Research into halide solid electrolytes has intensified due to their high ionic conductivity, oxidation stability and ductility, yet their close-packed anion frameworks offer limited structural tunability, hindering further enhancement of bulk Li+ conduction. Here, we demonstrate a universal bulk oxygen incorporation strategy for halide solid electrolytes, using WO2Cl2 to enable controlled introduction of oxygen into diverse Li x MCl6 (M = Zr, Y, Er, and In) lattices, effectively enhancing Li+ conduction. Complementary structural, spatial, and vibrational analyses, including synchrotron X-ray techniques, depth-resolved spectroscopy, and Raman measurements, confirm oxygen incorporation via the [WO2Cl4]2− polyhedral unit, validating the structural integrity of the modified halides. First-principles calculations reveal that the anchored oxygen flattens the Li+ migration energy landscape by diversifying Li sites and weakening Li–Cl interactions, accounting for the observed conductivity enhancement. In addition, the alleviation of the thermodynamic driving force for hydrolysis improves air and moisture stability, and the enhancement in ionic conductivity leads to improved electrochemical performance. These oxygen-anchored oxychlorides offer lattice-level regulation principles that underpin conventional halide design, ensuring both practicality and broad applicability.
naeaae48e2302: For perovskite solar cells (PSCs), despite the remarkable advancements in power conversion efficiency and environmental stability, degradation under operational conditions remains a barrier between research and commercialization. Understanding and monitoring the underlying physics of electronic band gap states during degradation as a result of ambient conditions is essential for further improvements in device stability. Here, advanced defect spectroscopy utilizing thermally stimulated currents (TSC) coupled to a metal‐insulator‐semiconductor (MIS) structure is used to determine the energetic landscape of band gap states in relevant state‐of‐the‐art triple cation mixed halide (TCMH) perovskite samples to demonstrate the capabilities of this method. MIS TSC is used to resolve the electrical effect of degradation induced by ambient conditions and natural illumination. Coupling these findings to optoelectronic and structural analysis of individual perovskite layers and functional PSCs, a correlation between material degradation, device performance and trap state evolution can be obtained. We find that with aging under ambient conditions and exposure to light, in TCMH the electron trap density is reduced, while the density of detected hole states increases. For this unexpected behavior, we propose a change of trap type and polarity during degradation.
nda48e702c936: Despite architectural advances, current nerve guidance conduits inadequately replicate the mechanoactive microenvironment required for functional neural regeneration. While membrane tension is increasingly recognized as an important biomechanical regulator of axonal extension and glial behavior, its therapeutic exploitation in peripheral nerve repair remains limited. Whether and how membrane tension‐related cues are relayed from support cells to neurons also remains unclear. Here, we developed a magneto‐mechanical augmentation strategy by functionalizing mesenchymal stem cells with superparamagnetic Fe3O4@polydopamine nanoparticles (FP@MSCs) and incorporating these cells into an aligned PCL/GelMA conduit. Under static magnetic stimulation, FP@MSCs showed increased membrane tension, cytoskeletal remodeling, and accelerated differentiation toward a Schwann cell‐like phenotype. Mechanistically, transcriptomic profiling and protein‐protein interaction mapping pointed to TIMP1 as a candidate paracrine mediator, which subsequently activated the ITGB1/CD63–FAK axis in recipient NE‐4C cells. Further analyses, including atomic force microscopy and osmotic perturbation, indicated that elevated membrane tension drove TIMP1 secretion, which subsequently amplified membrane tension in NE‐4C and promoted neuronal differentiation. In a rat 15 mm sciatic nerve gap model, the magneto‐mechanically activated conduit promoted motor, sensory and histological recovery. Together, these findings support a TIMP1‐dependent intercellular mechanotransductive pathway and suggest a magneto‐mechanical strategy for enhancing the regenerative performance of nerve guidance conduits.
n38e6d13d9d02: Burn wound repair requires not only rapid wound closure but also coordinated regulation of the evolving pathological processes across distinct healing stages to minimize scar formation. However, many existing wound dressings address only isolated aspects of healing and are often limited by burst release, short local retention, and insufficient intracellular delivery. Here, we report ATMP@Gel, a GelMA hydrogel incorporating an activatable tetrahedral miR‐146a‐5p nanoprodrug (ATMP), for multistage regulation of burn wound repair. The tetrahedral nanoframework improves miRNA stability and cellular uptake, while the hydrogel matrix prolongs local delivery; RNase H‐responsive activation further contributes to increasing the functionally available intracellular pool of miR‐146a‐5p. ATMP@Gel attenuates excessive inflammation and oxidative stress during early repair, shifts the macrophage marker profile toward a reparative state, and suppresses fibroblast overactivation and profibrotic remodeling at later stages of healing. In a murine full‐thickness burn model, ATMP@Gel accelerates wound closure and promotes angiogenesis, re‐epithelialization, restoration of skin appendage structures, and more normal‐like collagen architecture, while reducing residual scar area and scar‐associated fibrosis. Together, these findings demonstrate a miRNA nanoprodrug hydrogel strategy that integrates sustained local delivery with responsive intracellular regulation to coordinate multiple pathological processes throughout burn wound healing.
ne538052527b3: The increasing demand for flexible and rigid polyurethane foams has intensified the need for sustainable end‐of‐life management strategies. In this study, a strategy combining vinylogous urethane chemistry with oleochemistry to develop non‐isocyanate, bio‐based polymer foams with enhanced recyclability is employed. This approach presents a universal platform for fabrication of recyclable foams with tunable mechanical properties, ranging from flexible, elastic foams to rigid, stiff materials, owing to the versatile chemistry of vinylogous urethane networks. Moreover, the ability to control gelling and foaming kinetics leads to the fabrication of non‐isocyanate foams with beneficial low‐density (60–70 kg m−3) that can compete with typical conventional polyurethane foams. These findings indicate that the vinylogous urethane foams derived from renewable vegetable oils provide a promising strategy for addressing end‐of‐life concerns associated with conventional polyurethane foam applications.
n4138ade591a3: Multi‐field sensing luminescent crystals responsive to linearly polarized UV light, X‐rays, and temperature show great value in high‐precision thermometry and non‐destructive testing. Herein, we report a centimeter‐sized zero‐dimensional Mn‐based hybrid metal halide (C11H8F2N)2MnCl4 via an organic‐inorganic coupling strategy, integrating anisotropic photoluminescence, scintillation, and anti‐thermal‐quenching properties. The anisotropic arrangement of organic cations enables polarization‐dependent Mn2+ emission with a polarization degree of 0.36, realizing quantitative detection of the electric field vector for the first time in hybrid metal halides. The 0D configuration also suppresses non‐radiative transitions, resulting in a high photoluminescence quantum yield of 94.6% and a scintillation light yield of 27,000 photons/MeV under X‐ray excitation, with a low detection limit of 2.19 µGy/s and a high spatial resolution of 11.1 LP/mm. Furthermore, the adaptive fine‐tuning of organic cation spatial configuration with increasing temperature modulates their light absorption, leading to a pronounced anti‐thermal‐quenching behavior of Mn2+ luminescence with a 1.73‐fold enhancement over 20–260 K. Using 1% Sb3+ doping, a ratiometric temperature sensor is achieved with a maximum absolute sensitivity of 0.392 K−1 at 300 K and relative sensitivity of 3.88%·K−1 at 20 K, displaying excellent overall performance. This work provides a new strategy for designing multi‐field sensing hybrid metal halides.
n240dab39b773: The rapid growth of electric vehicles and portable electronics has intensified the demand for high‐energy‐density batteries. Accordingly, the development of advanced battery systems with high performance and broad compatibility has emerged as a dominant research direction in energy storage. The combination of solid‐state polymer electrolytes (SPEs) and lithium (Li) metal anodes is considered a core and effective strategy to realize high‐energy‐density and high‐safety batteries. However, issues such as poor solid–solid interface contact between the solid‐state electrolyte and electrode and uncontrollable interfacial side reactions have long been the critical bottlenecks restricting their performance and practical application. This review systematically revisits the evolution of electrolyte fabrication strategies from conventional ex situ preparation to in situ polymerization and reveals the technological progression from simple electrolyte fabrication toward integrated interphase engineering for high‐performance solid‐state batteries. In particular, we focus on the engineering of the interphase formed during the polymerization, revealing the conceptual shift and scientific connotations from suppressing side reactions to rationally utilizing them. Finally, we present perspectives on the essential challenges and development opportunities of in situ polymerization toward practical solid‐state batteries.
naa0ece2cdb00: Textile triboelectric nanogenerators (t‐TENGs) are a promising platform for self‐powered e‐textiles, converting mechanical human motion into electrical energy for harvesting and sensing, while benefiting from the softness, breathability, deformability, and large specific surface area offered by textile substrates. Among available fabrication strategies, solution processing is particularly attractive because it is additive, material‐efficient, roll‐to‐roll compatible, and readily adaptable to yarn‐ and fabric‐level functionalization under ambient or relatively low‐temperature conditions. This paper reviews solution‐processed t‐TENGs from the perspectives of printing techniques, ink formation, and applications. Key parameters governing functional ink design, including solvent selection, additive chemistry, rheological behavior, substrate wettability, and post‐treatment, are discussed. Printable inks are then categorized according to their function in the t‐TENGs, including conductive inks, tribo‐negative inks, and tribo‐positive inks, covering representative material systems based on metals, conductive polymers, carbon nanomaterials, silicones, fluoropolymers, and biodegradable polymers. The review further summarizes emerging applications of solution‐processed t‐TENGs in wearable power, self‐powered sensing, physiological monitoring, human–machine interfaces, and smart‐home systems, while discussing key challenges in durability, washability, environmental compatibility, scalable manufacturing, and power management. By linking material chemistry, ink design, textile processing, and device architecture, it provides practical guidance for developing high‐performance, scalable, and sustainable t‐TENGs.
nb54d3c631701: Covalent organic framework (COF) membranes hold significant promise for energy‐efficient desalination, yet achieving precise control over their crystallization and selective‐layer architecture remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report an amino‐acid‐assisted interfacial polymerization (AAIP) strategy that regulates reaction‐diffusion dynamics to enable the fabrication of highly crystalline, ultramicroporous membranes. L‐cysteine serves as a bifunctional molecular modulator, through cooperative electrostatic and hydrogen‐bond interactions to sequester isophthalic dihydrazide (IPH) monomers, thereby regulating monomer transport toward the reaction interface. The resulting reaction‐diffusion‐controlled growth facilitates the emergence of Turing‐patterned surface structure and promotes an ordered ABC‐stacked framework with high crystallinity. The resulting Tp‐IPH‐Cys20% membrane exhibits a refined ultramicroporous architecture. When tested with 2000 ppm NaCl feed solution under an operating pressure of 15 bar, the Tp‐IPH‐Cys20% membrane delivers a NaCl rejection rate of 98.1% and a water permeance of 1.0 L m−2 h−1 bar−1, outperforming conventional COF membranes while demonstrating exceptional durability under both acidic exposure and 104 h of continuous hydraulic stress. More broadly, this work establishes amino‐acid‐directed reaction‐diffusion engineering as a versatile strategy for controlling the evolution of crystalline porous membranes, offering new pathways for mitigating the permeability‐selectivity trade‐off in advanced separation materials.
na59cfdc388df: Distributed solar‐driven interfacial evaporation coupled with water electrolysis offers a sustainable route to simultaneously address water scarcity and energy crises. However, reliable integrated system design and disruption of high‐energy barrier imposed by strong hydrogen bonds remain key challenges. To solve these problems, an integrated solar‐driven coupling system was designed based on the unified TiN/TiO2 (N‐TiO2) platform, while two separate modules were developed based on photothermal Ag2@N‐TiO2 evaporator and Ni4Co1@N‐TiO2 electrocatalyst, achieving synchronous production and adjustment of freshwater and green hydrogen according to the target application scenario. Using active N‐TiO2 sites for water molecule adsorption and activation, Ag2@N‐TiO2 and Ni4Co1@N‐TiO2 heterostructures can break hydrogen bonding networks and weaken H‐O‐H bonds through strong interfacial interactions. Notably, quasi‐in situ Raman captures the release of low‐barrier “weakly hydrogen‐bonded water” from Ag2@N‐TiO2 interface, which reduces the vaporization latent heat for effective evaporation. Meanwhile, the Ni4Co1@N‐TiO2 interface promotes the release of active hydrogen (H*) to accelerate the Volmer step, thereby optimizing the hydrogen production kinetics. The integrated device achieves a high evaporation rate of 2.425 kg m−2 h−1 under 1 kW m−2 and a low HER overpotential of 113 mV at 100 mA cm−2, which offers a reliable strategy for sustainable seawater desalination and green hydrogen co‐production.
n68f7caf2f3c8: Anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEM‐WE) has attracted increasing interest because it combines the compact device architecture of membrane‐based electrolyzers with the potential to utilize platinum‐group‐metal‐free catalysts. Despite rapid advances in anion exchange membrane (AEM) hydroxide conductivity and alkaline stability, with some AEMs demonstrating over 8000 h stability and conductivities approaching 300 mS cm−1, these material‐level advances have not translated proportionally into device operation. Consequently, long‐term electrolyzer lifetimes remain far below those of proton‐exchange membrane systems. In this perspective, we argue that the AEM should be considered not merely as a hydroxide‐conducting separator, but as a functional component of the membrane electrode assembly, influencing water transport, interfacial compatibility, gas crossover, and failure mechanisms. We first discuss why the conductivity and alkaline‐soaking stability of AEM alone are insufficient predictors of practical performance. We then examine coupled challenges including interfacial effects, oxidative degradation near the anode, chemical‐mechanical degradation, and the limitations of current evaluation methods. Finally, we outline how future progress may depend on integrating membrane chemistry with scalable fabrication, greener synthesis, and more consistent benchmarking protocols. We hope this perspective helps situate current membrane research within a broader device‐level context and highlights key questions for the next stage of AEM‐WE development.
nea15601c03d5: Direction‐dependent charge transport and optical responses are characteristic of van der Waals (vdW) materials with strong in‐plane anisotropy. While transition‐metal trichalcogenides (TMTCs) exemplify this behavior, heavier analogs remain largely unexplored. In this study, uranium triselenide (USe3) is investigated as an anisotropic vdW material and a heavier analog of the well‐studied TMTCs. Strong in‐plane anisotropy is revealed using polarization‐resolved Raman spectroscopy, strain‐induced shifts of phonon modes are investigated, and direction‐dependent charge‐carrier mobility is quantified through transport measurements on field‐effect devices. First‐principles calculations based on density functional theory corroborate these findings, providing a theoretical basis for the experimental observations. Casting USe3 as an actinide analog of a TMTC establishes a platform for exploring low‐dimensional semiconductors that combine strong in‐plane anisotropy with f‐electron physics.
n571dec80f42c: Achieving both high activity and long‐term stability in alkaline seawater electrolysis remains challenging. To tackle this, we devise a synergistic engineering strategy that integrates iron doping with vacancy creation to tailor the local coordination environment of RuSe2 via a hydrothermal method followed by ultrafast Joule heating, which enables the simultaneous construction of asymmetric Fe−Se−Ru sites and Se vacancies. The optimal catalyst delivers ultralow overpotentials of 12 mV (alkaline water) and 20 mV (alkaline seawater) at 10 mA·cm−2, outperforming commercial Pt/C. In an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer, it achieved a cell voltage of only 1.87 V at 1.0 A·cm−2 in alkaline seawater and operated stably for 1000 h. Combined experimental characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the superior activity and stability originate from the synergy of asymmetric Fe−Se−Ru sites and Se vacancies, which enhances water dissociation, optimizes hydrogen adsorption, and suppresses chloride corrosion. This work provides a rapid route to high‑performance Ru‑based catalysts for durable seawater electrolysis.
n16df7125f788: Electrochemical co-reduction of CO2 and NO3 − is a promising route for sustainable urea synthesis, but its efficiency is limited by kinetic mismatch between CO2RR and NO3RR, and unfavorable adsorption–migration of *CO for C─N coupling. Herein, we design a nickel single-atom catalyst anchored on ZnO (NiSA/ZnO) to coordinate CO2RR and NO3RR kinetics by promoting C─N coupling for efficient urea electrosynthesis. At −0.8 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode, NiSA/ZnO achieves urea yield rate of 41.38 mmol h−1 gcat −1 and Faradaic efficiency of 31.47%. In situ spectroscopic characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations collectively reveal the formation of atomically defined Ni─O─Zn interfacial bridges, inducing charge redistribution and intrinsic electronic gradient across adjacent metal sites. This electronic heterogeneity enables spatially differentiated reaction pathways, with Ni sites favoring for CO2 activation toward *CO formation, while neighboring Zn sites facilitate NO3 − reduction to *NH2. Meanwhile, DFT calculations suggest that the interfacial electronic gradient thermodynamically drives *CO migration from Ni to Zn sites, which co-localizes the key intermediates with a lowered barrier for subsequent C─N coupling. This work demonstrates that atomic-scale interfacial bridge engineering can overcome kinetic bottlenecks in sustainable urea electrosynthesis, providing a general principle for regulating intermediate spillover and coupling in multistep electrocatalysis.
n83d1a9c2120f: Combinatorial materials libraries span multidimensional composition spaces efficiently, but high‐resolution functional characterization across them remains difficult. Here, we demonstrate an autonomous scanning probe microscopy platform for multi‐objective exploration of ferroelectric behavior in a ternary Al1‐x‐yScxByN thin‐film library. Automated piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM), guided by Bayesian experiment planning, maps surface morphology, piezoresponse amplitude, and local switching‐loop area across composition space. Rather than seeking a single optimum, the workflow reconstructs the Pareto landscape between structural stability and ferroelectric functionality. The autonomous decision loop operates on the PFM measurement alone. Wavelength‐dispersive spectroscopy and photoluminescence (PL) provide spatially registered correlative maps of the same library. X‐ray diffraction then tests the composition, defect, and property relations the exploration uncovers. The data resolve two composition‐dependent regimes. Below about 35% Sc on the cation sublattice, the films remain smooth and well textured. Switching descriptors then correlate with a defect‐sensitive PL signal. Above this composition, X‐ray diffraction shows a loss of crystalline texture which limits the switching response. The autonomous exploration located this boundary without human intervention, in six hours of instrument time against about a month on a grid. Combinatorial libraries thereby become tractable maps of coupled composition, defect, structure, and property relationships.
nbe2a3d1d7f2a: Unbalanced charge transport is a critical bottleneck in non‐fullerene organic solar cells. Here, we present a strategy to synergistically overcome this limitation in layer‐by‐layer (LbL) processed D18/L8‐BO devices by incorporating two‐dimensional SnSe2 nanoflakes at the donor/acceptor heterojunction. The dispersed SnSe2 acts as discrete charge‐transporting bridges between the D18 and L8‐BO layers, optimizing interfacial energetics, facilitating exciton dissociation, accelerating electron transport, and suppressing recombination. Consequently, the electron mobility is significantly enhanced while the hole/electron mobility ratio approaches unity, signifying balanced carrier transport. Thus, the power conversion efficiency increases markedly from 18.92% to 20.03%, with improved short‐circuit current density and fill factor. This work demonstrates a novel strategy of integrating 2D n‐type semiconductors with the LbL systems and provides an effective pathway toward high‐efficiency organic solar cells with balanced carrier transport and boosted exciton dissociation.
n42a2f5fc30dd: Achieving wide‐coverage near‐infrared (NIR) luminescence spanning from NIR‐I to NIR‐II regions in Cr3+‐sensitized rare‐earth‐ion (RE3+) phosphor systems without sacrificing the Cr3+ emission intensity remains a significant challenge. Herein, a novel double‐perovskite‐structured Cs2RbScF6 host with large interionic separation was first discovered, which enables successful full substitution of Sc3+ by Cr3+ without concentration quenching. The resulting Cs2RbCrF6 phosphor exhibits broadband NIR emission centered at 775 nm with a full width at half maximum of ∼118 nm, and high internal/external quantum efficiencies of 84.2%/32.1%. More importantly, this Cr‐rich host serves as an effective sensitizing platform for RE3+ ions (i.e., Yb3+, Nd3+, Er3+), extending the spectral coverage from 650 to 1600 nm via efficient Cr3+→RE3+ energy transfer, while remarkably retaining substantial Cr3+ emission intensity. This balanced coexistence of intense broadband Cr3+ and multiple RE3+ characteristic emissions enables a genuinely wide‐coverage NIR luminescence profile spanning 650–1600 nm. Finally, a prototype NIR phosphor‐converted LEDs device was fabricated and innovatively demonstrated practical utility for quantitatively monitoring various RE3+ concentrations and detecting aqueous‐phase entrainment in the organic phase during solvent extraction. This work provides a rational design strategy for developing high‐efficiency wide‐coverage NIR phosphors and offers a new broadband NIR light source for real‐time monitoring of RE solvent extraction processes.
n11cc7148ef72: The performance of wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskite sub‐cells in tandem solar cells is largely constrained by grain boundary and surface defects, along with unfavorable interfacial energy level alignment. To address these issues, we propose a bilayer co‐ligand post‐treatment strategy, initially employing 3‐(methylthio)propylamine hydroiodide (3MTPAI) and 1, 3‐propanediamine dihydroiodide (PDAI2), followed by a secondary piperazinium iodide (PI) layer. In this design, 3MTPAI penetrates the grain boundaries to passivate both grain boundary and surface defects, thereby suppressing non‐radiative recombination, while PDAI2 forms an initial surface dipole layer to enhance the built‐in electric field. The subsequent PI layer not only passivates residual defects but also generates a second dipole layer that acts synergistically with the first, facilitating carrier transport at the interface. Consequently, the optimized WBG (1.68 eV) single‐junction and tandem devices achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 23.55% and 32.33%, respectively, and show no efficiency loss after 500 h of operation. This work demonstrates that the bilayer co‐ligand strategy offers valuable insights for developing efficient and stable single‐junction and tandem solar cells.
n881adbaa3f6a: The practical deployment of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) is critically hindered by rampant dendrite growth and parasitic side reactions, originating from unregulated Zn2 + solvation chemistry and unstable electrode-electrolyte interfaces. Inspired by the zinc-targeting molecular recognition mechanism of angiotensin-converting-enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, we repurpose clinical drug lisinopril (LIS) as a trace multifunctional electrolyte additive for high-performance AZIBs. The multidentate and amphiphilic structure of LIS orchestrates a synergistic dual-regulation mechanism: LIS spontaneously adsorbs and in situ assembles into a robust gradient organic–inorganic hybrid solid electrolyte interphase that homogenizes Zn2+ flux and establishes a water-depleted electric double layer by its hydrophobic moieties; meanwhile LIS alters the [Zn(H2O)6]2+ solvation shell, disrupts the native hydrogen-bond network, and buffers interfacial pH fluctuations at the anode interface. Consequently, trace LIS enables highly reversible Zn plating/stripping, with Zn||Cu cells delivering an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.78% over 1500 cycles and Zn||Zn cells operating for 2400 h at 4 mA cm−2/4 mAh cm−2. Remarkably, the LIS-containing full cells retain 77.25% of their capacity after 10 000 cycles, and pouch cells maintain 74.46% capacity after 600 cycles. This work illustrates that pharmaceutical molecules with inherent Zn-binding motifs can be converted into function-oriented electrolyte additives to achieve durable AZIBs.
n36c202761792: Passive photoluminescent textiles hold great promise for emergency signaling in extreme environments, yet preventing the loss or quenching of luminescent particles under water, ice, and abrasion remains a major challenge. Inspired by the transparent skin protection mechanism of Aequorea victoria, we propose a periodic electrospinning‐ electrospraying synergistic strategy to fabricate a bioinspired superhydrophobic electrospun luminescence film (ELF) with a unique hierarchical “skeleton‐and‐flesh” composite structure. The transparent “skin” air cushion protective layer, endowed with stable superhydrophobicity, enables the ELF to persistently luminesce for over 180 s in both dark air and underwater environments. White and colored luminescence yarns are obtained via high‐temperature twisting and can be applied to patterned embroidery, encrypted optical messaging, and underwater warning displays. The woven centimeter‑scale textile exhibits significantly enhanced superhydrophobic stability, withstanding >120 min washing, 20 abrasion cycles, and anti‑icing at −28°C, showing potential for protective clothing in extreme cold wild environments. A proof‐of‐concept for a rescue experiment of a trapped underwater diver has been successfully demonstrated. This bioinspired strategy opens a new pathway for passive and durable optical signaling in harsh environments.
ne6233a7ceb4d: The practical application of lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries is severely hindered by the intrinsically sluggish redox kinetics and uncontrolled shuttle behavior of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs), while current catalytic strategies remain limited by insufficient integration of adsorption–conversion functionalities and inefficient interfacial electron transfer. Herein, we propose a Mo–O/Mo–N entangled coordination framework by coupling atomically dispersed Mo sites with an amorphous MoO3‐x–MoN heterojunction on conductive MXene nanosheets. This architecture enables a triple‐site synergistic mechanism, where oxygen‐deficient MoO3‐x ensures strong chemisorption of LiPSs, MoN accelerates catalytic conversion, and Mo single atoms further optimize the interfacial electronic structure and reaction kinetics. Benefiting from the synergistic modulation of adsorption strength and catalytic activity, the designed interlayer effectively suppresses LiPSs diffusion and promotes rapid and reversible sulfur redox reactions. As a result, the Li–S batteries deliver an ultralow capacity decay of 0.019% per cycle over 1400 cycles at 1 C, along with a high areal capacity of 5.35 mAh cm−2 under practical sulfur loading. This work provides new insights into atomic‐level coordination engineering and heterointerface design for advanced Li–S batteries.
n38c8ad8ec72f: Reliable energy storage in electrostatic capacitors requires dielectric materials that can withstand extreme thermal and electrical stresses, a demand that exceeds the capabilities of many commercial polymers. Cross-linking offers a promising route to improved thermal and electrical robustness, but existing strategies often depend on polymer-specific reactive groups, harsh activation conditions, or byproducts that limit broader adoption. Herein, we report a post-polymerization cross-linking strategy based on carbene-mediated C–H insertion, enabled by a stepwise thermal activation protocol. Using commercial fluorinated polyimide (FPI) and the commercial bis-diazirine cross-linker BLD201 as a model system, this approach yields free-standing cross-linked films with a high cross-linking efficiency of 95.8% at only 2 wt.% BLD201, despite the exclusive presence of aromatic/sp 2 C–H bonds in the polymer backbone. The resulting cross-linked FPI films exhibit outstanding capacitive energy storage performance, along with excellent spatial uniformity and long-term durability. A maximum discharged energy density of 4.4 J cm−3 is achieved at 250°C, which is among the highest values reported for state-of-the-art polymer films under comparable conditions. This work establishes thermally activated carbene cross-linking as a versatile route for transforming commercial aromatic polymers into thermally resilient electrostatic energy storage materials.
n6b50046c064c: Chiral perovskite nanocrystals (NCs) with strong circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) hold enormous potential for applicating in chiral optoelectronic fields, including 3D displays, chiral sensing, anti‐counterfeiting, and information storage. Nevertheless, the weak luminescence asymmetry and insufficient stability of CPL‐active perovskite NCs have severely hampered their practical applications. Herein, through a solvent‐induced in situ crystallization method, the MAPbBr3 NCs were successfully embedded into the network of blue‐emitting chiral peptide glass (L/D‐Zn‐Car). The L‐Zn‐Car chiral peptide glass acts as both a chiral template and a protective matrix, offering a confined chiral microenvironment for the nucleation and growth of MAPbBr3 NCs. Theoretical calculations combined with experimental evidences collectively confirm the strong coordination interactions between MAPbBr3 NCs and L‐Zn‐Car matrix, which not only facilitate efficient chirality transfer but also effectively suppress surface trap states. The optimized MAPbBr3@L‐Zn‐Car chiral glass exhibits excellent CPL performance, featuring high luminescence asymmetry (glum: 2.14 × 10−2), remarkable photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY: 76%), and superior stability. Furthermore, the chiral light‐emitting diode (LED) fabricated based on MAPbBr3@L/D‐Zn‐Car achieves high luminous efficiency (68.5 lm/W) and prominent CPL characteristics. This work establishes a feasible strategy for the rational design of high‐performance CPL‐active perovskite materials and broadens their application prospects in chiral optoelectronic fields.
n8a61903b9027: Neuromorphic hardware requires artificial synapses (ASs) with configurable plasticity to support diverse signal-processing functions while employing device architectures that minimize interconnect complexity among functional components. Electrolyte-gated synaptic transistors enable low-voltage conductance modulation, tunable synaptic plasticity, and mechanical flexibility through ion-mediated operation. However, the use of gel or liquid electrolytes often compromises mechanical robustness and processability. Here, we report ASs based on solid-state cationic polyurethane (cPU) gate dielectrics, in which Li+ mobility is regulated by the counter-anion of the cPU. Compact Br− counter-anions suppress Li+ transport and redistribution, thereby enabling long-term synaptic plasticity. In contrast, bulky BPh4 − counter-anions weaken Li+ coordination and facilitate Li+ transport through anion exchange with Tf2N−, resulting in short-term synaptic plasticity. The counter-anion-dependent Li+ transport mechanism is validated by first-principles calculations and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. We further integrate these counter-anion-engineered devices into vertically stacked, array-level architectures that implement reconfigurable AND/OR logic and in-memory computing via multiply-accumulate operations. This strategy establishes a foundation for future neuromorphic hardware by engineering solid-state ion dynamics to achieve configurable plasticity, vertical integration, and multifunctional array-level operation.
nc416d578fd63: Altermagnets (AMs) represent an emerging magnetic phase that combines compensated antiferromagnetic order with ferromagnet-like spin-splitting, offering a new route for efficient spin-current generation. Here, we experimentally demonstrate spin-torque generation in epitaxial CrSb and reveal a pronounced crystallographic dependence of the resulting spin-orbit torques (SOTs) across the (11¯00$1\overline{1}00$) and (112¯0$11\overline{2}0$) orientations. Using spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance, we identify unconventional SOT behavior, including a finite x-polarized damping-like torque and reversal of the y-polarized damping-like torque between the two crystal planes, features that cannot be explained by conventional spin Hall or Rashba–Edelstein mechanisms. The damping-like torque efficiencies are comparable to those of heavy metals and exhibit strong in-plane anisotropy directly linked to crystal symmetry. Symmetry analysis shows that the observed angular dependence originates from a crystallographic torque permitted by the C 2v point group, whereas AM-specific contributions from the magnetic spin Hall and spin-splitter effects remain negligible due to the multi-domain state and weak strain-induced g-to-d spin symmetry deformation in CrSb. These findings show that epitaxial CrSb can host strongly anisotropic spin-torques governed primarily by crystallographic and interfacial symmetry, providing a route toward crystallographically engineered spintronic devices.
n15c4c7728120: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising protective interlayers to mitigate Zn dendrite growth and parasitic side reactions, yet their aqueous vulnerability and unresolved electronic mechanisms hamper practical application. Herein, we propose an electronic structure engineering strategy via d-p orbital hybridization to customize the Zn anode interphase. Using UiO-66 derivatives (-NH2, -COOH, and -F4) as models, theoretical calculations reveal that strengthening the substituents’ electron-withdrawing capability deepens d-p orbital coupling and shifts the π* d-band center toward the Fermi level, thus inducing intense spatial charge polarization and enhancing Zn2+ affinity. Experimentally, the highly fluorinated UiO-66-F4 achieves the highest Zn2+ adsorption, drives selective SO4 2− exclusion, accelerates desolvation, and enables rapid ion transport. Synergizing with inherent physical hydrophobicity, this unique electronic-physical dual-shield of the UiO-66-F4 interlayer effectively averts H2O-induced side reactions and ensures highly reversible Zn plating/stripping. Consequently, the Zn@UiO-66-F4 anode delivers a 3600 h lifespan at 5 mA cm−2 and sustains 560 h under a stringent 90% depth of discharge, outperforming most MOF-modified anodes. Furthermore, flexible full cells exhibit impressive cycling stability and reliably power wearable systems even under severe deformation. Overall, this work establishes d-p orbital hybridization regulation as a powerful paradigm for customizing advanced functional interlayers toward ultra-stable Zn metal anodes.
n1879e8741a7e: Freshwater scarcity is a global challenge, increasingly compounded by heavy metal contamination of water systems. Solar-driven interfacial evaporation has emerged as a compelling solution owing to its energy efficiency and environmental benignity. Inspired by a desert plant − Alhagi camelorum, we develop a biomass-based composite nanofibrous membrane to facilitate the capture of heavy metals in contaminated water and solar-driven water evaporation. Following the electrospinning of cellulose, chitosan, and an indium-based metal–organic framework (MIL-68(In)), the in situ growth of copper oxide (CuO) nanoflowers is realized on the nanofiber network. The hierarchical porous network − assembled from interwoven nanofibers decorated with roughened nanoflowers − enables exceptional broadband light trapping. Meanwhile, the CuO nanoflowers serve as a catalytic interface, activating interfacial water molecules through efficient charge transfer that lowers the dissociation energy barrier, thereby enabling rapid and stable vapor generation. Under one-sun irradiation (1 kW m− 2), the membrane achieves an evaporation rate of 2.80 kg m− 2 h− 1 and a photothermal conversion efficiency of 98.95%. Density functional theory calculations elucidate the atomistic and electronic mechanisms underpinning this exceptional performance. This biomass-derived photothermal membrane simultaneously combines the capture of heavy metals and water purification, representing a meaningful advance in water purification and resource recovery.
n5754f34d0f36: Micro‐LED displays offer high brightness, high efficiency, and fast response, but large‐area manufacturing still faces challenges. However, reducing chip‐solution waste and repairing poor sub‐pixels are critical challenges that should be addressed for the commercial production of micro‐LED displays. Here, we present a dielectrophoretic injection‐suction printing (DEP‐ISP) process for fluid assembly of micro‐LED chips. This method reduces chip‐solution consumption, controls chip orientation using the DEP field, positions chips through subpixel grooves, and enables repair of misaligned chips. Using this approach, micro‐LED chips were assembled in a metal‐down, face‐selective manner at 390 subpixel sites per test cell, achieving an assembly yield of 99.8% and an orientation yield of 100% across six test cells. The assembled chips were then transferred to a PDMS/glass substrate under DEP conditions, producing a micro‐LED array device with an average displacement error of 1.62 µm and a transfer yield of 100%. SiO2 shell engineering further improved assembly selectivity, while repair processing increased the yield of misassembled chips. Although electrical performance still requires optimization, the successful turn‐on of some emitters confirms the feasibility of DEP‐ISP for micro‐LED integration. This study demonstrates a scalable route for micro‐LED assembly, repair, and transfer toward large‐area display fabrication.
n92d6040b6176: Micro‐LED An injection–suction printing strategy boosted by dielectrophoretic (DEP) manipulation enables the assembly, repair, and transfer of micro‐LEDs with high precision and yield. By combining controlled DEP forces with fluidic transport, individual micro‐LEDs are selectively guided to target pixels, providing a scalable and reliable manufacturing strategy for high‐resolution micro‐LED displays. More details can be found in the Research Article by Young Rag Do and co‐workers (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.77302).
nc55788e08f9c: The adsorption and dissociation of water molecules at the catalyst‐electrolyte interface dictate the activity and selectivity of the electrochemical two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction to H2O2. In this work, we report the deliberate dimensional engineering of phenanthrenequinone‑based covalent organic frameworks (PQ‑COFs) to boost H2O2 electrosynthesis via chain–chain cooperative water adsorption. Two isomeric COFs with well‑defined 1D and 2D architectures were constructed via condensation of V‑shaped or linear PQ di‐amines with a tetra‑aldehyde linker. Comprehensive characterizations confirm the formation of crystalline, imine‑linked frameworks with integrated redox‑active PQ units. Electrochemical evaluations reveal that the 1D COF exhibits superior activity and selectivity (H2O2 selectivity up to 87.7%) compared to its 2D analogue, delivering a stable H2O2 yield of 244 mg L−1 after 100 min of electrolysis in an H‑type cell. Mechanistic studies demonstrate that the closely packed 1D chains enable cooperative inter‑chain interactions, which strengthen interfacial water adsorption and reorganize hydrogen‐bonded water networks. The dynamic aqueous microenvironment accelerates water dissociation and proton transport, while optimizing the binding energy of critical intermediates to favor selective H2O2 generation.
nd60b33c11875: Cellulose nanofiber (CNF) aerogel‐based water evaporation electricity generators (EEGs) have attracted increasing attention owing to their sustainability and environmental friendliness. However, their practical application is severely hindered by wet structural stability and limited power output. Herein, we report a dual‐crosslinking strategy for constructing a high‐performance CNF‐based aerogel that simultaneously enhances mechanical robustness and hydrovoltaic electricity generation. The aerogel framework is stabilized through synergistic covalent crosslinking between CNFs and carboxymethylated chitosan, combined with metal ionic complexation, resulting in a robust yet highly hydrophilic and water‐resistant macromolecular network. This dual‐crosslinked structure enables efficient hygroscopicity and long‐term stability, facilitating spontaneous and continuous electricity generation via rapid water transport, high ionic conductivity, and strong ion selectivity. As a result, the assembled EEG delivers an output voltage of 0.92 V and a power density of 4.65 µW cm−2 in 3.5% NaCl solution, surpassing most reported EEGs. Moreover, the device demonstrates sustainability through biodegradation and regeneration, while maintaining high power outputs. These results present the strong potential of dual‐crosslinked CNF aerogels for applications in seawater desalination, wastewater treatment, low‐power energy supply, and autonomous water leakage detection, providing a promising platform for self‐powered Internet of Things sensing systems.
n9e07da17327b: Lithium‐metal all‐solid‐state batteries offer a pathway toward high‐specific‐energy storage but remain limited by instability at the solid‐state electrolyte (SSE)/Li interface. Fluorinated chloride solid electrolytes exhibit improved kinetic stability toward Li metal at low current densities (≤0.2 mA cm−2), but become increasingly susceptible to electron injection at high current densities (≥1 mA cm−2), leading to sustained reductive decomposition and interfacial degradation. Here, we develop LiCl‑deficient Li3‑xInCl5.2‑xF0.8 solid electrolytes to regulate interfacial electron transport. LiCl deficiency generates Li vacancies preferentially at 4 g sites and lowers the barrier for In migration into these vacancies, thereby forming In‐on‐Li antisites. These antisite‐centered defect environments serve as electron‐localization centers that trap injected electrons, suppress long‐range electronic transport, and inhibit the reduction of In3+ to metallic In. This electron‐localization mechanism promotes a self‐passivating interphase and markedly improves high‐current‐density compatibility with Li metal. The optimized Li2.76InCl4.96F0.8 composition exhibits an ionic conductivity of 1.24 mS cm−1, stable Li plating/stripping at 1.0–1.5 mA cm−2, and durable full‐cell cycling with LiNi0.6Co0.2Mn0.2O2 (NCM622) cathodes at 1 mA cm−2. These findings establish LiCl‐deficiency‐induced electron localization as an atomic‐scale electronic regulation strategy for enabling high‐current‐density compatibility between chloride solid electrolytes and Li‐metal anodes, thereby advancing the development of high‐specific‐energy all‐solid‐state lithium‐metal batteries.
ned680b1c52af: Oxygen vacancy (Vo) engineering is crucial for regulating electronic structures and charge responses in functional materials, yet Vo induced localized states can enhance charge localization and limit the participation of charge carriers in charge‐response processes, resulting in insufficient charge supply for defect‐mediated electronic responses. Developing a strategy that alleviates charge‐supply limitation while preserving the electronic modulation enabled by localized defect states remains challenging. To address this challenge, we investigate electronic compensation of Vo related states using Mo2C MXene/MoO3‐x heterostructures constructed through an in situ redox method, in which Mo2C MXene serves as the electron donating component and tunable Vo in MoO3‐x acts as defect‐state regulation centers. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and experimental results reveal that electron compensation from Mo2C MXene promotes defect‐mediated charge response and dielectric relaxation, thereby alleviating charge supply limitations associated with localized vacancy states and enabling systematic modulation of defect electronic structures. This defect‐state regulation is further demonstrated in electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorption, achieving an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 7.28 GHz and a minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of −51.49 dB. This work provides insight into defect state‐mediated charge regulation and provides a perspective for defect engineering toward tailoring of electronic and charge response behavior.
n2de0c961ac82: Stability at industrially relevant current densities remains a central challenge for transition-metal phosphide based hydrogen evolution electrocatalysts operating in alkaline condition. To combat catalyst degradation, here the interfacial hydroxyl chemistry is regulated by robustly constructing an amorphous CoP/CeO2− x heterostructure through a facile two-step electrodeposition strategy. Operando Raman spectroscopy combined with density functional theory calculations reveals that oxygen-vacancy-rich CeO2− x selectively captures *OH intermediates generated on Co sites, enabling efficient hydroxyl spillover away from CoP and thereby suppressing P oxidation and dissolution. The amorphous CoP framework further facilitates interfacial coupling and hydroxyl migration by providing abundant unsaturated coordination sites and dense Co/Ce interfacial contact. Benefiting from this synergistic effect, CoP/CeO2− x delivers enhanced activity together with remarkable durability, sustaining 1 A cm−2 for over 320 h in alkaline electrolyte. When implemented as the cathode in an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer, the catalyst operates stably for 750 h at 1 A cm−2 and 60°C with a low degradation rate of ≈52 µV h−1. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of interfacial hydroxyl-spillover engineering for stabilizing CoP-based electrocatalysts under practical operating conditions.
n880c0c041e65: Diabetic peri‐implantitis (DPI) is characterized by persistent and dysregulated inflammation in a hostile microenvironment, where conventional therapies fail to achieve long‐term control. Increasing evidence indicates that the key pathological feature lies not only in excessive inflammatory activation, but in the failure of inflammation resolution. Here, we propose an all‐stage inflammatory regulation strategy targeting the full progression of DPI, including initiation, propagation, and resolution. An adaptive composite gel (CGCI) was developed by integrating predominantly amorphous copper‐doped bioactive glass with a boron‐modified poly(vinyl alcohol) hydrogel. The system forms a shear‐thinning and self‐healing network, enabling injectability and effective biological sealing. The amorphous bioactive glass mediates rapid Cu ion release for early antibacterial intervention, while the hydrogel provides sustained interleukin‐10 delivery to promote macrophage‐mediated efferocytosis and vascular/lymphatic remodeling. To enable programmable delivery, structural entropy was operationalized within a model to quantitatively describe degradable hydrogel network evolution and establish a predictive framework linking structure to release kinetics. Guided by this model, CGCI achieves stage‐specific therapeutic delivery aligned with inflammation dynamics. Single‐cell transcriptomics reveals coordinated macrophage–endothelial interactions, and in DPI beagle model, CGCI enables effective all‐stage inflammatory regulation and tissue regeneration.
ne0ac9270c790: Halogen‐free solvent processed organic solar cells (OSCs) usually show much lower power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) if compared with halogenated solvents, especially for sequential deposition (SD) process. Herein, erosion‐SD processing with halogen‐free solvents was demonstrated, in which an eroded material was pre‐inserted into a donor (D18) bottom layer. Subsequent deposition of acceptor (L8‐BO) solution swells the bottom layer more easily, enabling deeper acceptor penetration and optimizing vertical phase separation. Judicious selections of eroded materials and halogen‐free solvents open chances to re‐organize SD morphology. With toluene:CS2/toluene as halogen‐free solvents and partially removable polymer acceptor PYDT as eroded material, OSCs based on D18:PYDT/L8‐BO achieved a remarkable PCE of 21.05% (certified 20.71%), greatly higher than 20.53% achieved with chloroform/chloroform solvent system. Moreover, the erosion‐SD processed 300 and 500 nm thick active layers exhibited superior PCEs of 19.64% and 18.75%, respectively, showing promising ability to re‐organize morphology toward halogen‐free solution printing.
n6c763623574e: The electro‐optic effect powers microwave‐to‐optical quantum transducers, photonic quantum computing switches, and high‐speed optical interconnects. A larger electro‐optic coefficient directly reduces the drive voltage and device footprint of electro‐optic modulators, making the search for materials with large coefficients a central challenge in photonics. Here, guided by phase‐field modeling, we engineer an electro‐optic coefficient of 43 000 pm V−1 in monoclinic KNbO3 thin films, the largest ever measured in any material, exceeding industry‐standard LiNbO3 by 1000×. This exceptional response arises from electric field‐driven “lateral swaying” of the ferroelectric polarization vector between symmetry‐equivalent monoclinic variants, which reorients the optical index ellipsoid far beyond the conventional Pockels response that relies on a linear coupling between field and polarization. The ultralow coercive fields of the monoclinic phase (∼1 kV cm−1) place this giant response within reach of standard drive electronics, enabling drive voltages orders of magnitude below the current state‐of‐the‐art. The response is stable to within 1% − 2% over hours, robust under thermal and electrical cycling, and demonstrated up to 1 MHz, establishing low‐symmetry ferroelectric phases as an unexploited design space for next‐generation energy‐efficient electro‐optic modulators for classical and quantum photonic integrated circuits.
n56a251c22fe2: Quantum‐dot (QD) color conversion pixels with partitioned black matrix (BM) enable low‐crosstalk color generation for Micro‐LED displays, yet conventional structures face an inherent trade‐off, the crosstalk‐suppressing BM induces parasitic absorption and reduces conversion efficiency. Inspired by the light‐confining core‐shell structure of optical fibers, we propose a novel reflective QD micropillar pixel architecture for high‐efficiency, crosstalk‐suppressed full‐color Micro‐LED displays. Vertically aligned QD micropillar pixel array is fabricated via in situ photolithography, followed by sidewall deposition of a highly reflective aluminum (Al) cladding layer via evaporation. Unlike conventional planar color conversion layers, where the optical path is inherently constrained by film thickness, the vertically aligned three‐dimensional (3D) micropillar fundamentally extends the interaction length between excitation light and QDs. By further enabling metal‐mirror multiple reflections of excitation light within the micropillar, this design substantially prolongs the optical path and fosters secondary excitation, leading to a marked improvement in color conversion efficiency (CCE). Furthermore, the Al cladding forms a lateral photon‐recycling microcavity, mitigating BM absorption and optical crosstalk. Breaking the efficiency and crosstalk trade‐off, our device achieves green CCE of 27.15%, red CCE of 28.6%, and an ultra‐wide color gamut of 131.54% NTSC, promising for near‐eye full‐color Micro‐LED light engines.
n566550ba00ea: In situ formed gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) improve safety and interfacial compatibility in high‐energy lithium metal batteries (LMBs), yet, simultaneously achieving long‐term cyclability, high energy density, superior rate capability, and all‐climate adaptability remains challenging. We report a viscoelastic and self‐healing GPE synthesized via a thermally triggered concurrent reaction: (i) radical copolymerization, (ii) in‐situ generation of primary amines via isocyanate hydrolysis and their subsequent nucleophilic addition to residual isocyanates to form urea, and (iii) nucleophilic ring‐opening of fluoroethylene carbonate. The dynamic hydrogen‐bond network enables autonomous healing of microcracks induced by electrode volume fluctuations, preserving intimate electrode–electrolyte contact. Polymer−solvent interactions facilitate Li+ desolvation while suppressing solvent decomposition. The polymer‐DFOB−‐derived interphase suppresses side reactions and accommodates cathode volume changes. In Li||LiNi0.83Co0.11Mn0.06O2 (NCM83) cells, the GPE‐based cell delivers 151.7 mAh g−1 at 5 C with 81.1% retention after 800 cycles. Notably, the cells exhibit exceptional wide‐temperature durability, delivering 82.9 mAh g−1 after 600 cycles at −40°C and 165.9 mAh g−1 over 200 cycles at 70°C. Even at 10 mg cm−2, the cell achieves 197.2 mAh g−1 at 0.5 C with 92.4% retention after 200 cycles. This work establishes a feasible molecular‐level paradigm for realizing high‐energy‐density, fast‐charging, and all‐climate‐adaptable LMBs.
n26c48d460a20: The development of highly efficient and stable hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts is crucial for the large‐scale production of clean hydrogen energy. Herein, PtRu composite nanomaterials confined to TiO2 nanotube arrays were prepared by anodic oxidation‐hydrothermal method, which integrated multifunctional active sites such as single‐atom Pt, single‐atom Ru, Pt clusters; Through synergistic effects, the material maintains remarkable HER activity with very low noble‐metal loadings, and significantly surpasses commercial Pt/C and PtRu/C catalysts in diverse applications. In situ infrared and Raman spectroscopy observed the interfacial adsorption of H2O and [H] formation on Pt/Ru sites, unveiling their co‑participation, while DFT calculations further clarified the synergy of multiple active sites in H2O adsorption, activation, dissociation, and [H] production. Meanwhile, by creating a state of enrichment in the hollow tubes and wall pores, the hollow structure promotes the active sites exposure and confined metal sites, while the abundant pores on the nanotube walls provide dynamic fluid channels for the timely release of hydrogen, forming gas‐liquid separation channels with the electrolyte and promoting matter exchange. This study combines surface‑rich supports and multi‑functional sites to boost noble metal utilization, and establishes gas‑liquid separation channels to promotes matter exchange, offering a strategy for ultra‑low noble metal HER electrocatalysts.
n85118d0a73ae: Developing impact‐resistant materials that simultaneously integrate self‐healing capability and printability remains challenging due to the trade‐offs among energy dissipation, chain mobility, and processability. Herein, we propose a synergistic strategy of combining hierarchical hydrogen bonding with low‐viscosity monomer polymerization to construct a photocurable polyurethane–urea elastomer (APU–HEA) for digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing. By introducing 2‐hydroxyethyl acrylate (HEA), the system achieves reduced viscosity (about 2.8 Pa·s), enhanced chain mobility, and the formation of dynamic hydrogen‐bonding networks. The resulting material exhibits high elongation (2730 ± 52%) and toughness (263 ± 3.1 MJ m−3), along with efficient self‐healing (∼91.1 ± 1.2% recovery at 100°C). It also demonstrates excellent printability, enabling fabrication of complex structures with feature sizes below 100 µm. Benefiting from dynamic bond dissociation and reconstruction, the material shows improved intrinsic impact resistance with an energy dissipation ratio of 25%. Furthermore, integrating a lattice architecture yields a material–structure synergistic system, which significantly enhances energy absorption (from 58.0 ± 5.3% to 82.1 ± 9.3%) and reduces peak impact force (from 58.5 ± 6.3 N to 5.8 ± 0.7 N) in helmet protection. This work provides a versatile strategy for designing advanced impact‐resistant polymer systems.
n1471fee92832: Lithium/sodium metal batteries (LSMBs) are promising candidates for next‐generation high‐energy‐density storage, yet their practical deployment remains constrained by dendrite formation, unstable electrode‐electrolyte interfaces, and safety risks. Functional separator coatings offer an attractive strategy for stabilizing metal anodes because they are compatible with existing battery manufacturing and can be readily integrated into cell designs. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the evolution from conventional polyolefin‐based separators to advanced functional architectures. The physicochemical mechanisms through which functional coatings regulate ion transport, homogenize metal deposition, suppress dendrite growth, and improve thermal stability are critically reviewed. Representative coating materials, including ceramics, polymers, carbonaceous materials, metal‐organic frameworks, and hybrid systems, are discussed in terms of their structure‐function relationships, advantages, and limitations. The scalability of different coating strategies is evaluated in terms of coating thickness, line speed/throughput, material utilization, equipment requirements, and process continuity, thereby facilitating the selection of appropriate fabrication routes for distinct application scenarios. Finally, key challenges and future directions are outlined to guide rational separator design and practical manufacturing. This review aims to provide mechanistic insights and design principles for translating functional coated separators toward commercially viable metal batteries.
n4e1460967d77: Commercial thermoelectric (TE) modules are mostly made from bismuth telluride (Bi2Te3) based alloys due to their superior TE performance at low temperatures. However, the TE performance of n‐type Bi2(Te,Se)3 remains inferior compared to its p‐type counterpart, posing a significant bottleneck to further increasing the conversion efficiency of TE devices. In this study, we present an effective strategy to enhance the TE performance of n‐type Bi2(Te,Se)3 by incorporating 2D MoS2 nanoflakes, which effectively modulates grain morphology and phase composition, leading to a remarkable enhancement in electrical conductivity. As a result, a maximum peak figure of merit (zT) value of 1.3 at 450 K is achieved, with a high average zT exceeding 1.2 between 300 and 500 K. This work provides a promising pathway for developing high‐performance n‐type Bi2(Te,Se)3‐based thermoelectric materials that are indispensable for manufacturing high‐efficiency TE devices.
nd03be3d9c748: Converting CO2 into useful chemicals is a cornerstone of sustainable chemistry; among viable routes, the reverse water-gas shift (RWGS) reaction supplies CO for subsequent fuel and olefin synthesis, yet achieving simultaneously high CO selectivity, fast CO2 activation, and stability with non-noble metals remains elusive. Here, we employ a pure H2 torrent to rapidly reduce a Co-salophen framework, forging a core-shell Co@CoOx-C catalyst consisting of a highly crystalline metallic Co core and a defect-rich CoOx shell capable of dynamic reconstruction under redox conditions. The metallic Co core dissociates H2, driving hydrogen spillover to the metal-oxide interface, where CO2 is efficiently activated, resulting in selective CO formation at the highly active Co/CoOx boundary. Rapid CO desorption from coordinatively saturated CoOx sites suppresses further hydrogenation, affording >99% CO selectivity and a CO formation rate of 254.0 mmol gcat −1 h−1 at 500°C maintained for >100 h. These findings demonstrate that engineering dynamic Co/CoOx interfaces via H2 torrent reduction overcomes the intrinsic selectivity limitations of cobalt-based RWGS catalysts and highlight defect-rich core-shell structures derived from H2-reduced metal-salophen precursors as a versatile platform for next-generation CO2 conversion technologies.
n93d99c9592a3: The practical application of lithium metal batteries is severely restricted by dendritic lithium growth and the continuous evolution of unstable solid electrolyte interphases, both of which originate from sluggish Li+ desolvation kinetics. Herein, a host‐guest recognition‐enabled covalent organic framework is developed to regulate interfacial ion migration. By nanoconfined copolymerization of ionic‐liquid monomers within the channels, multi‐cation molecular chains (MCMC) are integrated into the framework to construct a DVA‐COF‐MCMC interphase with selective Li+ transport capability. The cationic recognition sites selectively immobilize bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide anions through strong host‐guest interactions, disrupting Li+‐anion coordination and establishing Li+‐exclusive transport pathways. Theoretical calculations and in situ characterizations reveal that the recognition‐driven ion regulation redistributes the local charge environment, lowers the Li+ dissociation energy barrier, and promotes the formation of a homogeneous LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase. Consequently, the modified lithium anode delivers a high Li+ transference number (0.81), a wide electrochemical stability window (4.8 V), and stable Li plating/stripping (1200 h). Full cells paired with LiFePO4 and LiNi0.9Co0.05Mn0.05O2 cathodes exhibit outstanding rate capability. This work transforms covalent organic framework interfacial engineering from passive channel confinement to active channel recognition, offering a new paradigm for high‐performance lithium metal batteries (LMBs).
n242931549177: Efficient photocatalysis over polymeric carbon nitride (PCN) for value‐added chemical synthesis is challenged by rapid charge carrier recombination and sluggish surface redox reaction kinetics. Herein, crystalline carbon nitride (CCN) introduced with Co single atoms and cyano groups (Co‐CCN) was successfully synthesized through a molten‐salt method for photocatalytic selective oxidative coupling of benzylamine (BA) into N‐benzylidenebenzylamine (NBBA). In comparison to PCN and CCN, the obtained Co‐CCN exhibits much higher photocatalytic performance, with both BA conversion and NBBA selectivity reaching 99%. Moreover, the NBBA yield, reaching 24.75 mmol g−1 h−1, encouragingly outperforms almost all the reported PCN‐based photocatalysts. Spectral characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the electron‐deficient Co‐N4 sites act as oxidation sites, promoting hole accumulation and facilitating the adsorption and activation of BA, while the strongly electron‐withdrawing cyano (‐C≡N) groups act as efficient electron‐extraction sites, enhancing charge separation and promoting O2 absorption and activation, which synergistically contributes to the excellent photocatalytic activity.
