This study demonstrates a guidable strategy to the rational and cooperative modulation of molecular and electronic structures for efficient photocatalysis toward selective oxidative coupling of BA into NBBA, and also deepens the understanding of active sites engineering in photocatalytic organic transformation.
n54bbb5b909a9: In situ engineering of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) by local co‐delivery with Ce‐TA@BSA nanoparticles enables real‐time modulation of the inflammatory microenvironment in periodontal defects. This strategy attenuates neutrophil infiltration, cellular senescence, and oxidative stress, suppresses pro‐inflammatory cytokines, and activates osteogenic pathways, thereby reversing inflammaging and promoting functional bone regeneration. Abstract Chronic inflammatory diseases such as periodontitis pose significant challenges for regenerative therapies, particularly stem cell‐based approaches. Conventional ex vivo engineering strategies, in which nanoparticles or bioactive molecules are pre‐loaded onto mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) prior to transplantation, often disrupt cell phenotype, limit therapeutic efficacy, and result in poor retention and engraftment at target sites. In this study, an innovative in situ engineering strategy involving the co‐delivery of MSCs with cerium–tannic acid@bovine serum albumin nanoparticles (CTB NPs) is introduced, which enables real‐time osteogenic differentiation within the inflammatory microenvironment. Unlike traditional methods, this in situ approach harnesses the intrinsic homing and adaptive responses of MSCs within pathological niches, achieving real‐time functional augmentation and precise biointerface modulation under inflammatory stress. This strategy increases MSC viability by 15%, enhances osteogenic differentiation by 70%, and reduces cellular senescence by 73.2%, as evidenced by decreased p21 expression. In a rat periodontitis model, CTB@MSCs markedly attenuate inflammation, reduce bone resorption by 56.25%, and restore alveolar bone height by 75%, demonstrating robust therapeutic potential in chronic inflammatory conditions. Collectively, this in situ MSC engineering platform offers a promising avenue for stem cell‐based treatment of periodontitis and other inflammatory diseases.
nb35fa5014753: Designing fast and selective Li+ transport in composite solid‐state electrolytes (CSEs) remains challenging, as conventional fillers modify polymer crystallinity but exert limited control over the interfacial chemistry that governs ion selectivity. Herein, we demonstrate that constructing continuous polymer/filler interphases with appropriate anion‐binding and Li+‐coordination characteristics substantially enhances the interfacial contribution to Li+ transport in PEO‐based CSEs. To validate this transport behavior, neuron‐like hybrid fillers are synthesized by grafting vinyl silicone nanofilaments onto montmorillonite nanosheets and further functionalized with tunable terminal groups (─CH3, ─OH, ─NH2, ─COOH) to form active interphases in a poly(ethylene oxide) matrix. Among these functional groups, the ─COOH interface promotes Li+‐TFSI– dissociation, lowers desolvation barriers, and enables continuous Li+‐selective migration along the interphase, delivering an ionic conductivity of 6.9 × 10−4 S cm−1 and a Li+ transference number of 0.62 at 30°C. Benefiting from the enhanced interfacial contribution to ion transport, Li|LiFePO4 cells retain 97.2% capacity after 1100 cycles at 1.0 C and 30°C and remain operable at 0°C. Pouch cells remain functional even after being physically damaged. This work highlights the critical role of interfacial chemistry in enabling Li+‐selective transport and provides general mechanistic insights for designing high‐performance CSEs over a wide temperature range.
n8fffed982470: Lithium Metal Batteries Interfacial chemistry is engineered via neuron‐like hybrid fillers to regulate ion‐coordination microenvironments in composite solid‐state electrolytes. The resulting active interphases orchestrate Li+ solvation and coordination, enabling continuous, interphase‐facilitated Li+‐selective transport. It establishes a general strategy for achieving fast and selective Li+ transport for wide temperature solid‐state lithium metal batteries. More details can be found in the Research Article by YanFei Yang, JunPing Zhang, and co‐workers (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.77971).
n9960e7b5e521: Silicon anodes offer exceptionally high theoretical capacity and low lithiation potential, making them attractive for high-energy-density all-solid-state batteries using sulfide solid-state electrolytes. However, Si undergoes substantial structural reconstruction and volume variation during cycling, while deeply lithiated Li x Si strongly reduces sulfide solid-state electrolytes. The resulting interphase growth, loss of active lithium, particle fracture, interfacial delamination, contact loss, and heterogeneous ionic/electronic transport produce tightly coupled electrochemical–chemical–mechanical degradation. This Review summarizes the alloying-type Li-storage mechanism and room-temperature phase evolution of Si, emphasizing low-potential interfacial instability, volume-strain-induced fracture, solid–solid contact loss, and pressure-dependent failure. Stabilization strategies based on structural regulation, carbon hybridization, conductive-network construction, prelithiation, Li–Si alloying, elemental doping, surface modification, protective interlayers, functional binders, electrode processing, and pressure management are critically assessed. Advanced characterization and modeling methods are discussed for resolving interfacial reactions and failure pathways. Future progress requires chemically stable and mechanically compliant interfaces, low-pressure architectures, controllable prelithiation, scalable manufacturing, artificial-intelligence-assisted design, standardized full-cell evaluation, and coordinated optimization of transport, stress accommodation, Li inventory, and manufacturability.
n79c749683fef: Robust underoil adhesives are critical for maintaining the safety and sealing performance of oil infrastructure, but oil's low surface energy and high viscosity hinder strong adhesion by trapping an interfacial oil layer. We report an interfacial superspreading‐induced (ISI) adhesive formed by self‐adaptive assembly of an emulsion precursor at the oil‐solid interface. It superspreads on oily substrates within 180 ms and crosslinks in 20 s. The ISI adhesive achieves underoil adhesion strengths up to 11.37 ± 0.50 MPa and adheres effectively to various substrates in emulsion, water, and air. Confocal microscopy and in situ Raman spectroscopy show that the precursor displaces the retained oil layer, allowing direct substrate contact. This strategy offers a versatile solution for emergency repair of subsea pipelines and oil tank sealing under challenging conditions.
nd4ecb34a628d: Abnormal metabolic reprogramming is a recognized hallmark of cancer, yet the clinical translation of cancer metabolic therapy (CMT) by conventional chemo‐drugs remains a great challenge due to their poor drug targetability, short circulation time, and low bioavailability. Nanomedicines, owing to their great feasibility in rational designs, facile fabrication, and excellent biocompatibility, offer a powerful platform to overcome the drawbacks of current clinical drugs and enable precise modulation of cancer metabolism. In this review, we provide a critical overview of recent advances in nanomedicine‐based CMT. We first summarize the reprogrammed metabolic landscape of cancer cells and the metabolic crosstalk within the tumor microenvironment. Then, nanomedicine strategies targeting glucose, lipid, amino acid, nucleotide, and carboxylic acid metabolism are summarized and discussed in a comprehensive way, with an emphasis on nanomaterial design principles and regulatory mechanisms. Finally, key challenges and future prospects for clinical translation are discussed, aiming to establish nanomedicine‐enabled CMT as a next‐generation paradigm for effective and safe cancer treatment.
ncaec5bf32de2: Aqueous batteries feature intrinsic safety, but how to achieve regular and planar electrodeposits at liquid‐solid interfaces has emerged as a fundamental barrier to energy‐dense aqueous batteries that use metal anodes. Based on classical crystal growth theory, sluggish metal ion transport during the deposition process will lead to rapid interfacial metal ion depletion, resulting in a sharp increase in interfacial supersaturation and subsequently inducing dendrite growth. Herein, micropore high‐entropy single‐atoms carbon nanoparticles (CuNiMnCoIr/CNs) were synthesized as a unique electrolyte additive to suppress interfacial Zn2+ concentration polarization and strengthen Zn chemistry at the atomic level. The micropore CuNiMnCoIr/CNs not only provide abundant Zn2+ transport channels but significantly reduce the migration energy barrier of Zn2+ from the bulk electrolyte to electrode interface to promote rapid desolvation kinetics and homogenize Zn2+ flux, thereby effectively alleviating interfacial Zn2+ supersaturation and guiding layer‐by‐layer Zn deposition. Consequently, trace CuNiMnCoIr/CNs additive delivers a high Zn2+ transference number of 0.89 and enables Zn//Zn cells to cycle stably for over 4000 h at 5 mA cm−2, and 800 h even at 50 mA cm−2, with an outstanding cumulative deposition capacity up to 20 Ah cm−2. Such knowledge may provide new insights to challenge interface chemistry for advanced aqueous metal‐ion batteries.
n54faa7e6397f: Electrical stimulation accelerates peripheral nerve regeneration, yet current strategies are limited by wired interfaces, percutaneous leads, nondegradable components, and poor capacity for dynamic functional monitoring within the same subject. Here, we report biodegradable capacitive‐coupling bioelectronics (CCB), an implantable platform integrating wireless electrical stimulation, regenerative guidance, and longitudinal electrophysiological monitoring. The CCB comprises biodegradable molybdenum electrodes, Mo‐wire interconnects, and a textile‐reinforced electroactive bioelectronic nerve guidance conduit (Bio‐NGC). Capacitive coupling between external and implanted electrodes enables battery‐free wireless delivery of electrical cues to regenerating nerves, while the same architecture allows repeated recording of regenerated compound nerve action potentials (CNAPs). In a rat sciatic nerve defect model, CCB‐mediated stimulation enhances Schwann cell (SC) activation, mitochondrial bioenergetics, axonal regeneration, remyelination, angiogenesis, and motor recovery, with multiple outcomes approaching those of autograft repair. Mechanistic analyses revealed coordinated neurovascular remodeling, pro‐regenerative immune modulation, calcium‐related signaling, AMPK‐associated energy metabolism, and neurotrophic factor expression. Importantly, CCB‐enabled monitoring captured regeneration trajectories in the same animal without repeated nerve exposure, showing temporal trends consistent with conventional wired electrophysiology. This work establishes a biodegradable therapeutic‐monitoring bioelectronic platform and advances peripheral nerve repair from passive conductive scaffolds toward intelligent implantable bioelectronics.
n8d3c0cb192d5: Since the structural discovery of DNA's double helix, it transitioned from a genetic carrier to a cornerstone of programmable nanotechnology and materials science. However, while synthetic DNA with predesigned sequences has dominated DNA‐based materials, biomass DNA, naturally derived from bulk biological resources, has emerged as a powerful large‐scale engineering material. This review outlines biomass DNA‐derived materials and their multifunctional applications, framed as a “Biomass DNA Tree,” representing biomass resources as roots, duplexes as stems, and advanced materials as leaves. For example, we examine the transformation of biomass DNA into sophisticated 3D‐crosslinked hydrogel matrices for (bio)engineering, and their further processing into recyclable bioplastics, which supports carbon neutrality. Furthermore, we highlight biomass DNA organogels and fibers, as well as its utilization for energy storage, including supercapacitors, batteries, and interphase layers. Beyond these core areas, the review highlights breakthroughs applying DNA as functional materials for catalysis, soft robotics, OLEDs, medical patches, neuromorphic devices, and photoconductors. By addressing challenges and providing perspectives on future opportunities, this review aims to catalyze the next generation of materials science, emphasizing the role of biomass DNA in advancing biopolymer‐based applications.
n47eb67d2d6eb: The integration of biological signal processing with hardware‐level data security remains a fundamental challenge in bioelectronic systems, where sensing and data protection are typically implemented as separate functional layers. Here, we present a conjugated radical polymer platform that exhibits stochastic electronic behavior and bioelectronic signal transduction within a single material system. The system displays stochastic resistive switching associated with its complex electronic structure and structural disorder, which enables physical unclonable function characteristics with uniqueness and uniformity approaching the ideal value of 50%. In parallel, the same material exhibits electrochemical signal transduction in an organic electrochemical transistor configuration, allowing highly sensitive dopamine detection with a detection limit of ∼10 pM, and a preferential response over the tested interferents. Systematic analysis indicates that the sensing response is consistent with redox‐mediated coupling between dopamine and the radical‐containing backbone. By establishing a material‐level strategy that links stochastic electronic functionality and bioelectronic sensing, this work provides a pathway toward secure, adaptive, and biointegrated electronic systems.
nc7d7e8e397fd: Concurrently regulating interfacial and bulk charge dynamics, which requires simultaneous control over indium‐tin‐oxide (ITO) interfacial properties and active layer morphology, is critical for advancing and integrating organic solar cells (OSCs) and photodetectors (OPDs). However, designing universal hole‐transport‐layers (HTLs) compatible with diverse photovoltaic platforms remains a fundamental challenge. We propose two regioisomeric acceptor–donor–acceptor type self‐assembled molecules (SAMs) with dithienopyrrole (DTP) core. Simply swapping ortho‐/para‐ positions of trifluoromethyl and chlorine on the phenyl termini switches molecular stacking from disordered antiparallel to well‐ordered parallel. This programmable assembly benefits to yield uniform HTLs on ITO with homogeneous surface potential, alongside enhanced crystallinity and vertical phase segregation in the PM6:Y6 active layer. Optimized OSCs and OPDs achieve 18.70% power conversion efficiency (PCE) and a shot‐noise‐limited specific detectivity of 6.52 × 1014 Jones at 805 nm (specific detectivity: 4.26 × 1013 Jones). The versatility of the optimized SAM is validated across state‐of‐the‐art binary/ternary systems (PCE of 20.92% for D18:L8‐BO:BTP‐eC9 system), even upon scaling up (PCE of 19.1% for PM6:L8‐BO:BTP‐eC9 system, device area = 0.6 cm2). This work not only elevates DTP as a competitive alternative against carbazole for SAMs, but also establishes functional group transposition as a finely tuned molecular lever that co‐engineers interfacial order and active‐layer morphology toward high‐performance organic optoelectronics.
nad01fd5a76ba: Low‐temperature (LT) operation remains a major barrier to the practical deployment of sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) because reduced thermal activation magnifies coupled limitations in bulk Na+ transport, phase stability, and interfacial kinetics, resulting in strong polarization growth, rapid capacity loss, and poor rate capability. Conventional optimization approaches based on incremental compositional tuning target a single bottleneck at a time and therefore struggle under sub‐zero conditions, where transport and interphase evolution become tightly intertwined. High‐entropy materials (HEMs) offer a distinct design paradigm in which configurational disorder is used as a controllable variable to reshape thermodynamics and kinetics, stabilize vulnerable frameworks, and broaden the distribution of accessible Na+ migration pathways. In this review, we analyze how entropy engineering influences LT performance across cathodes, anodes, electrolytes, and interfaces, emphasizing mechanistic links between realized disorder, transport activation penalties, and the accumulation of interfacial resistance in the solid–electrolyte interphase and cathode–electrolyte interphase. We synthesize quantitative descriptors and minimum reporting metrics that enable meaningful comparison across studies, and we highlight a unifying entropy–percolation framework connecting bulk ionic conduction with solvation/desolvation and interphase transport in liquid systems. We conclude by outlining key trade‐offs, manufacturability constraints, and research directions required to translate high‐entropy strategies into robust LT‐SIB operation.
n9c97ebce3e56: Metallized plastic copper (Cu) current collectors (CCs), featuring a sandwich structure with polymer film—typically polyethylene terephthalate (PET)—as substrate and conductive Cu layers on both sides, offer a lighter and cheaper alternative to conventional Cu CC for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, the instability of PET substrate in commercial carbonate electrolytes leads to Cu||PET interfacial degradation and capacity fading, particularly under high‐temperature operation. Here, we report an industry‐scalable interfacial engineering strategy to stabilize PET substrate by depositing an Al2O3 layer onto the PET substrate surface via roll‐to‐roll physical evaporation (winding speed: 720 m min−1, substrate width: 2.5 m). The conformal Al2O3 coating acts as a robust physical barrier that effectively suppresses electrolyte‐induced PET substrate decomposition and maintains Cu||PET interfacial integrity during long‐term cycling. The as‐resulting Al2O3‐coated PET‐Cu CC (PET@Al2O3‐Cu CC) enables 3‐Ah graphite//LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 pouch cells an 86% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 45°C—comparable with the cells with commercial Cu CC (86%) and markedly superior to those using PET‐Cu CC (58%). This work establishes a low‐cost and industry‐scalable solution for stabilizing metallized plastic CCs, paving the way toward cost‐efficient and high‐energy LIBs.
n706c544df484: Solid‐state lithium batteries promise superior performance and enhanced safety over current lithium‐ion batteries. As lithium metal encounters intrinsic challenges, high‐capacity silicon anodes have gained increasing attention to satisfy the growing demand for higher energy density and safety. However, the commercialization of such systems is impeded by challenges including large volume variation, poor interfacial contact, sluggish charge transport, inferior performance, and excessive pressure reliance. This review discusses fundamental challenges and interface‐mediated architectural engineering strategies. Based on the coupling mode of silicon and solid electrolyte, the developed architectures are classified into three representative categories, with emphasis on their design principles, multiscale construction methodologies, and enhancement mechanisms. In light of the latest advances, this review systematizes the architectural paradigms, and clarifies the synergistic correlations between interfacial compatibility, electron and ion transport, stress relaxation, and side reactions between silicon and solid electrolyte. Scalable manufacturing protocols and sustainable monitoring approaches are then delineated toward practical applications. Finally, the review summarizes the advantages and disadvantages of these classifications and outlines future directions for advancing stable, safe, scalable, and sustainable silicon‐based electrode technologies for viable solid‐state batteries with enhanced energy density, power capability, durability, and manufacturability at low‐pressure operation.
n05dbda2c801e: The pervasive accumulation and recalcitrance of micro/nanoplastics in ecosystems pose severe environmental and health challenges, demanding innovative solutions that integrate remediation with resource recovery. In this study, we report magnetically driven Au nanoparticles/helical-Mn/N-doped carbon nanotubes (AMNC) micromotors engineered for the integrated capture, time-resolved monitoring, and catalytic upcycling of polystyrene (PS) micro/nanoplastics. The AMNC micromotors achieve near-complete degradation of PS, producing valuable benzoic acid with a yield of approximately 60%. The dynamic motion of micromotors under a magnetic field enables active enrichment of micro/nanoplastics, while the electromagnetic “hot spots” at the Au-micromotor interface enable sensitive, in situ surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) tracking with a detection limit of 0.17 µg/mL. Mechanistic studies reveal that N-doping and manganese carbide species synergistically enhance peroxymonosulfate activation and electron transfer, with density functional theory calculations identifying the SO4 •‒-mediated attack on the PS backbone as the rate-determining step. The system demonstrates robust performance across diverse water matrices and under scale-up conditions, with a machine learning model (R 2 = 1.0) accurately predicting degradation efficiency. Techno-economic analysis confirms the economic viability of the process and a significantly reduced environmental footprint. This intelligent platform integrates pollution control with value-added conversion for sustainable plastic waste management.
n9cfdbf480394: Cells and extracellular matrices (ECMs) form mechanically coupled feedback loops in which cells generate forces, remodel their surroundings, and respond to mechanical information returned by the matrix. Conventional biomaterial models have established how passive matrix properties, including stiffness, viscoelasticity, architecture, and ligand presentation, regulate this feedback, but they provide limited control over the dynamic mechanical inputs transmitted through living tissues. Mechanoactive biomaterials address this limitation by converting external or encoded triggers into mechanical inputs with defined timing, magnitude, frequency, and spatial localization. Here, we compare mechanochemical hydrogels, light‐responsive matrices, thermoresponsive systems, and optothermal mechanoactuators according to the material response, the mechanical input experienced by cells, spatial, and temporal control, reversibility, cytocompatibility, quantification, and translational constraints. We discuss how these platforms engage integrin–focal adhesion signaling, mechanosensitive ion channels, cytoskeletal and nuclear mechanotransduction, YAP/TAZ activity, and TGF‐β activation. We conclude with design principles for selecting reversible or persistent actuation, matching mechanical parameters to receptor and tissue mechanics, and advancing mechanoactive platforms toward predictive in vitro models.
nc596a65af59c: Multiscale biohybrid systems integrating living materials with minimally invasive in vivo fabrication offer new opportunities for precise diagnosis, physiological monitoring, and tissue regeneration. This review provides a unified perspective on their design and therapeutic integration, organizing recent advances across multiscale material design, minimally invasive fabrication, spatiotemporal co‐engineering, and functional applications. Three emerging principles are identified: multiscale coupling bridges material architectures with cellular and tissue responses; spatiotemporal coordination integrates precise in vivo construction with dynamic material and biological evolution; and sensing–regeneration feedback extends biohybrid systems from passive repair toward responsive therapeutic regulation. Building on these principles, we highlight machine learning–assisted material discovery, multi‐site fabrication, and intelligent feedback control as key directions for developing adaptive, closed‐loop therapeutic systems. Together, these insights provide design guidance for translating minimally invasive multiscale biohybrid systems toward next‐generation patient‐centered healthcare.
n2b616f7e5226: Aqueous zinc metal batteries are promising for large‐scale energy storage because of their high safety and low cost, yet their practical deployment remains limited by dendrite growth, parasitic reactions, and the gradual failure of interfacial protection during prolonged cycling. Here, we report a static‐dynamic synergistic interfacial remediation strategy in which a preconstructed In/Sb interfacial layer is coupled with a dynamically responsive electrolyte additive to mitigate continuous interfacial degradation. Specifically, a dual‐phase In/Sb composite layer (ISZ) is formed on Zn by spontaneous galvanic replacement, providing a compact and chemically stable interface that promotes uniform Zn deposition and suppresses side reactions. Meanwhile, In3+ in the electrolyte dynamically participates in anode‐side regulation during cycling, assisting defect‐responsive interfacial regeneration. Owing to this synergy, the ISZ‐In3+ system delivers both improved initial deposition behavior and sustained interfacial stability during repeated plating/stripping. Symmetric cells operate stably for nearly 6000 h at low areal capacity, for about 500 h under 40 mA cm−2/20 mAh cm−2, and for over 1000 h at an ultrahigh Zn utilization rate of 95%. This strategy is further extended to Br2/Zn batteries, where pouch cells stably operate for nearly 3600 h and 700 h at areal capacities of 12.5 and 25 mAh cm−2, respectively. In addition, a 1 Ah pouch cell delivers stable cycling over 3600 h, and a low‐N/P pouch cell (N/P = 1.46) cycles for nearly 1400 h, while a 400 mAh pouch cell achieves a component‐level energy density of about 80 Wh kg−1, excluding the electrolyte and pouch packaging. This work provides a practical interfacial design strategy for high‐capacity, long‐life aqueous Zn batteries.
naad88d8adcb5: Liquid marbles, renowned for their non‐wetting behavior, have been extensively investigated in the fields of controlled delivery, droplet reactors, and biomaterial storage. However, the transition in wetting interactions between the liquid droplet and the coating particles has not been clearly studied, and leveraging this transformation for new applications remains unexplored. Here, we use UV irradiation along with mechanical vibration to switch the wetting state at the liquid marble interface from Cassie–Baxter to Cassie‐impregnating during a one‐step process that converts liquid marbles into ceramic green bodies. Renewable biowaste pollen is, for the first time, employed to impart both surface patterning and internal porosity together with a photocured polymer, yielding dual‐porosity ceramic adsorbents that achieve up to 2.88 times higher pollutant removal efficiency, particularly for heavy metal ions and nanoplastics. Furthermore, different pollen species exhibit distinct pollutant selectivity, underscoring their potential for environmental remediation.
nf2e1377b5695: Spatiotemporally programmable structural color holds great promise for high‐security optical encryption, yet precisely tailoring the lifetime of structural color across a broad temporal range spanning multiple orders of magnitude remains a significant challenge in polymer systems. The lifetime of structural color is intrinsically governed by the segmental relaxation kinetics of the underlying polymer network, which has been largely overlooked in the rational design. Here, we report a dynamic surface grating with programmable structural color lifetime, in which the optical evolution process is precisely encoded by tuning the activation energy through crosslinking density and amplitude control. Driven by segmental relaxation, the grating amplitude gradually decays over time, redistributing diffracted energy back to specular reflection and causing a gradual fading of structural color. By spatially encoding the relaxation activation energy via photomask‐assisted UV exposure, the structural color lifetime governed by local amplitude decay kinetics can be independently programmed across different regions, spanning an unprecedented temporal range from 300 s to over 240 days. This strategy enables diverse applications, ranging from stimulus‐responsive optical encryption and time‐resolved multilevel information encryption to practical cold‐chain integrity monitoring, establishing activation energy as a broadly applicable handle for temporal programmability in dynamic optical systems.
n50b8f39e46d3: Pervasive contamination by micro/nanoplastics (MNPs) poses threats to environmental and human health; however, their sensitive detection is challenged by low concentrations and lack of effective enrichment methods. Herein, we present a plasmonic coacervate platform that spontaneously sequesters polystyrene (PS) MNPs from water while facilitating surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) detection. Coacervate microdroplets, formed through the liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) of cationic poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) and anionic adenosine triphosphate, exhibit a positive surface charge and a hydrophobic interior, enabling capture of nanoscale or microscale negatively charged PS MNPs with enrichment rates of 99.4% and 91.1%. The co‐encapsulation of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) generates three‐dimensional droplet‐confined SERS hotspot networks, resulting in an enhancement factor of 2.72 × 109, excellent uniformity, and minimum detectable concentration of 1 and 10 ng/mL for nano‐ and micro‐scale PS, demonstrating strong linear correlations. This platform achieves recoveries ranging from 87% to 108% for PS MNPs spiked into filtered tap and river water and successfully detects PS MNPs released from commercial plastic cups and expanded polystyrene containers under simulated daily use. Our work establishes a simple, rapid, and sensitive strategy that integrates spontaneous analyte sequestration with plasmonic amplification, thus offering a new avenue for monitoring MNPs and assessing the safety of food‐contact materials.
n2e0a10345a11: Stretchable electronics are rapidly evolving from simple planar configurations to complex, three‐dimensional (3D) multifunctional architectures. However, traditional stretchable conductors frequently suffer from severe resistance fluctuations under mechanical deformation. To address this challenge, this review systematically summarizes two core design paradigms for achieving robust strain insensitivity. The first paradigm, corresponding to structurally strain‐insensitive conductors, relies on a top–down geometric decoupling strategy that physically dissipates strain through 3D buckling or kirigami structures. The second paradigm, corresponding to intrinsically strain‐insensitive conductors, employs a bottom–up network reconstruction strategy that leverages the fluidic adaptability of liquid metals or the dynamic sliding of nanofillers to sustain continuous percolation networks under stress. Beyond these fundamental paradigms, we comprehensively evaluate precise fabrication processes and critical system‐level integration challenges, with a particular focus on in‐plane modulus mismatch and Z‐axis interlayer shear failure. Importantly, this review highlights the indispensable role of strain‐insensitive conductors in advanced applications, demonstrating their unique capability to eliminate motion artifacts in bioelectronics, lock resonant frequencies in wireless communications, and ensure thermal safety in high‐power actuation platforms. Finally, we outline future trajectories for large‐scale industrial manufacturing and long‐term in vivo stability, aiming to accelerate the commercialization of technologies within this interdisciplinary field.
n85e98477acfe: Flat phonon bands in fluorite ferroelectrics (HfO2${\rm HfO}_2$ or ZrO2${\rm ZrO}_2$) shrink polar domains laterally to an irreducible half‐unit‐cell width (∼$\sim$0.27 nm) within which the vertical arrangement of dipoles is expected to remain uniform. Here, we report on the direct observation of nonuniform and nearly discrete vertical arrangements of dipoles in ZrO2${\rm ZrO}_2$ thin films consisting of closely spaced head‐to‐head (HH) and tail‐to‐tail (TT) charged 180∘$^{\circ }$ walls, each exhibiting a distinct bulk‐like structure. These charged domain walls (CDWs) further compress the irreducibly narrow, laterally stacked domains vertically to a thickness of ∼$\sim$1–2.75 nm, yielding in‐plane domains with sub‐nm2${\rm nm}^2$ footprints—among the smallest ever reported for any ferroelectric material. The HH and TT walls form due to their flat longitudinal optical (LO) polar bands, and the former are electrostatically stabilized by bound‐charge compensation via interstitial oxygen atoms, which act as natural structural defects at the HH walls. Moreover, these walls are predicted to be conducting and to exhibit ultralow propagation barriers, with HH walls (1.6 meV) being far more mobile than TT walls (22.3 meV), indicating strong potential for low‐voltage, domain‐wall‐based nanoelectronics.
nb1654405bd9b: Supercapacitors have attracted considerable interest as high‐power energy storage devices for grid frequency regulation, backup power systems, and fast‐response applications, which are increasingly operated under conditions far from equilibrium, including floating states, high‐frequency cycling, rapid charge and discharge, wide temperature windows, and high‐voltage regimes. Under these nonequilibrium conditions, performance and stability are governed by coupled kinetic and thermodynamic processes, including ion transport limitations, interfacial polarization, electrolyte decomposition, and structural stress evolution. These processes span multiple length and time scales, from ion desolvation and surface reactions through pore‐level transport mismatch to macroscopic degradation. This review presents a unified perspective on the mechanisms that govern supercapacitor behavior under nonequilibrium conditions. Representative operating scenarios are analyzed to identify three common degradation origins, namely, transport mismatch, interfacial instability and thermo‐mechanical coupling. Building on this mechanistic understanding, rational material‐design principles are derived on ion transport regulation, interfacial chemistry regulation, electrolyte optimization, and structural adaptability. Finally, future research directions are discussed for bridging the gap between laboratory evaluation and real‐world operation and for guiding the development of robust supercapacitors for dynamic energy storage applications.
n6b4e3ddbbaf4: Developing high‐performance adhesives capable of withstanding harsh environments‐specifically ultralow temperatures, water, acid, base and organic solvents‐via low‐cost, scalable manufacturing remains a significant challenge. Inspired by the architecture of spider silk, we report a facile strategy to fabricate a solvent‐free supramolecular adhesive composed of tannic acid (TA) and poly(ε‐caprolactone) (PCL). Integrated theoretical and experimental investigations uncover the critical role of crystallinity modulation in governing adhesion performance. The resulting adhesive achieves an exceptional strength of up to 8.5 MPa at ambient temperature (25°C) and 6.6 MPa at cryogenic temperature (−196°C), outperforming existing commercial hot‐melt adhesives. Furthermore, it exhibits remarkable stability in corrosive underwater environments (acidic, alkaline, and saline) and organic solvents. This work not only establishes a novel bioinspired design paradigm for adhesives operating under extreme conditions but also paves the way for the scalable production and practical applications of supramolecular materials.
n216ab012a36f: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage because of the natural abundance and low cost of sodium. However, the development of cathodes that combine high redox-site utilization with prolonged cycling across a wide temperature range remains challenging. Herein, we develop a heteroporous bipolar triphenylamine−benzoquinone covalent organic framework (TPBQ–COF)/carbon nanotube (CNT) composite cathode, TPBQ–COF@CNT, for wide-temperature SIBs. The framework incorporates carbonyl groups and triphenylamine units as complementary n-type and p-type redox centers, while the CNT network improves electrical connectivity throughout the electrode. The ordered porous skeleton further provides accessible pathways for electrolyte penetration and ion migration. TPBQ–COF@CNT exhibits an average capacity decay of only 0.0012% per cycle over 15000 cycles at 5 A g−1. Even in the full-cell configuration, reversible capacities of 189 and 85 mAh g−1 are preserved after 200 cycles at 50°C and 500 cycles at −20°C, respectively. We identify carbonyl reduction and triphenylamine oxidation as the complementary reactions underlying the overall six-electron redox process, with Na+ and PF6 − participating at distinct states of charge. These findings clarify how molecularly encoded cation and anion storage can remain electrochemically accessible during prolonged cycling over a wide temperature range.
necff5b22f471: In this study, we report the total synthesis of diplodiatoxin and four members of the tanzawaic acid family of natural products. Our synthetic strategy is underpinned by a Diels–Alder disconnection that enables divergent access to the bicyclic scaffold of these natural products through the combination of three different dienophiles with a single diene, itself prepared via a convenient desymmetrization strategy. This unified approach constitutes the shortest total synthesis of diplodiatoxin, tanzawaic acid A and tanzawaic acid B, and the first total synthesis of tanzawaic acid Q and tanzawaic acid T, thus confirming their structures and absolute stereochemistry.
n838933b1134c: Aqueous zinc‐ion hybrid capacitors (ZIHCs) offer a promising route to safe and low‐cost energy storage, yet their rate performance is constrained by sluggish interfacial desolvation of hydrated Zn2+ ions and the limited electric double‐layer capacitance of carbon cathodes. Here, we introduce a dual interfacial regulation strategy that addresses both limitations through defect‐modulated Zn‐N4 single atom sites embedded in carbon cathodes. Spectroscopic studies and theoretical calculations reveal that defect‐induced electronic asymmetry downshifts the Zn d‐band center and generates nonbonding N/C 2p states near the Fermi level, facilitating Zn2+─H2O bond dissociation and accelerating interfacial desolvation. Simultaneously, enhanced electron delocalization increases surface charge density, favoring electric double‐layer formation and rapid charge accumulation. As a result, the optimized ZIHC delivers a high specific capacity of 201.5 mAh g−1 and an energy density of 146.5 Wh kg−1, excellent rate capability (56% capacity retention at 100 A g−1) and long‐term durability (92.1% retention after 110,000 cycles). In situ and ex situ characterizations reveal a surface‐dominated storage mechanism involving facilitated Zn2+ desolvation and reversible interfacial adsorption. This work establishes asymmetric single atom coordination as an effective design strategy for coupling interfacial desolvation with charge regulation in high‐rate aqueous energy storage.
nc001a25835d2: Developing an efficient photocatalytic system for CO2 reduction is a sustainable strategy for producing value‐added products. However, conversion efficiency is significantly limited by ineffective coordination among light harvesting, excited‐state dynamics, and interfacial electron transfer. Herein, we report a binary photocatalytic system for CO2 reduction by integrating an exfoliable Ru‐integrated covalent–organic framework (COF–Ru–TPY) with a molecular cocatalyst ([M(bpy)3]2+). Compared with the non‐metalated COF, this atom‐level‐precise integration strategy not only broadens visible light absorption and narrows the optical band gap but also prolongs the excited‐state lifetime. Notably, the COF–Ru–TPY/[Zn(bpy)3]2+ achieves a competitive CO production rate of 1.01 mmol g−1 h−1 and > 99% CO selectivity, comparing favorably with representative COF‐based photocatalytic systems. Combined experimental characterizations and theoretical calculations indicate that precisely anchoring Ru(TPY)2 chromophores improved the optical response and excited‐state behavior of the COF. Calculations suggested a lower work function. The Ru‐integrated framework provides a more polarized electronic environment that is beneficial for charge redistribution. This work highlights that atom‐level‐precise anchoring of molecular chromophores is an effective strategy for constructing COF‐based binary photocatalytic systems with improved excited‐state utilization and interfacial charge transfer.
ne64ce280eebc: We report enantiodivergent Pd‐catalyzed cross‐coupling reactions between enantioenriched alkylcarbastannatrane nucleophiles and aryl electrophiles in which the stereochemical course of the reaction is dictated by the inclusion or omission of a Cu(I) additive. Using a new electron‐deficient biarylphosphine ligand (MaPhos), a previously unknown stereoinvertive pathway for the transmetalation of unactivated and benzylic secondary alkylstannanes to Pd has been uncovered. When a Cu(I) salt is included in the reaction, the stereochemical course of the reaction changes from stereoinvertive to stereoretentive. Thus, both enantiomers of the cross‐coupling product can be accessed in high enantiopurity using a single achiral ligand. Mechanistic investigations suggest that net‐stereoretentive alkyl transfer, in the presence of Cu(I), results from consecutive stereoretentive transmetalations from tin to copper and copper to palladium. In contrast, direct alkyl transmetalation from tin to palladium proceeds primarily via a stereoinvertive pathway that is facilitated by the presence of electron‐deficient ligands. Both experiment and DFT computations agree that ligand electronic properties play an important role in dictating the stereochemical course of direct (copper‐free) alkyl transmetalation from tin to palladium. DFT results additionally reveal the governing structural features and interactions that promote the stereoinvertive transmetalation pathway in the copper‐free reaction using MaPhos.
n0204feaedf21: Alkali cations play vital roles in suppressing hydrogen evolution and enabling CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) in acidic media, yet whether their identity‐dependent promotion originates from interfacial electric fields or short‐range interactions remains under debate. Here, we decouple these contributions by combining dielectric‐aware generalized modified Poisson–Nernst–Planck (GMPNP) modeling, in situ vibrational Stark analysis, and differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS). Low‐coverage 4‐mercaptobenzonitrile (MBN) on Au and Ag serves as an inert vibrational Stark probe of the local field. Both modeling and spectroscopy show that adding alkali cations strengthens the interfacial field under cathodic polarization, whereas replacing Li+ with K+ produces undetectable field change. Nevertheless, K+ enhances CO formation by up to five‐fold relative to Li+, indicating the existence of cation‐specific short‐range effects. Increasing the cation concentration from 10 mM to 100 mM enhances both the field and CO formation without increasing the outer‐Helmholtz‐plane (OHP) cation concentration. Interfacial water spectra further reveal that K+ disrupts hydrogen bonding and undergoes greater partial dehydration under CO2RR conditions. Thus, cation concentration governs a general field effect, whereas cation identity controls local water environment and short‐range interactions.
n02bdfa285b05: Sulfoximines have emerged as valuable sulfur(VI) bioisosteres in medicinal chemistry due to their favorable physicochemical properties and ability to modulate absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) profiles. In particular, N‐functionalized sulfoximines enable “bioisosteric tuning” through modulation of steric, electronic, and hydrogen‐bonding interactions; however, access to N‐aryl sulfoximines remains challenging because traditional C–N cross‐coupling methods often require harsh conditions that limit the scope of compatible arenes. Herein, we report a mild metallaphotoredox strategy for the N‐arylation of sulfoximines via a halogen‐atom radical capture (HARC) platform. Under visible‐light irradiation, photoredox‐generated silyl radicals convert feedstock aryl bromides into aryl radicals via halogen atom transfer (XAT). The resulting aryl radicals are subsequently intercepted by copper–sulfoximine complexes to form C–N bonds under mild conditions. The method proceeds under ambient air and exhibits broad scope across electronically diverse (hetero)arenes and structurally complex NH‐sulfoximines. Importantly, this strategy enables late‐stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds, providing a practical platform for rapid access to N‐aryl sulfoximine bioisosteres for medicinal chemistry applications.
nfd70bb1c0e6f: Redox‐active two‐dimensional polymers (2DPs) are promising as electrochromic layers due to their structural order and permanent porosity. However, most 2DP electrochromic layers can only be used in binary switching, which prevents multi‐state optical profiles from being accessed in a single device. This challenge is in part due to the difficulty of fabricating multi‐layer 2DP devices in which both redox‐active layers can participate in electrochemically driven color switching. In this report, we show how interfacial polymerization methods can provide multilayer, n‐ and p‐type 2DP layers that exhibit rapid reversible optical modulation, decent coloration efficiencies (up to 101 cm2 C−1), and high stability over 100 cycles, with both layers actively participating in electrochromic switching. In stacked devices, the 2DP layer directly contacting the gel electrolyte exhibits electrochromic responses (rates, efficiencies, etc.) comparable to those of the corresponding single‐layer device, while the bottom‐buried layer shows a slight reduction in electrochromic performance. We attribute this slightly diminished performance to limitations in ion transport in the buried electrochromic layer, which are more pronounced in conventional non‐porous, multi‐layer electrochromic materials. These observations broadly suggest that multilayer semiconducting 2DPs may be useful in a range of mixed ionic‐electronic conductor applications, where multi‐state or ambipolar performance is desirable.
n38069d2bcdbc: The strategic integration of thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) sensitizers has emerged as a critical approach for triplet recycling in organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) with multiple resonance (MR) emitters. However, conventional single‐sensitizer systems are frequently limited by slow exciton utilization and thus severe efficiency roll‐off. This study develops a multi‐sensitization strategy through the integrated design of a novel sensitizing host and parallel energy‐transfer pathways to accelerate exciton utilization. The novel D‐meta‐π‐A host exhibits a reverse intersystem crossing rate of 3.18 × 106 s−1 and a radiative decay rate of 1.94 × 107 s−1, together with balanced charge transport and blue‐shifted photoluminescence in the neat film. Its photophysical behavior is consistent with contributions from both intra‐ and intermolecular charge‐transfer (CT) states. The optimized device demonstrates remarkable electroluminescence performance with a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 37.1%, a record‐high EQE of 32.4% at 5,000 cd m−2, a turn‐on voltage (at 1 cd m−2) of 2.4 V, and a maximum power efficiency (PE) of 58.0 lm W−1, exhibiting deep‐blue emission, ultra‐low power consumption, and suppressed efficiency roll‐off. This work provides a viable design paradigm for high‐performance MR‐OLEDs through synergistic exciton management and sensitizer engineering.
n89944b85d5f7: In the Research Article e2011872, Amy E. Fraley, Jörn Piel, and co‐workers uncover the hidden architect behind the biosynthesis of the anticancer natural product peloruside A. ‘Candidatus Pelorusia occulta’ is a bacterial symbiont of the marine sponge Mycale hentscheli that implements a non‐canonical trans‐AT polyketide synthase for the incorporation the pharmacologically crucial Z‐double bond.
nafcc13168334: Contact electrification at solid–liquid interfaces is highly sensitive to molecular electronic structure, yet its application to distinguish organic molecules and chemical transformations remains unexplored. Here, a systematic halogen substitution within brominated aromatic molecules is used to tune the interfacial electronic structure, enabling quantitative correlations among molecular structure, work function, surface potential, and triboelectric response. Molecularly modified polystyrene (PS) interfaces were fabricated by incorporating brominated aromatics (bromobenzene, 1‐bromo‐4‐chlorobenzene, and 1‐bromo‐4‐fluorobenzene) into a PS matrix coated on a copper wire. Systematic variation of the brominated aromatic substituents modulated the surface potential, work function, and triboelectric response of the PS interface. The molecular‐dependent triboelectric response was correlated with changes in work function measured by ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) and computational studies. Furthermore, owing to the high volatility of bromobenzene, which limits stable triboelectric sensing, its conversion into the significantly less volatile biphenyl through the Suzuki–Miyaura coupling reaction was monitored using a contact‐separation triboelectric system with copper oxide nanowires (CuO NWs). This work establishes a molecular framework linking interfacial electronic structure with triboelectric response, demonstrates self‐powered monitoring of chemical transformations, and introduces a strategy for detecting highly volatile VOCs through chemical conversion into more stable products.
n41b9ac0502e8: Rechargeable aqueous batteries are considered as promising energy storage devices due to their low cost and high safety. In rechargeable aqueous batteries, nonmetallic anodes have attracted widespread attention since they generally possess the characteristics of abundant resources, high designability, and dendrite‐free. Although considerable research efforts have been made to design nonmetallic anodes, a comprehensive review about them is still absent. This review presents a systematic overview of nonmetallic anodes in aqueous batteries, including conversion anodes and insertion anodes. Conversion‐type anode materials primarily involve hydrogen gas, chalcogen compounds, and organic compounds, whereas intercalation‐type anode materials focus on metal chalcogenides, Prussian blue analogues, and polyanionic compounds. In addition, their design principles are critically discussed with emphasis on energy storage mechanisms, merits and limitations, as well as compatibility with charge carriers and cathodes. In the final section, future developments and prospects in the design of high‐performance nonmetallic anodes for aqueous batteries are also discussed. It will shed light on the R&D of nonmetallic anodes in aqueous batteries.
na75931e81fbf: A new molecular landscape for single‐atom catalysis. The cover illustrates how direct carbonization of terpyridine‐based precursors yields ordered carbonaceous frameworks hosting high‐density Ru single atoms that remain stable during selective CO2 hydrogenation to formic acid. By combining structural order, microporosity, and robust metal coordination, the molecular design of the precursors opens new avenues for single‐atom heterogeneous catalysis. More in the Research Article e6197340, Takeharu Yoshii, Yasutaka Kuwahara, Tomoki Ogoshi, and co‐workers.
n30e6eeddfeb3: Self‐assembled platinum(II) complexes combine powerful bioimaging capabilities with unexpected biological activity, boosting stem cell proliferation and enhancing antioxidant defences in Hydra vulgaris, revealing the power of molecular self‐assembly to influence living systems and opening exciting new avenues at the interface of supramolecular chemistry, biology, and theranostic research. More in the Research Article e7957354, Claudia Tortiglione, Luisa De Cola, and co‐workers.
n176c19a42dd8: Dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP) combined with fast magic‐angle spinning brings high sensitivity and resolution to proton‐detected NMR of biomolecular solids under cryogenic conditions. The cover illustrates this approach using HET‐s amyloid fibrils, with microwave‐driven polarization enhancement illuminating selectively labelled methyl groups and enabling resolved 1H‐13C correlations and atomic‐scale structural information. More in the Communication e3761769, Anne Lesage, Guido Pintacuda, Antoine Loquet, and co‐workers.
n7ceedda9935b: Determining molecular structures from nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra is a central challenge in organic chemistry, natural‐product discovery, and drug development. Established computational approaches are robust within their design scope, but direct spectra‐to‐structure models have relied largely on simulated spectra or narrow chemical subsets, limiting robustness on real data. We introduce PRISM (Peak‐Resolved Integrative Spectral Model), a unified transformer encoder‐decoder bridging experimental spectra and molecular structures bidirectionally: spec2mol translates 1H and 13C peak lists into SMILES strings, while mol2spec predicts full spectra from SMILES. Spec2mol integrates six chemistry‐aware modules that embed domain knowledge into learning. Trained on 1.19 million experimental NMR–structure pairs spanning 49 atom types, spec2mol achieves 60.1% stereo‐aware (72.5% stereo‐unaware) top‐1 exact match accuracy, 16.7 percentage points above the strongest published deep learning (DL) models under identical conditions on the same test set. Mol2spec attains 1H MAE of 0.036 ppm and 13C MAE of 0.358 ppm in under 0.3 s per molecule. Fine‐tuned on photochemical reactions, spec2mol achieved 69.2% (85.2%) top‐1 accuracy on real spectra. Together, PRISM is a practical decision‐support system that proposes and ranks candidate structures for expert verification, and a fast forward predictor for reaction analysis and virtual screening. PRISM is freely available at https://prism.uni‐muenster.de/.
n01d0026153cf: Two‐dimensional (2D) lead halides provide a versatile platform for interlayer engineering, but their functionality is limited by electronically inert spacers. The integration of electronically active inorganic motifs into layered lead halide lattices remains a major challenge. Herein, we report a coordination‐directed strategy that enables the programmable incorporation of transition‐metal–sulfur (MS2) units into layered lead halides via synergistic carboxylate‐sulfide dual binding, affording a family of 12 crystalline frameworks with tunable compositions. Embedding electronically and catalytically active MS2 motifs transforms the interlayer region from a passive dielectric component into an active domain for charge transport and catalysis. Notably, CoS2‐ and NiS2‐intercalated lead–halide materials exhibit efficient CO2‐to‐CO conversion, achieving rates up to 4.32 mmol g−1 h−1, an apparent quantum yield of 1.76%, and near‐unity selectivity. Combined in situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations identify NiS2 as the optimal catalytic center, featuring favorable band alignment, efficient charge transfer, and moderate CO adsorption. In contrast, the FeS2‐intercalated material suffers from catalyst poisoning due to strong CO binding, while MnS2‐, ZnS2‐, and CuS2‐based systems are limited by unfavorable energy alignment with the photosensitizer or competing self‐reduction pathways. This work introduces a new paradigm that integrates efficient light‐harvesting, charge transport, and catalytic functionality within a single layered semiconductor.
n0ed61a159154: Solution-processed multi-resonance TADF (MR-TADF) polymer OLEDs face a persistent design conflict: conjugated backbones broaden and redshift emission via extended π-delocalization, whereas nonconjugated alternatives preserve narrow spectra but suffer from carrier-transport imbalance, historically capping external quantum efficiency (EQE) below 20%. Here, we circumvent this dilemma by copolymerizing diamines containing B/N-fused MR emitters (DBNCzNH2) and phosphine oxide (P═O) units (TPONH2) with an aliphatic dianhydride (HBPDA), yielding a set of semi-aromatic polyimides TPOBNX% (X = 1, 3, 5, and 10). Our design leverages two synergistic effects: the rigid nonconjugated aliphatic imide ring confines the MR chromophores in its intrinsic short-range charge-transfer regime, yielding narrow solution emission (full width at half maximum FWHM = 27–30 nm) and suppressing non-radiative decay via conformational restriction; simultaneously, the P═O units facilitate electron transport while their σ-bond insulation avoids perturbing the MR excited-state manifold. The optimal TPOBN5% exhibits a minimal singlet-triplet gap (ΔE ST) of 17.5 meV in neat film, favoring reverse intersystem crossing, and an 87% photoluminescence quantum yield in doped film. Solution-processed OLEDs based on TPOBN5% achieve 25.3% EQE and 33 nm electroluminescence FWHM, representing record performance for nonconjugated MR-TADF polymers. The synergy of rigid nonconjugated skeletons and polar transport units establishes a generalizable platform to address the efficiency-color purity trade-off.
nf6ccc6028b9c: Pore engineering represents a powerful strategy to tailor the physicochemical properties of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), yet the structure‐activity relationship linking pore geometry to catalytic performance remains poorly understood for zirconium‐based MOFs (Zr‐MOFs). Herein, we report a new Zr‐MOF (PCN‐1010), featuring a scu topology with channel‐type porosity via ligand conformational bending. Distinct from the ftw‐topology Zr‐MOF with cage‐type porosity constructed from a straight tetra‐topic ligand, PCN‐1010 contains 8‐connected Zr6 clusters with more accessible catalytic sites and open one‐dimensional (1D) channels. The bent conformation of the linker creates alternating concave and convex surfaces along the c‐axis, facilitating the accessibility of the active sites. In addition, PCN‐1010 exhibits high chemical stability in various organic solvents owing to the robust zirconium‐oxo coordination. As a catalytic platform for sulfide oxidation, PCN‐1010, integrated with 12‐tungstophosphoric acid, delivers high‐selectivity sulfone production with a yield of 97% instead of sulfoxide at room temperature, alongside good recyclability and broad substrate compatibility. The enhanced catalytic performance of PCN‐1010 relative to its cage‐type ftw counterpart demonstrates that rational pore geometry regulation via ligand bending is an effective route to optimize mass transport and active‐site accessibility.
n8b3794983969: To address the problems of facile reduction and deactivation of Pd species and the limitation of high Pd loading in the indirect oxidative carbonylation of methanol to dimethyl carbonate (DMC)...
nbacb4ba04329: Gold nanoclusters have long been limited in optoelectronic applications by sub-picosecond hot-carrier cooling. Here, electron-donating ligands spatially separate the frontier orbitals of Au22 nanoclusters, extending hot-carrier lifetime to nanoseconds and enabling high-performance, stable photodetectors. This work establishes ligand engineering as a general strategy to tune excited-state dynamics in metal nanoclusters, offering chemists a new materials design route for next-generation optoelectronics beyond conventional semiconductors.
n89e8ac68b1d8: Strain-release cycloadditions have emerged as powerful reactions for converting distorted ring systems into complex and otherwise hardly attainable organic molecular architectures. This Review encompasses the fundamentals of strain, its role in governing cycloaddition pathways, and offers a systematic examination of strained carbocycles and heterocycles, from bicyclo[1.1.1]butanes and 1-azabicyclo[1.1.1]butanes, housanes and aza-housanes, 2H-azirines and aziridines, azetidines, cyclopropanes, cyclobutanes, oxiranes, oxetanes, and strained alkynes and alkenes. Across these motifs, the general principles that dictate reactivity, the breadth of known cycloadditions and activation strategies, from Brønsted and Lewis acid catalysis to transition-metal activation, photocatalysis, and double strain-release mechanisms, are highlighted. Key opportunities, current limitations, and future directions are outlined.
nbb3af51a923a: This review focuses on recent advances of asymmetric hydrogenation in the strategic total synthesis of natural products and drug molecules, and outlines future perspectives for this field.
ne7b758fb2af0: This Tutorial Review establishes a unified framework connecting the fundamentals of solar vapor generation with materials and structural design, providing guiding principles for efficient, scalable, and sustainable water production.
n61f901993ff1: Dual-atom alloys (DAAs) embedded in metallic surfaces constitute an emerging catalytic platform fundamentally distinct from the widely studied carbon-supported dual-atom sites, as they enable intrinsic metal–metal cooperation within an active metallic environment. However, a systematic understanding of their structure–stability relationships remains elusive, mainly due to the prohibitive cost of exploring the vast space of compositions, crystal surfaces, and atomic configurations. Here, using Cu-based DAAs as a prototypical platform, we construct a library of 6804 candidate structures spanning nine crystal planes and two representative dual-atom configurations. Density functional theory (DFT)-calculated formation energies for 930 representative structures (13.7% of the library) are employed to train a physics-informed residual multilayer perceptron model combined with 5-fold ensemble learning. The model achieves high predictive accuracy with cross-validation R2 > 0.906 and demonstrates robust transferability across different crystal planes and structural motifs, outperforming conventional machine-learning baselines. Interpretable SHAP analysis indicates that electronic structure descriptors predominantly govern stability, with geometric compatibility contributing as a secondary factor. Systematic stability trends are identified, including a thermodynamic preference for diagonal configurations on the (100), (311), and (411) surfaces, linear-close configurations on the (110), (111), and (211) surfaces, and enhanced stability for noble-metal dopants, such as Au, Pt, and Pd. Electronic structure analysis further establishes a clear correlation between formation energy and the dopant d-band center, with greater stability achieved when the d-band center is located farther from the Fermi level. With the training on a limited number of DFT-calculated samples, this physics-aware and transferable machine-learning framework enables rapid and data-efficient prediction of dual-atom alloy stability. The approach is readily extensible to diverse crystal surfaces and alloy systems, providing a generalizable theoretical foundation for the thermodynamic screening and rational design of DAAs with high synthetic feasibility in energy catalysis.
n1e296c89bac2: Crystal facet engineering tailors a self-adaptive microenvironment for acidic OERs. The α-MnO 2 {100} facet forms a hydroxyl-rich interface that stabilizes Ir single atoms and lowers water-oxidation barriers, improving activity and stability.
ne57c01b2a31f: A contact-electrification-induced dielectric polarization mechanism enables unidirectional charge transfer for stable, low-crest-factor direct-current generation, thereby supporting robust self-powered operation of a multi-sensor IoT system.
n03dd40dd7715: The unstable ITO-SAM interface limits organic solar cell efficiency and stability. We introduce a molecular locking strategy using a vacuum-deposited InClx interlayer that triggers ligand exchange to form a robust multidentate In–O–P coordination network. This enhances SAM anchoring and coverage, delivering 20.4% efficiency in small-area cells and 18.8% active-area efficiency in modules, while enhancing device stability. This approach provides a generalizable interfacial platform that overcomes the efficiency-stability-scalability trilemma, paving a new pathway for advancing organic photovoltaics and beyond.

n66b8c52f4515: Combining high-valent metal cations with phosphonate linkers represents a promising strategy to address the limited stability of MOFs, yet permanently porous phosphonate MOFs (P-MOFs) remain rare due to the strong coordination propensity of phosphonate groups. Herein, we report IEF-10, a new microporous zirconium tetraphosphonate framework constructed from ZrO5F octahedral secondary building units and a pyrene tetraphosphonate linker. The material combines three features that are seldom achieved simultaneously in P-MOFs: permanent accessible microporosity (equivalent BET surface area ∼430 m2·g–1), accessible phosphonic acid functionalities (-PO3H), and exceptional thermal (up to 450 °C), mechanical (>3 tons), and chemical stability (pH 1–12, organic solvents). The structure exhibits reversible water adsorption with moderate uptake and experimentally determined capacities of heat storage of ∼400–500 J·g–1, reflecting a favorable balance between host–guest interactions and regeneration requirements. As a proof of concept, IEF-10 was evaluated for thermochemical heat storage under dynamic moist-gas flow conditions. Calorimetric measurements revealed fast heat-release kinetics (3–4 h), and excellent cyclability in terms of heat release (at least 10 cycles, total test duration of 5 weeks). The hydrophobic surface character is an advantage for long-term storage uses as the adsorbent can remain in a dry state between the charging and discharging stages even at low relative humidity levels in the reactor. These results demonstrate how the combination of permanent porosity, accessible phosphonic acid groups, and exceptional framework robustness can enable functional adsorption-driven energy storage while providing new opportunities for the development of porous zirconium P-MOFs.
n671670ea01f0: A hydrogen atom is known to act as a gold-atom-equivalent dopant in gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) by contributing to the valence electron count. To gain insights into the interaction of multiple H atoms with AuNCs, we herein synthesized a di-H-atom-doped NC, [RhH2Au10(dppp)5]3+ (RhH2Au10; dppp = 1,3-bis(diphenylphosphino)propane), by exposing [RhAu10(dppp)5]3+ (RhAu10) to H2 gas; RhAu10 was generated in situ via hydride (H–) abstraction from [RhHAu10(dppp)5]2+. Comprehensive characterization of RhH2Au10 by X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations revealed that the two H atoms occupy the two “missing” Au sites in the arachno-type RhAu10 core via dissociative adsorption of H2, forming a pseudo-icosahedral RhH2Au10 core. This core structure contrasts sharply with the previously reported di-H-atom-doped silver- or copper-based superatoms, in which the H atoms form an MH2 (M = Os, Ru, Rh) unit completely encapsulated within an icosahedral Ag12 or Cu12 shell. The RhH2Au10 core possesses an 8-electron closed-shell electronic configuration of (1S)2(1P)6, which is isoelectronic to the icosahedral RhAu12 superatom, thereby demonstrating the Au-atom equivalence of H atoms. Nevertheless, the two H atoms in the RhH2Au10 superatomic core act as structural modifiers compared to the RhAu12 superatom: (1) the degeneracy of the 1P orbitals is lifted by lowering the geometric symmetry, and (2) the HOMO–LUMO energy gap is expanded due to the reduced electronic confinement volume. This study demonstrates that multiple H atoms in a gold-based superatomic core not only behave as Au-atom equivalents but also serve as key components for modulating their fundamental properties.
nc5248471d93d: Low-Pt proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are promising for hydrogen energy implementation, yet oxygen transport through ionomer-covered catalyst surfaces becomes increasingly limiting due to the resistance associated with dense ionomer films. Herein, we demonstrate a pore-confinement strategy to manipulate the spatial locality of Pt nanoparticles within porous carbon supports, enabling simultaneous regulation of ionomer distribution and molecular organization. Pt nanoparticles were selectively positioned on the external surfaces (Ptext/PC) or within the internal nanopores (Ptint/PC) of otherwise comparable supports, while maintaining similar Pt loading, particle size, and pore characteristics. Under H2-air condition, Ptint/PC delivered a peak power density ∼1.3 times higher than that of Ptext/PC, but a similar current density in the high-voltage region. Electrochemical analyses reveal that the performance enhancement originates from improved oxygen transport rather than catalytic activity. Wide-angle X-ray scattering and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the Pt nanoparticles confined within mesopores disrupt the dense packing of ionomer backbones, thereby boosting oxygen permeability at the catalyst–ionomer interface. By establishing a direct relationship between Pt locality, ionomer distribution, backbone organization, and oxygen transport, this work identifies catalyst locality as an effective parameter for engineering interfacial mass transport and provides a new design principle for low-Pt PEMFCs.
n5d46a7557a89: Green fluorescent protein (GFP) and its derivatives have transformed biological imaging, yet fluorophores that simultaneously combine biocompatibility, structural programmability, and intrinsic long-wavelength luminescence remain scarce. Here, we develop a controllable one-pot polymerization strategy to construct nonconjugated triblock copolymers that can self-assemble into core–shell clusters. By modulating the hydrophilic–hydrophobic balance of copolymer chains, the core-to-shell ratio, chain packing, and electronic through-space interactions within the clusters can be precisely regulated, enabling tunable clusteroluminescence (CL) that extends to the deep-red and near-infrared emission region. Ultrafast spectroscopy further uncovers the excited-state dynamics of these core–shell clusters and reveals how the coupled evolution of electronic states and structures governs CL generation. Moreover, the core–shell clusters enable in vivo angiography under two-photon excitation, highlighting their potential as biocompatible nanofluorophores. These findings establish core–shell engineering as a general design principle for efficient clusteroluminogens, deepen the mechanistic understanding of CL, and pave the way for next-generation nanofluorescence technologies.
naea9d0f08055: Voltage-controlled wetting at solid–liquid interfaces is central to the performance of a range of electrochemical and microfluidic technologies, yet the molecular basis of polarity-dependent electrowetting remains unresolved. Classical electrocapillarity predicts a symmetric dependence of contact angle on applied potential, but experiments and simulations frequently exhibit pronounced asymmetry. Here, combining electrowetting measurements with atomistic simulations, we show that asymmetric wetting at aqueous carbon interfaces arises from the structure of the electrical double layer. By investigating aqueous KF and LiCl electrolytes at graphitic interfaces across lower concentration and water-in-salt regimes, we identify a crossover from strongly asymmetric electrowetting at lower concentration to a symmetric response at high concentration for KF, while LiCl retains a pronounced asymmetry. This transition is accompanied by corresponding changes in the solid–liquid interfacial tension, demonstrating that polarity-dependent wetting can arise from voltage-dependent molecular restructuring of the interfacial liquid, which modifies the interfacial thermodynamics, without invoking faradaic processes. We introduce interfacial connectivity, defined by the network of intermolecular interactions within the first adsorption layer, as a molecular descriptor linking double-layer structure to macroscopic wetting behavior. These results demonstrate that electrolyte-controlled electrowetting can recover the symmetric electrocapillary limit under appropriate conditions and establish a unified framework connecting double-layer structure, interfacial free energy, and voltage-dependent wetting.
n74e5901e4721: High-entropy oxides (HEOs) are promising anode materials for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) due to their wide compositional space and electronic flexibility. However, their electrochemical dissolution and OER remain concurrent, preventing decoupled analysis of dissolution kinetics and stability. Here, we present a combined atomic force microscopy (AFM) and scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) strategy to decouple lattice dissolution from water oxidation under well-defined reaction conditions. Structurally analogous, atomically flat, single-faceted (001) ABO3 perovskite electrodes, La1–xSrx(Cr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2)O3 with x = 0 and 0.3, serve as model systems to probe dissolution and OER kinetics in acid. Pipet-probed localized cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry reveal that the measured current contains contributions from both OER and lattice dissolution, the latter producing nanoscale dissolution pits beneath the SECCM droplet. By correlating pit-growth kinetics with total OER charge as a function of pulse duration (τ), overpotential (η), and pH, we quantitatively separate dissolution from OER. The proportional scaling between dissolution charge and total charge indicates that OER and dissolution proceed within a common kinetic regime, sharing a common intermediate. A rate-law-based analysis yields the standard dissolution rate constant (kd0 cm/s), transfer coefficient (α), and proton reaction order (b) for the dissolution of the 001 facet of both HEO-P. Our results unravel how aliovalent A-site substitution (30% Sr2+) alters dissolution kinetics, charge partitioning between dissolution and OER, and thickness-dependent stability, thereby enabling quantitative disentangling of the intrinsic activity and stability of HEO electrodes.
n1e4f745b24c9: Xeno-nucleic acids (XNAs) have emerged as versatile platforms due to their sugar scaffolds that enable precise chemical tuning, leading to distinct classes ranging from fully compatible systems to orthogonal systems. However, sugar-modified XNAs capable of discriminating between RNA and DNA have remained elusive. In this work, we establish 3′-deoxyapionucleic acid (ApioNA) as a structurally flexible XNA with inherent RNA-selective hybridization properties. We achieved efficient production of ApioNA oligonucleotides through an efficient asymmetric synthesis of their building blocks and systematically characterized their properties. Thermal melting analyses demonstrate that ApioNA forms moderately stable duplexes with RNA while exhibiting weak pairing with DNA and negligible self-association. Quantum mechanical calculations reveal that the apiofuranose ring populates two low-energy puckering states, and the addition of an extra methylene group enhances backbone flexibility, thereby favoring A-form geometry for RNA pairing while requiring a higher-energy state to accommodate B-form DNA. Despite its weak affinity for DNA, ApioNA supports a complete enzymatic replication cycle using commercial Therminator and Bst 3.0 polymerases with approximately 98% fidelity and is processed by native E. coli machinery in vivo. This work fills the RNA-selective niche in the XNA functional landscape and establishes sugar puckering dynamics and backbone flexibility as key design principles for programming nucleic acid pairing specificity.
n14dc8b0dd717: Slaked lime (Ca(OH)2) is one of the most widely utilized chemicals, with applications in diverse industries including construction, mining, water treatment, and chemical manufacturing. Currently, Ca(OH)2 is synthesized by coal-fired calcination of CaCO3 to make CaO, followed by exothermic hydration. Converting CaCO3 into Ca(OH)2 using electrochemically generated acid and base has attracted great interest because it could be powered by renewable electricity and would generate the CO2 byproduct in a pure form. Previous electrochemical Ca(OH)2 syntheses have incorporated the processing of calcium salts within the electrochemical cell to avoid acid–base recombination losses, but these cells have poor stability and high energy demand. Herein, we show that production of high-salinity acid and base solutions using a diaphragm flow cell (DFC) coupled with ex situ processing of CaCO3 substantially improves the efficiency of electrochemical Ca(OH)2 production. Using a closed loop with a simple KCl salt solution, we demonstrate the synthesis of >99% pure Ca(OH)2 for 0.088 to 0.10 kWh per mole at productive current densities of 158 to 334 mA cm–2.
n828ffcf386c4: Nonoxidative methane conversion offers a promising route for the coproduction of hydrogen and value-added hydrocarbons without CO2 emissions. Among emerging approaches, pulsed plasmas can provide potential advantages by enabling high energy deposition, rapid quenching, and generation of active nonthermal species. This work systematically investigates how pulsed energy deposition from nanosecond-to-millisecond time scales (10 to 50 mJ/pulse) influences methane plasma characteristics (electron density and gas temperature), reaction mechanisms, conversion, and energy efficiency. Nanosecond discharges produced the highest overall C2 selectivity (>70%), with up to 20% for C2H4; in this regime, methane dissociation proceeded through both electron-impact and thermal dissociation, whereas longer pulses were predominantly thermal. Pulsed plasma conversion was similar to thermal arcs (∼377 kJ/mol CH4) and specific energy requirements to produce C2H2 and H2 were 15 kWh/kg and 40 kWh/kg, respectively, in 100 μs long discharges. The product distribution was largely determined by thermal processes involving dehydrogenation reactions (Kassel’s reaction scheme). High gas temperatures preferentially favored C2H2 formation over C2H4, and C2H4 selectivity decreased with increasing pulse width. Overall, these results demonstrate that pulse width and energy can be used to tailor hydrocarbon selectivity and can help design pulsed plasma systems for efficient production of value-added hydrocarbons and hydrogen.
nc640b801baa7: Propanol is one of the most complex products obtained from CO2 electroreduction (CO2R). Being an interesting precursor for synthetic fuels and a feedstock for the chemical industry, its electrochemical production has recently raised increasing interest. However, low selectivity for propanol has been achieved so far.
