nb0871641e43e: Computational chemistry has become an indispensable tool for generating data and insights, pervading all branches of experimental chemistry. Its most central concept is the potential energy hypersurface, which is key to all chemistry and materials science, as it assigns an energy to a molecular structure, the necessary ingredient for reaction mechanism elucidation and reaction rate calculation. Density functional theory (DFT) has been the most important method in practice for obtaining such energies, which is reflected in the use of high-performance computing hardware. In the last two decades, a new class of surrogate potential energy functions has evolved with remarkable properties: quantum accuracy combined with force-field speed. Until very recently, their application was hampered by the fact that they needed to be trained on truly large system-specific data sets, generated before a computational chemistry study could be started (in sharp contrast to DFT, which, as a first-principles method, works out of the box but at a far higher price of computational cost). Very recently, this roadblock has been overcome by so-called foundation machine learning interatomic potentials, which are poised to completely change the way we do computational chemistry, likely prompting us to abandon DFT as the prime method of choice for this purpose in less than a decade.
n1c2f4efa125d: We report the synthesis and magnetic properties of one-dimensional lanthanidocenate coordination polymers, [Ln(η5-LSn)2K]n (Ln = Tb, Dy; LSn = [1,4-bis(tert-butyl-dimethylsilyl)-2,3-bis-phenyl-stannolediide]). These were obtained by abstracting the solvent molecules from the potassium atoms of the corresponding monomers [Ln(η5-LSn)2K(thf)4]. The flexible coordination of the stannole dianion enables polymerization via potassium-mediated Sn–K–arene interactions, yielding linear chain structures while preserving a highly axial coordination environment around the Ln3+ center. Magnetic studies reveal that both [Ln(η5-LSn)2K]n (Ln = Tb, Dy) compounds behave as single-molecule magnets in zero field, with significantly enhanced performance compared to their monomeric analogues. In particular, [Dy(η5-LSn)2K]n exhibits an increased effective energy barrier of Ueff = 1812 K, representing an improvement of ∼20%, alongside suppressed quantum tunneling of magnetization and slower relaxation dynamics. Detailed analysis of the relaxation mechanisms indicates that polymerization reduces spin–phonon coupling, as evidenced by a marked suppression of the Raman relaxation process, despite softer lattice vibrational modes. Ab initio calculations confirm the retention of highly axial electronic structures. These results demonstrate that assembling axial lanthanidocenate units into one-dimensional frameworks is an effective strategy to enhance magnetic anisotropy and control relaxation pathways, providing a route to mitigate relaxation in high-performance lanthanide-based single-molecule magnets.
n88ea4b8d5f78: O3-type layered oxides represent an attractive class of sodium-ion battery cathodes, combining high theoretical specific capacity and high pristine Na content. However, their deeply desodiated frameworks at high voltages (≥4.0 V) are prone to redox-coupled distortion of TMO6 octahedra within the transition metal (TM) slabs, leading to severe structural degradation. Here, we originally define an ionic field strength disparity coefficient (η), which enables quantitative evaluation of the local chemical-field heterogeneity. The η is derived from the ratio between the standard deviation and the average value of ionic field strength (Φ) of all TM ions, defined as Φ= Z/r2, where Z and r correspond to the ionic charge and ionic radius, respectively. Introducing compensatory cations with an intermediate Φ value between two cations featuring largely disparate Φ values effectively reconciles local chemical-field discrepancy and lowers the η parameter upon charge–discharge processes. Moreover, synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy, strain mapping analyses, and first-principles calculations reveal that the low-η sample demonstrates the reduced lattice strain and enhanced structural reversibility. Consistently, electrochemical evaluation shows that it retains more than 80% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 10C, markedly outperforming the unmodified counterpart with only 22% retention. This work establishes the η as a quantitative descriptor for inactive dopant selection and provides a general strategy for developing highly stable layered oxide cathodes.
n5bd4512c57c5: Nonribosomal peptide synthetases (NRPSs) assemble structurally complex natural products but remain challenging targets for high-resolution structural analysis because of their conformational heterogeneity and dynamic catalytic cycles. SacC/SfmC is an unusual single-module NRPS that diverges from canonical peptide-forming assembly lines and instead catalyzes two sequential Pictet–Spengler reactions between a tyrosine-derived unit and a peptidyl aldehyde generated through thioester reduction. This cascade forms two C–C bonds, stereoselectively installs multiple stereogenic centers, and constructs the pentacyclic scaffold of bis-tetrahydroisoquinoline antitumor alkaloids including safracin B and the clinically important ecteinascidins. Here, we establish a state-resolved cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) strategy for structural interrogation of the monomeric noncanonical NRPS SacC and report its thioesterification-state structure at 2.76 Å resolution. Stabilization of this transient catalytic state was achieved by combining the cognate MbtH-like partner protein with a tailored covalent adenosine vinylsulfonamide probe that mimics the aminoacyl-adenylate intermediate and traps the phosphopantetheine-tethered species within the adenylation domain. The structure directly visualizes a carrier protein-tethered intermediate and reveals the spatial organization of the Pictet–Spengler, adenylation, peptidyl carrier protein, and reduction domains, providing the first structural view of a Pictet–Spengler cyclization domain embedded within an NRPS assembly line. In parallel, nonreducible ester probes corresponding to downstream PCP-bound intermediates were developed to enable structural interrogation of additional catalytic states along the SacC reaction trajectory. These results demonstrate that rational chemical probe design enables state-resolved cryo-EM analysis of highly dynamic, single-module NRPSs and establishes a general strategy for capturing catalytic trajectories and enabling the engineering of noncanonical NRPS reactivity.
nbbe0d3e3f3d7: Dithiolene metathesis catalysts have enabled breakthroughs in materials and medicinal contexts in which control of cis/trans alkene stereochemistry translates into control over function. Their extreme air-sensitivity, however, impedes widespread uptake. Building on the discovery that air-exposure selectively decomposes the leading catalyst Ru(S–S)(H2IPr)(═CHAr) (Ru-1a; S–S = 1,2-S2C6H2-3,6-Cl2, Ar = C6H4-2-OiPr) into four-coordinate oxo complex Ru-2 Ru(O)(S–S)(H2IPr), we demonstrate that the latter offers convenient access to Ru-1a and related catalysts via reaction with phosphorus ylides (Ph3P═CHR; R = Ar, Ph, H). This “deoxygenative metal carbenation” (DMC) strategy opens new opportunities in olefin metathesis. Beyond regeneration of Ru-1a after decomposition, it enables direct, tunable access to more active on-cycle species (potentially including tagged benzylidenes) from a robust, shelf-stable precursor. In situ generation of these well-defined active species confers metathesis activity and stereocontrol comparable to or better than pristine, meticulously handled Ru-1a, and far superior to samples of Ru-1a even briefly exposed to air in solution. In eliminating the need for production, shipping, and storage of air-sensitive Ru-1a, this advance is anticipated to expand the uptake of olefin metathesis for production of stereodefined alkenes.
n5c8de7fd0c13: The design of efficient photocatalysts requires control over both exciton dissociation and the subsequent transport of charge carriers. Donor–acceptor two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are widely used to promote charge separation, but the role of directional charge transport in these layered materials is still not well understood. Here, we combine photophysical characterization and time-dependent density functional theory calculations to study three TAPD-based COFs for photocatalytic H2O2 production via oxygen reduction. All materials show efficient in-plane donor–acceptor charge transfer with similar exciton dissociation behavior. At the same time, clear differences appear in their charge transport properties. The calculations indicate that electrons move preferentially along the stacking direction, while holes remain more delocalized within the COF plane. This anisotropic transport is most pronounced in the COFs where stronger interlayer coupling favors the formation of interlayer charge-transfer states, as observed in transient absorption measurements. These states allow electrons and holes to separate over adjacent layers, which reduces recombination losses and corroborates the observed differences in photocatalytic activity. Our results indicate that directional interlayer charge transport, rather than local donor–acceptor charge separation alone, is an important factor in determining photocatalytic performance in COFs.
n10bdc71000c7: Organophosphate hydrolysis under near-neutral conditions is intrinsically slow and generally requires strongly basic media or tailored catalysts. Here, we demonstrate that the electrolyte microenvironment can promote hydrolysis of dimethyl 4-nitrophenyl phosphate (DMNP) through an electrochemically generated base. Chemical controls show that DMNP hydrolysis depends on the combined effects of bulk pH, phosphate speciation, electrolyte concentration, and substrate accessibility. Under galvanostatic operation, cathodic water reduction generates OH– in situ, coupling hydrogen evolution to specific-base SN2(P) hydrolysis of DMNP. Time-resolved 31P NMR shows reciprocal DMNP consumption and dimethyl phosphate formation, while complementary UV–vis spectroscopy is consistent with formation of p-nitrophenolate. Although K2HPO4 and NaClO4 provide similar DMNP conversion at the same current, phosphate lowers the required overpotential and substantially improves energy-normalized conversion efficiency. Translation to a zero-gap membrane-electrode assembly enables stable full-cell operation and quantitative DMNP consumption within 1 h in a larger-volume, flow-compatible configuration. These findings establish galvanostatic in situ base generation as a controllable and modular strategy for organophosphate treatment in near-neutral aqueous media.
ne736f6de4e25: Dual-anion regulation induces covalency-driven amorphization in Li-Zr-Cl electrolytes, promoting Li+ transport, oxidative stability, and mechanical compliance. This bond-covalency-mediated strategy enables long-life all-solid-state lithium batteries and provides a general design principle for high-performance halide solid-state electrolytes.
n7385a583557b: Curvature couples polarization, crystalline defects, and interfacial electrostatics in freestanding ferroelectric oxides. Here, we examine bent epitaxial Pb(Zr0.2Ti0.8)O3/SrTiO3/Pb(Zr0.2Ti0.8)O3 (PZT/STO/PZT) membranes using atomic-resolution electron microscopy, strain and polarization mapping, relative projected-potential reconstruction, and molecular dynamics simulations. The tensile-side PZT remains comparatively lattice-continuous and accommodates bending mainly through polarization rotation and domain reorganization. The compressive-side PZT exhibits dislocations, slip-related lattice offsets, surface steps, and localized strain concentration. Curvature-series observations and images across U-shaped and N-shaped regions indicate that the defect-rich region follows the local compressive stress state. Bending also breaks the approximate electrostatic symmetry of the two PZT/STO interfaces: the tensile side shows weakened negative interfacial contrast, whereas the compressive side shows a dislocation-associated increase in relative projected potential. These results identify curvature as a variable for selecting polar versus plastic relaxation pathways and modulating interfacial electrostatic landscapes in flexible ferroelectric heterostructures.
nd8372d4936c1: Upconverting lanthanide-doped particles are widely used as nanoscale temperature sensors, particularly in biological and photonic environments. However, extending their functionality to simultaneously measure temperature and light intensity remains a challenge, as the luminescent response is highly sensitive to both the environment composition and its temperature. In this work, we combine deep-learning methods with large-scale spectral data sets to investigate the reliability of Er/Yb-doped particles to function as dual sensors. Spectral data are collected from single particles levitating in vacuum and ensembles of particles in application-relevant wet and dry media. Although traditional ratiometric methods reliably retrieve temperature irrespective of the environment and specific experimental apparatus, they fail to disentangle the complex dependencies needed for dual sensing. Our trained models overcome these limitations, accurately predicting both temperature and laser power despite environmental variability. This approach opens a new route toward robust, data-driven sensing with upconverting particles in complex or fluctuating conditions.
n973fa9c05764: Flexible photonic devices and soft microlasers have attracted increasing attention for wearable sensing, biomedical monitoring, and deformable optoelectronic systems. Their mechanical compliance enables intimate contact with soft biological tissues, allowing optical signals to be modulated by external mechanical stimuli. Such characteristics make flexible laser-based platforms particularly suitable for mechanical sensing and physiological signal detection. In this work, we present a flexible microlaser array-based photonic platform designed for mechanical sensing and pulse monitoring. By integrating microscale laser emitters into a soft, transparent matrix with a microstructured architecture, the device maintains stable laser emission while responding to external pressure and dynamic strain. The optical response of the microlaser array exhibits sensitivity to mechanical perturbations, enabling the detection of periodic signals associated with the human pulse. This work highlights the potential of flexible laser photonics as a versatile tool for noninvasive mechanical and physiological sensing in wearable healthcare applications.
nba03913388a3: Using two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) ferromagnets in spintronic devices can enhance their performance through well-controlled vdW interfaces and reduced power consumption. Cr2Te3 appears as a promising candidate because of its strong perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, but the Curie temperature is limited to 180 K. In this work, we use annealing in air to uncover the magnetic phase diagram of Cr2Te3. We correlate magnetic properties with layer stacking and the interlayer distance; both depend strongly on the annealing temperature. In particular, disorder in layer stacking plays a key role in the magnetic properties of Cr2Te3 and more generally of vdW ferromagnets. By annealing at 375 °C, we can eventually raise the Tc of Cr2Te3 up to 303 K in the epitaxial Cr2Te3/WSe2 vdW heterostructure with in-plane magnetic anisotropy. This work provides a simple method to control the magnetic properties of 2D ferromagnets and incorporate them into spintronics devices.
n5ec1c3f27341: Silicon anodes enable high-energy-density Li-ion batteries but face reversibility challenges when operating under extreme temperature and charge-rate conditions. Now, a liquid electrolyte design results in interface protection and reduced electrode expansion during such operation, while also having lithium plating tolerance.
nb2bc4b44a338: Cathode interlayers play a pivotal role in improving the performance of organic solar cells. Yao, Zhang, Zhang, Wang et al. show a stepwise solvent treatment to achieve a vertically aligned cathode interlayer, enabling a certified efficiency of 20.65% in binary organic solar cells.
ne155ad15dc4f: Gene expression reconstituted outside the cell controls the composition and dynamics of cytoskeletal networks, bringing the tools of synthetic biology to active matter and opening a route to genetically programmed biomaterials.
nb70f07fba36a: Stacking-controllable 2D In2Se3 grown by chemical vapour deposition reveals a strong dependence of ferroelectricity on stacking order. A 2H/3R homojunction memristor achieves an on/off ratio one order of magnitude higher than that of pure-phase devices, offering opportunities for advanced ferroelectric memory applications.
nc220489fcb25: Chemical ligation of synthetic polymers is achieved via supramolecular polymerization followed by dynamic covalent polycondensation in a process that does not require thermal activation.
na37558c52271: By creating permanent cavities of well-defined size and shape within a fluid, porous liquids bring the precise control over gases afforded by microporous solids to the realm of liquids. Here, we reflect on how the porous liquid concept, beyond simply imparting fluidity to a porous solid, provides a promising platform for overcoming long-standing challenges with manipulating dissolved gases.
n465e258842c4: Silver-catalyzed ethylene epoxidation is a cornerstone of the chemical industry, yet the operando surface structure of Ag nanoparticles and the identity of selectivity-governing active sites remain elusive. Here, we integrate machine learning potentials, stochastic surface walking global optimization, molecular dynamics simulation, and statistical analysis to resolve the surface landscape of Ag nanoparticles approaching experimentally relevant sizes under reaction conditions. Oxygen-induced reconstruction transforms pristine Ag facets into a globally amorphous oxide layer composed of three types of locally ordered ring motifs interspersed with structural defects. A pentagonal motif (ring5), topologically required to accommodate nanoparticle curvature and absent in conventional slab models, dominates the surface across all investigated particle sizes. Its recessed central Ag atom acts as an electronic charge buffer that weakens the critical C–Ag bond in the oxametallacycle intermediate, conferring high intrinsic ethylene oxide selectivity. Microkinetic analyses confirm that the oxygen species of ring5 regulate ethylene oxide yield, peaking at a nanoparticle oxidation degree of O/Ag ≈ 0.3–0.4. This work establishes a statistical paradigm for decoding active phases on realistic catalyst surfaces through dynamic structural ensembles.
nc8456e98e64c: The complex structure of polyurethanes (PURs) presents a major barrier to their efficient recycling. Here, we report a chemoenzymatic cascade that enables the simultaneous recycling and upcycling of PUR through rapid alkaline pretreatment followed by urethanase-catalyzed depolymerization. Using in-house-synthesized model polyether- and polyester-based PUR elastomers, we establish that soft-segment chemistry dictates the composition, morphology, and accessibility of the pretreated residues, thereby governing the efficiency of the subsequent enzymatic hydrolysis. This insight enabled translation of the cascade to a commercial PUR elastomer, achieving >93% chemical conversion and recovery of up to 1 mM 4,4′-methylenedianiline (MDA) (97.2% purity), corresponding to a 40-fold increase over the nonenzymatic control, together with polyols obtained in 95% isolated yield that were directly reused for PUR synthesis. Mechanistic studies further show that alkaline pretreatment enhances substrate accessibility for the enzyme, and structural analysis of urethanase SP2 reveals a carbamate-specific hydrogen-bonding interaction that promotes urethane hydrolysis while minimizing esterase activity. The cascade was additionally applied to highly crosslinked commercial PUR foams and adhesives, demonstrating its versatility toward industrially relevant waste streams. Overall, this work establishes a mechanistically informed chemoenzymatic platform for PUR depolymerization and provides a strategy for converting chemically recalcitrant PUR waste into reusable molecular building blocks.
n1b554c55772f: Alkenes are among the most abundant and versatile feedstocks in synthetic chemistry, yet methods for their direct and regioselective conversion into nitrogen-containing frameworks remain scarce. In particular, the direct catalytic amidination of alkenes has remained underdeveloped. Herein, we report a rhodium-catalyzed anti-Markovnikov amidination of alkenes using a stable pyridinyl formimidamide synthon. This reaction enables the direct installation of amidine moieties onto a wide range of alkenes, including styrenes, aliphatic alkenes, and challenging internal alkenes that undergo efficient chain-walking with high regioselectivity and broad functional group tolerance, accommodating unprotected amines, phenols, and halides. The resulting pyridyl amidines can be readily transformed into amides, carboxylic acids and esters, establishing a practical platform for alkene diversification. Notably, late-stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules, including cyclosporine A, FK506, and quinine etc., provides access to previously inaccessible analogues. Mechanistic investigations, highlighted by the crystallographic capture of a key rhodium–aminopyridinyl formimidamide intermediate, provide compelling evidence for the proposed catalytic cycle. Collectively, this work not only fills a critical gap in alkene functionalization but also offers a concise and general route to high-value nitrogen-containing architectures.
n9cedba7009ee: The asymmetric construction of nonadjacent stereocenters in a single catalytic system remains a significant challenge due to the difficulty in controlling stereochemical relay between sequential transformations. Herein, we report a dual-enzyme relay catalytic system that integrates an artificial streptavidin-based copper metalloenzyme (Sav-Cu) with an engineered ketoreductase (KRED) for the one-pot synthesis of polycyclic alcohols bearing 1,3-non-adjacent stereocenters. In this relay process, the engineered SavDMase variant (S112A/K121D) catalyzes a non-natural decarboxylative Mannich reaction to establish the R-configured stereocenter in the enantioenriched ketone intermediate, which is then recognized by the engineered KREDAV mutant (S96A/Y190V) and reduced with high diastereo- and enantioselectivity to install the S-configured alcohol stereocenter, thereby furnishing the (R,S)-configured product as the dominant stereoisomer. The optimized system furnishes the products in up to 83% yield, 99% ee, and 96% de across a broad substrate scope, and is readily applicable to 2 mmol-scale synthesis. Structural analysis, docking, and molecular dynamics simulations support complementary roles of the two catalytic modules: SavDMase promotes productive organization of the Mannich step, while KREDAV stabilizes the reactive binding pose and constrains the hydride-transfer trajectory to enforce stereoselective reduction. This work demonstrates how artificial and natural enzymes can be integrated in relay catalysis to solve challenging stereochemical relay problems beyond the reach of individual biocatalysts.
nb3798da3a65c: In heterogeneous catalysis, the electronic structures of catalysts' active sites are modified to optimize intermediate binding and bond activation for achieving high reaction activity. However, studies on regulating the atomic structures of catalytic materials to enhance the configurational diversity of adsorbed intermediates remain scarce. Herein, we demonstrate that engineering under-coordinated active site motifs enables an entropy-enhanced catalytic mechanism that harnesses the configurational freedom of surface intermediates to improve reaction rates at reduced temperatures. Using CO2 methanation as a model reaction, we identified that under-coordinated Ru2+−oxygen vacancy (Ru2+−VO) sites promote delocalized catalyst−intermediate interactions and reduce the reaction energy barrier. Stable Ru2+−VO sites were created on Au nanoparticle-grafted (RuOx)a(CeOy)b solid-solution nanorods through plasmonic effects under reducing conditions. Eyring plot analysis revealed an activation entropy gain of TΔΔS‡ ≈ 12 kJ mol−1 for CO2 methanation at 300 °C, in situ spectroscopy revealed a *HCOO-mediated pathway, and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations indicated a 0.22 eV free-energy barrier for *HCOO formation on Ru2+−VO motifs. A CH4 production rate of 550 mmol gcat−1 h−1 with >98% selectivity and >280 h stability at 300 °C was achieved at a high gas hourly space velocity of 40,000−100,000 mL gcat−1 h−1. The findings provide a conceptual framework beyond adsorption energy optimization in catalyst design, showing that configurational entropy is a tunable descriptor for enhancing catalytic kinetics.
n5cb9e09ff6c8: Efficient activation of interfacial water molecules and fast proton transfer are critical but challenging for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Herein, a Lewis–Brønsted dual-acid catalyst design strategy is proposed to achieve accelerated acidic OER by synergistically optimizing the configuration of interfacial water molecules and proton transfer kinetics on Mn-doped IrO2. In this catalyst, the Mn dopant serves as a Lewis acid site that readily captures hydroxyl groups, which perturbs the local hydrogen-bonding network and induces interfacial water molecules to form an H-down configuration toward surface active sites, thereby promoting the enrichment and dissociation of reactive interfacial water. On this basis, the formation of the Mn–Obri–Ir local structure enhances the Brønsted acidity of the bridge oxygen (Obri) site, accelerates the deprotonation of the Obri–H bond, promotes the formation of key OER intermediates and accelerates the reaction kinetics. Mn dopant also induces electron enrichment around Ir, suppresses excessive oxidation and dissolution of Ir species, and enhances catalyst stability performance. These synergistic effects enable Mn-IrO2 to achieve a 160 mV overpotential at 10 mA cm–2 and to operate stably for 1500 h at 10 mA cm–2 and 1200 h at 1.0 A cm–2 in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), demonstrating the promising potential of the Lewis–Brønsted dual-acid strategy in acidic OER catalyst design.
n5b2edc4d58d9: The selective conversion of methane to methanol remains a major challenge in catalysis, and no earth-abundant homogeneous catalyst has been demonstrated to carry out this transformation with high turnover. To explore previously synthesized complexes that might be amenable for this transformation, we start from macrocyclic ligands from experimental structures in the Cambridge Structural Database. After expanding this set of ligands with Hammett-tuning functionalization, we construct a design space of 21.9 million Mn and Fe catalysts. We employ active learning using neural network surrogate models with quantified uncertainty to efficiently identify catalysts with optimal methane-to-methanol turnover. We do this by jointly optimizing density functional theory (DFT)-computed hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) and methyl radical rebound energetics. Square planar tetraaza-based macrocycles in combination with low-spin Fe(II) or Mn(II) emerge as a privileged class of transition metal complexes within the Pareto-optimal set, with Mn(II) catalysts exhibiting balanced energetic tradeoffs of the two steps. In contrast, porphyrin catalysts exhibit favorable HAT but unfavorable rebound, and seesaw catalysts, which are not widely employed, are indeed the least favorable in our set. Full reaction coordinate analysis of representative Pareto-optimal catalysts reveals that HAT and rebound thermodynamics no longer govern turnover, which is instead determined by the stability of the metal–oxo intermediate and the rebound kinetic barrier. Nonetheless, the resulting energetic spans for these catalysts remain competitive with known earth-abundant, methane-to-methanol catalysts, underscoring the effectiveness of active learning for discovering previously unexplored, synthetically accessible catalysts and unraveling catalyst design principles for methane-to-methanol reactivity.
n30646491aa66: Transition-metal-catalyzed cyclization of 1,n-enynes represents a versatile platform for the construction of structurally diverse chiral heterocycles. Despite substantial advances in this field, the enantioselective cyclizative alkylation of 1,n-enynes remains a formidable synthetic challenge, primarily due to the inherent difficulty in simultaneous control of regio-, chemo-, and stereoselectivity. Herein, we disclose a highly enantioselective cyclizative alkylation of 1,6-enynes employing two complementary alkylating reagents: diazo compounds and readily available alkyl iodides. This protocol proceeds under mild conditions and features broad substrate scope, delivering enantioenriched γ-lactams and pyrrolidine derivatives bearing quaternary stereogenic centers in good yields (up to 81%) and enantioselectivities (53 examples, up to 98% ee). Mechanistic studies corroborate that these two types of alkylating reagents follow entirely distinct catalytic pathways.
n6fd9c930f1c5: Selective one-step conversion of methane (CH4) to methanol (CH3OH) remains a grand challenge in catalysis, constrained by the trade-off between C─H bond activation and product overoxidation. Here, we integrate density functional theory (DFT) calculations with plasma-catalytic experiments to investigate direct CH4-to-CH3OH conversion using H2O as the sole oxidant on CuxOy clusters within MOR zeolite, compared to the CuO(111) surface. We show that C─H bond activation proceeds preferentially via homolytic H-abstraction on zeolite-confined CuxOy clusters, with Cu3O3/MOR exhibiting a low activation barrier of only 0.21 eV, more than three times lower than that on CuO(111). Vibrational mode-specificity analysis shows that the C─H stretching modes couple most effectively on higher-barrier surfaces. Importantly, we demonstrate that plasma-generated radical intermediates (CH3·, H·, OH·) reshape the reaction thermodynamics, with the Gibbs free energy shifting from endothermic (+1.13 eV) to exothermic (–3.21 eV and –8.25 eV), enabling pathways inaccessible under thermal conditions. Experimentally, Cu/MOR catalysts prepared by ion exchange, which favor well-dispersed zeolite-confined Cu-oxo sites, achieve the highest CH3OH production rate (0.26 mmol/h) at low plasma power (6.5 W), outperforming catalysts prepared by wetness impregnation. This work bridges Cu-oxo site topology, vibrational mode specificity, and radical-mediated thermodynamics, offering valuable insights for plasma-catalytic selective CH4-to-CH3OH conversion.
n96109b342764: The free C2-OH group of glycosyl donors is generally viewed as a liability in glycosylation because it can act as a competing nucleophile and compromise stereocontrol. Here, we show that this functionality can instead be harnessed as a programmable stereochemical element in a catalyst-controlled stereodivergent glycosylation. A single β-configured 2-hydroxy glycosyl 8-alkynyl-1-naphthoate donor was found to deliver either β- or α-glycosides simply by changing the gold(I) catalyst system. Triflate-based catalysts promoted highly β-selective glycosylation, whereas bistriflimide-based conditions enabled complementary α-selective glycosylation from the same donor. The method is applicable to a range of carbohydrate and noncarbohydrate acceptors and enables the programmable assembly of glucooligosaccharides bearing β-(1→6), α-(1→6), and alternating α/β-(1→6) linkages from a common donor platform. Mechanistic studies, including intermediate characterization, variable-temperature NMR experiments, computational analysis, and control glycosylations with the corresponding 2-O-Bn donor, reveal distinct roles of the donor 2-OH group in the two stereochemical manifolds.
n07dd93a63c45: Photocatalytic activation of inert chemical bonds represents a promising route for selective conversion of organic molecules such as acetonitrile (CH3CN) into value-added products. However, as the most common reactive oxygen species, •OH radicals are nonselective and usually lead to overoxidation reactions, making it difficult to realize the target product with both high activity and selectivity in the photocatalytic system. Here, we demonstrate that, through oxygen vacancy (Vo) engineering, selective CH3CN conversion into HCOOH is enabled over a WO3 photocatalyst under mild conditions. Under simulated solar irradiation, the as-prepared Vo-rich WO3 nanosheets display notable photocatalytic CH3CN conversion performance, with a HCOOH yield rate of 8.8 mmol g–1 h–1 and a selectivity as high as 86.5%. In combination of various in situ spectroscopic techniques, it is revealed that the Vo constructs a coupling match between of •OH radicals and •CH2CN intermediates on the WO3 photocatalyst surface, which facilitates the selective conversion of CH3CN into HCOOH while preventing its overoxidation. This work extends the conversion pathway of CH3CN in a photocatalytic route and provides deeper insight into the selective conversion of inert molecules.
n7ba9123ac4bf: We investigate the interplay between carbon accumulation and redox-driven deactivation pathways in cerium-containing nickel (NiCe) and palladium (PdCe) bimetallic precursor materials upon eventual decomposition into a Ni- or Pd-ceria interfacial system during dry reforming of methane (DRM). By probing defined intermediate states, information from surface electronic structure, morphology, and bulk structure to track structural and chemical changes across several reaction, deactivation, and CO2 titration cycles is combined to identify how carbon accumulation, oxygen transfer, and dynamic metal–ceria interfacial interactions evolve under DRM reaction conditions. Despite their similar cerium-containing precursor architecture and surface composition, the two systems allow studying two detrimental deactivation processes. Bimetallic NiCe decomposes more readily into a Ni-ceria interface, where carbon formation is progressively suppressed. Loss of activity is a result of oxidation of Ni particles mediated by enhanced oxygen transfer from ceria. In contrast, bimetallic PdCe is much more decomposition-resistant, and the localized Pd-ceria interface exhibits high activity throughout multiple DRM cycles, even in the presence of substantial carbon deposition and filamentous carbon growth. The results demonstrate an intrinsic coupling between carbon accumulation and oxygen transfer to the metallic component, with carbon acting as a competing sink for reactive oxygen species. We emphasize the significance of dynamic interfacial structures and show that ceria-mediated oxygen transfer produces contrasting, metal-dependent catalytic outcomes. Whereas in NiCe, efficient oxygen delivery suppresses carbon accumulation, but progressively oxidizes Ni and diminishes methane activation, in PdCe, carbon generation outpaces oxygen-mediated removal, yielding a carbon-rich yet catalytically persistent surface.
n48f8def67571: A modified colloidal atomic layer deposition at room temperature grows a vacancy-ordered Cs2SnCl6 shell epitaxially on CsPbCl3 nanocrystals, avoiding the core degradation and parasitic shell nucleation that accompany high-temperature routes. The resulting core–shell nanocrystals achieve an absolute photoluminescence quantum yield of 62% and retain 65% of their emission after six months of ambient storage and 30% after 48 h of exposure to added water.
n874a803e9337: Rechargeable magnesium (Mg) metal batteries are promising high-energy-density alternatives to lithium-ion systems, yet sluggish cathode kinetics hinder their development. Departing from the conventional host-centric view, we demonstrate that reversibility in Mg batteries can be governed by electrolyte-derived reaction chemistry. Here, we harness trace water to impart controlled electrolyte reactivity, enabling electrolyte-derived Mg/Cl-containing species to participate in cathode activation. In tunnel-type MnO2, the regulated electrolyte induces lattice expansion and improves electrochemical reversibility. In organic cathodes, improved rechargeability is consistent with a stabilizing role of Cl– in anion-coupled redox. Because polar-solvent chemistry can irreversibly passivate Mg metal, a Sn/MgCl2 artificial interface suppresses parasitic anode reactions while preserving cathode activation. This strategy enables reversible electrochemistry across oxide, organic, and conversion cathodes, including α/γ-MnO2, methylphenothiazine, tetrathiafulvalene, and hybrid I2/O2 systems. These findings establish electrolyte-derived chemical activation as a guiding principle for regulating cathode reaction pathways in magnesium batteries.
n7b18684a7f4e: Leveraging oxygen redox in lithium-rich layered oxides paves the way for increasing the energy density of lithium-ion batteries, whose practical implementation is plagued by poor stability. Although a uniform Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is suggested to improve cycle stability, the synthesis–structure relationship governing domain formation remains underexplored. Here, we show that Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is derived by the precursor structure according to the degree of transition-metal separation. Through a comparative investigation of the synthesis mechanism, we reveal the templating effect that more clustered transition-metal oxide precursors lead to more localized Li2MnO3-like ordering in the final cathodes, a tendency also observed with a different lithium source. Furthermore, it is corroborated that cathodes with more dispersed Li2MnO3-like ordering derived from less-ordered precursors exhibit improved electrochemical stability with a mitigated voltage decay. Our findings highlight the significance of precursor design and engineering for structural regulation of high-performance lithium-rich layered oxide cathodes.
n8d648f4076f8: The rational combination of multiple electrolyte additives is a promising strategy for constructing stable interphases in lithium-ion batteries. However, unintended additive interactions can alter the preferential reduction/oxidation pathways at electrode surfaces, compromising cell performance. In this study, we identify a detrimental interaction between succinonitrile (SN) and lithium bis(oxalato)borate (LiBOB) on a graphite-silicon (Gr-Si) anode. Specifically, an electron-deficient boron-embedded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) derived from LiBOB promotes the reduction of the electron-rich nitrile moieties of SN, disrupting fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)-driven SEI construction. Based on this mechanism, SN was replaced with triisopropanolamine borate (TPAB), which mitigates transition metal dissolution through its amine moiety while forming a robust borate-based cathode electrolyte interphase. Moreover, TPAB combined with LiBOB avoided detrimental side reductions at the anode–electrolyte interface. The FEC-LiBOB-TPAB combination creates thermally stable interphases on the Gr-Si anode and LiNi0.91Co0.08Al0.01O2 cathode (4.8 mAh cm–2), enabling 68.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 45 °C and 1C.
n03850d8c938a: Polymer film capacitors are fundamental to modern power electronics, yet low permittivity restricts their energy density. Although poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) possesses high intrinsic permittivity, stabilizing its polar structure remains thermodynamically challenging. Here, we report a scalable physical processing strategy to optimize PVDF-based films via a specialized shear-imposed coating methodology. By employing a micro-structured blade, we generate intense local shear flow fields that exert hydrodynamic tension to drive a coil-stretch transition. This process drives an α-to-β phase transition and templates the growth of oriented, polar-phase-rich crystal structures. Furthermore, we develop a stage-wise regulation strategy using binary solvents to orchestrate evaporation dynamics, effectively trapping these metastable shear-induced conformations before relaxation. Effective across the PVDF copolymer family, this method enables P(VDF-HFP) films to achieve a high energy density of 20.05 J/cm3, a 44% improvement over conventional casting. This work provides a general, non-chemical pathway for manufacturing high-performance functional polymers through multi-physical field synergistic regulation.
ned76db721745: Atomic precision in metal–sulfur assemblies offers a transformative pathway to programmable nanomaterials, with applications spanning energy-efficient optoelectronics to highly selective CO2 reduction catalysis. However, the inherent lability of the metal–sulfur bond remains a formidable barrier to the rational design of robust frameworks. While strong-field ligands such as cyclic (alkyl)(amino)carbenes (CAACs) are gold-standard scaffolds for stabilizing reactive monometallic centers, their impact on the structural fidelity of multinuclear clusters remains elusive. Herein, we report a combined experimental and theoretical investigation of a CAAC-supported Cu8(μ3-S)4 cluster─a high-impact prototype for metal-chalcogenide systems with relatively weak metal–sulfur bonds. Through electrochemical and protonation studies, we demonstrate that while the potent σ-donor ability of the CAAC ligand successfully enforces solution integrity and thermal resilience, the structural boundaries of the multinuclear scaffold under chemical stress are ultimately governed by the core topology and metal–sulfur bond lability rather than local metal–ligand bonding. In-depth density functional theory (DFT) analysis demonstrates that while the CAAC ligands actively strengthen the peripheral Cu–S bonds via a pronounced inverse trans influence, the trigonal pyramidal (μ3-S) motifs remain vulnerable to proton-induced bond labilization and oxidative S–S coupling. Our findings establish that the design rules for multinuclear assemblies diverge fundamentally from monometallic species: whereas CAACs successfully passivate peripheral coordination sites to thermal decomposition, they do not preclude internal, core-mediated degradation pathways. These clear boundaries reveal that achieving structural durability in functional base metal–sulfur assemblies requires pairing strong local donors with supramolecular and/or multidentate ligand strategies designed explicitly to buttress the metal–sulfur core.
na63ddf29bdbb: Supercapacitors, possessing rapid charge–discharge time scales and cycle lifetimes, provide opportunities to mitigate fluctuations from intermittent energy sources. However, while supercapacitors exhibit lower energy densities to lithium-ion batteries, advancing supercapacitor energy density is necessary to improve their utility in applications requiring rapid operating time scales. Supercapacitor energy densities critically hinge on interfacial capacitances and electrolyte voltage windows. Ionic liquids have been heavily investigated as supercapacitor electrolytes due to promising properties like high electrochemical stability, nonflammability, and nonvolatility. Yet, energy densities of ionic liquid-derived supercapacitors are often limited by low interfacial capacitances due to pronounced ion–ion correlations. Here, we show capacitance can be significantly enhanced in ionic liquids over wide voltages by mixing ionic liquids to improve electric double layer entropy. Importantly, capacitance increases exhibited by mixtures persist over the entire electrochemical stability window, showing like-charged co-ions often play similar roles to oppositely charged counterions when determining double layer capacitance. By leveraging electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and surface forces measurements, we conclude that capacitive enhancements originate from changes in short-range nanostructures in ionic liquids, where atomic force microscopy measurements reveal that mixing ionic liquids results in more compact bound ion layers with increased disorder and compressibility. Notably, we find that long-range decay lengths are statistically similar between neat ionic liquids and an equimolar mixture at potentials where we report up to 150% capacitance enhancement, indicating decoupling between the bulk electrostatic decay length and interfacial capacitance. Overall, our results reveal that modulating compositional entropy of ionic liquid double layers provides avenues to increase supercapacitor energy densities and advance next-generation energy storage.
nf2c64444c817: Deterministic switching of skyrmion topology is a central frontier in topological spintronics, yet current paradigms rely almost exclusively on dissipative-current-driven spin torques. Here, we propose a fundamentally distinct mechanism for the nonvolatile switching of the skyrmion topology in two-dimensional multiferroics. We reveal that the intrinsic magnetoelectric coupling intimately links the out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization to interlayer magnetic exchange. Consequently, an electric-field-driven polarization reversal deterministically converts the interlayer coupling between the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic states. This macroscopic exchange reversal directly flips the microscopic skyrmion core polarity and reverses its topological charge, thereby stabilizing the two electrically addressable topological phases. Guided by our established design principles, we rigorously validate this mechanism in a Co2CF2/MoN2 multiferroic heterostructure by using combined first-principles calculations and atomistic spin simulations. Our findings bypass the limitations of continuous current injection, establishing a robust physical framework for energy-efficient multiferroic topological spintronics.
n01061537f593: Natural enzymes achieve catalytic efficiency through the synergistic coupling of substrate activation and the efficient utilization of reactive intermediates. However, current nanozyme design paradigms focus predominantly on modulating substrate activation while overlooking the efficient utilization of highly reactive intermediates─a limitation that severely constrains substantial gains in catalytic activity. Inspired by the frustrated Lewis pair (FLP) composition of Fe2+ and tetrahydrobiopterin in tryptophan hydroxylase, we propose an FLP engineering approach to integrate 2,5-pyrazine-dicarboxylic acid (Pz) into the Materials of Institut Lavoisier-101 metal–organic framework (MIL-101(Fe)-H MOF) to construct MIL-101(Fe)-Pz MOF. This construct features pyrazine-nitrogen as a Lewis base and unsaturated Fe sites as Lewis acids. Compared with the Lewis acid-only MIL-101(Fe)-H MOF control, the as-fabricated FLP substantially accelerated the peroxidase-like activity of MIL-101(Fe)-Pz MOF, increasing the maximum reaction velocity by 4.83-fold when H2O2 was used as the substrate and by 17.88-fold when 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) was used as the substrate. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses revealed that the distinct electronic interactions within FLP facilitate electron transfer, promote H2O2 activation, improve hydroxyl radical utilization, and lower the reaction energy barrier, thereby boosting the reaction kinetics. This work highlights the indispensable role of substrate activation and active intermediate utilization in enhancing nanozyme performance and also provides guidance for the design of next-generation bioinspired nanozymes.
na94c29e8485a: Heterostructures of 2D materials offer high tunability of magnetic properties, including current-induced magnetization switching by unconventional spin–orbit torques. The microscopic mechanisms governing spin-torque switching in van der Waals systems, however, remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate current-induced magnetization reversal in an Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) and WTe2 heterostructure using scanning harmonic magneto-optical Kerr effect microscopy. Spatially resolved magnetization maps show that field-free switching unfolds from asymmetric domain nucleation at the edges of the FGT flake, followed by domain wall propagation. This switching behavior is deterministic and bipolar, consistent with spin–orbit torques arising from the injection of both in-plane and out-of-plane spins from WTe2 into FGT. The critical currents for up-to-down and down-to-up switching differ because of asymmetric domain nucleation and directional domain wall pinning effects. Micromagnetic simulations reproduce the switching behavior observed experimentally, showing how the initial domain nucleation sites are determined by the sample geometry and combined influence of in-plane and out-of-plane spins and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. Finally, by systematically varying the field-like and damping-like torque components and sweeping the spin polarization between in-plane and out-of-plane, we identify the torque configurations that yield the most efficient switching in van der Waals magnets with different shapes.
n06f743d7beac: Silicon–carbon anodes are among the most promising candidates for high-energy lithium-ion batteries, yet their practical implementation remains constrained by lithiation-induced outward deformation, electrode cracking, and persistent interphase degradation. Here, closed pores are introduced as internal stress-regulation units to address the coupled mechanical and electrochemical instability of silicon–carbon anodes. Heteroatom-doped carbon hosts are engineered to contain abundant closed nanopores, which redirect expansion-induced stress toward the particle interior and suppress macroscopic electrode swelling. Meanwhile, heteroatom doping enlarges the carbon interlayer spacing and enhances electronic conductivity, enabling accelerated and more balanced Li+ insertion/extraction kinetics. As a representative material, the nitrogen–doped silicon–carbon composite delivers a reversible capacity of 1756.5 mAh g− 1, an initial Coulombic efficiency of 90.2%, and 868.4 mAh g−1 at 3 C, while reducing electrode thickness expansion from 38.4% to 13.1% after 50 cycles. The material is further produced in 6 kg batches and enables 2 Ah LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) pouch cells with 80.0% capacity retention after 1200 cycles and only 8.4% thickness growth after 900 cycles. Machine–learning–guided phosphorus doping further validates the transferability of the closed-pore design. This work establishes closed-pore stress regulation as a scalable structural strategy for practical low-expansion silicon–carbon anodes.
n98975993b9fa: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) constitutes a major energetic bottleneck in electrochemical hydrogen production. Replacing OER with low‐potential organic oxidation provides an effective route to reduce cell voltage while enabling value‐added chemical synthesis. Here, a nanostructured Au electrocatalyst is developed from recycled electronic waste via a corrosion‐template–assisted electrodeposition strategy. Co(OH)2 nanoarrays grown on nickel foam act as a sacrificial template to regulate galvanic displacement between chloride‐coordinated Au(III) species and metallic Ni, inducing polycrystalline Au nucleation with tailored surface structures. Subsequent electrodeposition precisely controls Au size and dispersion, resulting in a substantially enlarged electrochemically active surface area. In alkaline media, the Au electrode selectively drives aldehyde oxidation of 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural to 5‐hydroxymethyl‐2‐furoic acid at potentials well below those required for OER, while enabling concurrent anodic hydrogen evolution and stable low‐voltage bipolar hydrogen production. In a flow‐electrolysis configuration, current densities of ∼0.6 A cm−2 are sustained at a low cell voltage of ∼1.2 V for over 200 h. By decoupling low‐potential aldehyde oxidation from high‐potential deep oxidation in a tandem electrolyzer, stepwise electrochemical upgrading from HMF to FDCA is achieved with reduced overall energy input. This work establishes a scalable electrochemical platform that integrates low‐voltage hydrogen production with high‐value biomass conversion.
n6cc6a580b2a3: Aqueous Mn metal batteries (AMMBs) have emerged as promising candidates for stationary energy storage owing to the natural abundance of Mn, their operational safety, and their high energy density. However, the high chemical reactivity of the Mn metal anode induces a severe hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), resulting in poor cycling reversibility. Fundamentally, HER is a parasitic cathodic reaction competing with Mn electrodeposition and may accompany Mn corrosion. Its kinetics are influenced by the interfacial water environment within the electric double layer (EDL). In this study, we propose a strategy for reconstructing the EDL by adding n‐decyltrimethylammonium bromide (10‐DTAB), a surfactant with a relatively high lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), to the electrolyte to stabilize the Mn anode. The high LUMO energy level enhances its reduction stability, thus preventing continuous decomposition during cycling and enabling sustained interfacial protection. Consequently, the Mn anode exhibits a markedly enhanced Coulombic efficiency of 93%. This study demonstrates a durable EDL regulation paradigm based on high‐LUMO additives, offering new insights into stabilizing Mn metal anodes and advancing AMMBs toward practical applications.
nc64fefbc690c: Tomographic volumetric printing (TVP) enables rapid fabrication of complex, centimeter-scale 3D architectures. TVP of native proteins such as collagen is attractive because it preserves native bioactive motifs that regulate cell–matrix signaling. However, direct TVP of collagen remains challenging because dityrosine crosslinking, driven by visible-light-activated Ru(II)bpy3 2+/sodium persulfate (SPS), lacks an effective inhibitory mechanism. This results in near-immediate crosslinking upon light exposure, leading to an insufficient nonlinear threshold response that fails to suppress background curing. Here, we introduce vitamin C (L-ascorbic acid) as a biocompatible redox regulator to overcome this limitation. We demonstrated that vitamin C established a photo-redox threshold by suppressing Ru(III) accumulation and scavenging persulfate radicals within the Ru/SPS system, thereby delaying dityrosine crosslinking until vitamin C depletion. This threshold generated the nonlinear response required for TVP, enabling high-fidelity volumetric printing of collagen. Post-printing construct densification (∼53% shrinkage) further improved feature resolution (80 µm positive; 120 µm negative) and yielded mechanically stable and highly stretchable hydrogels (up to 180% strain). Collagen resin with vitamin C supported both cell seeding post-printing and cell-laden printing with high cell density and viability, enabling the rapid biofabrication of cell-instructive 3D microenvironments.
n77a3f8a20622: Electrosynthesis of N,N‐dimethylformamide (DMF) via C─N coupling offers a sustainable alternative to energy‐intensive thermal routes but is hindered by low reactant concentration at the anode and sluggish proton‐coupled electron transfer. Here we report a new electrochemical route for DMF synthesis by the co‐oxidation of dimethylamine and ethylene glycol. Notably, over a CuO electrode, the addition of 0.5 mM sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate (SDBS) to the electrolyte significantly enhances reaction kinetics and Faradaic efficiency for DMF (FEDMF), achieving a DMF production rate to 0.78 mmol h−1 cm−2, over three times higher than that without SDBS. Using a 25 cm2 CuO electrode in 0.5 M NaHCO3 with 0.5 mM SDBS, a current of approximately 2.0 A and a DMF production rate of 7.5 mmol h−1 are achieved. Mechanistic investigations reveal that SDBS acts as a multifunctional ionic anchor, reorienting its sulfonate group toward the anode and projecting its hydrophobic tail into the electrolyte under reaction conditions. This configuration suppresses the oxygen evolution reaction while simultaneously enriching reactants, promoting deprotonation and proton transfer, and facilitating electron transfer, thereby enhancing both reaction kinetics and FEDMF.
n63a697a97325: Direct synthesis of organonitrogen compounds from dinitrogen (N2) remains a formidable challenge because N2‐to‐C─N bond formation requires nitrogen fixation to be coupled with selective functionalization of N2‐derived intermediates before their termination as ammonia. Herein, we report a cascade electrochemical strategy that converts N2 into aryl imides and aryl sulfonimides in a gas‐diffusion electrochemical flow cell. Under proton‐donor‐free conditions, electrochemically generated Li3N is intercepted by acyl or sulfonyl chlorides, enabling one‐pot synthesis of aryl imides and sulfonimides from N2 in yields up to 57%. This represents a notably high yield for direct N2‐derived organonitrogen synthesis. This work couples N2 fixation and C─N/S─N bond formation, expanding electrochemical nitrogen fixation beyond ammonia synthesis toward direct construction of value‐added C─N/S─N bonds.
nbdce9ae60748: Realizing ultra‐narrowband multiple‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) with long‐wavelength emission remains a formidable challenge due to the increased vibronic coupling and excited‐state relaxation with the extension of π‐conjugated framework. In this contribution, a proof‐of‐concept of centrosymmetric molecular strategy fused with quadruple boron–nitrogen heteroarenes is proposed to develop ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters. Thus, two MR‐TADF emitters, called DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR, are prepared and characterized. Compounds DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR exhibit the emission peaks at 562 nm and 518 nm in toluene solution, respectively. Small full‐width at half‐maximum (FWHM) of only 16 nm (0.063 eV) for DCz‐MR and 12 nm (0.055 eV) for DAn‐MR are obtained in toluene, especially 14.2 nm (0.058 eV) for DCz‐MR and 8.2 nm (0.040 eV) for DAn‐MR in hexane. In solution‐processed phosphorescence‐sensitized organic light‐emitting diodes, DAn‐MR delivers a maximum external quantum efficiency of 24.8% with an electroluminescence FWHM of 27 nm. This research work provides a new method for designing ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters.
ne1c80ac258e7: MYC is an intrinsically disordered oncoprotein that drives cancer progression via widespread transcriptional dysregulation. Upon binding partner protein MAX, their basic‐helix1‐loop‐helix2‐Zip (bHLH‐Zip) domains assemble into an ordered heterodimer that binds E‐box DNA to promote cellular proliferation. This interface has been undruggable by small molecules. Here, we report a novel covalent downsizing strategy to inhibit MYC‐MAX interaction by targeting the C‐terminal Cys438 present in MYC, but absent in MAX and related proteins. Incorporating a mild acrylamide electrophile to covalently bond specifically with Cys438 enabled truncation of MAX to shorter peptides with high affinity for MYC. Using intracellular protein‐fragment complementation, MAX‐derived sequences were optimized for interaction with MYC. Further downsizing, inserting a helix‐inducing constraint, and optimal electrophile positioning produced a serum‐stable 24‐residue covalent inhibitor that captured endogenous MYC from cell lysates. Esterifying six Glu/Asp residues enhanced membrane permeability, while intracellular esterolysis achieved robust cytosolic and nuclear accumulation of the MYC inhibitor. Microscopy confirmed nuclear delivery correlating directly with progressive loss of nuclear MYC. The esterified compound exhibited antiproliferative activity across MYC‐dependent cancer cell lines, inhibited migration, and triggered ubiquitin‐proteasome mediated MYC degradation, downregulating key target genes downstream of MYC. This covalent downsizing approach is a generalizable chemical strategy for targeting recalcitrant transcription factors.
n19b2becbf244: Radiotherapy (RT) efficacy is often limited by two key challenges: rapid restoration of tumor genomic integrity through DNA repair and the lack of tumor‐confined radiosensitization. Although existing radiosensitizers can enhance initial DNA damage, they generally fail to suppress subsequent self‐repair of tumor cells and often induce off‐target toxicity due to nonspecific activation. Here, we report a hydrated electron (eaq−${\mathrm{e}}_{{\mathrm{aq}}}^ - $)‐activated nano‐radiosensitizer (RT‐nRS) that enables tumor‐confined radiosensitization by converting transient RT‐induced damage into persistent subcellular dysfunction. Unlike conventional RT‐responsive systems that rely on short‐lived reactive oxygen species, RT‐nRS leverages the longer lifetime of eaq−${\mathrm{e}}_{{\mathrm{aq}}}^ - $ to trigger the irradiation‐induced zwitterion‐to‐cationic surface transformation, thereby maintaining systemic circulation stability while enhancing tumor cellular internalization. Furthermore, preferential accumulation and prolonged retention within the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) enable RT‐nRS to induce sustained ER stress, thereby simultaneously amplifying DNA damage and suppressing DNA repair. Our results demonstrate that RT‐nRS effectively overcomes tumor radioresistance while minimizing off‐target toxicity to non‐irradiated normal tissues, leading to significantly enhanced radiotherapy efficacy. Our work establishes hydrated electron‐responsive chemistry as a strategy for spatiotemporally controlled radiosensitization and provides a general framework for converting transient radiotherapeutic stimuli into durable biological outcomes.
n33afb079102a: The inherent trade‐off between high mechanical performance and recyclability in carbon fiber‐reinforced epoxy composites (CFREs) remains a fundamental challenge in epoxy resin design. Herein, we introduce a topology engineering strategy based on an imide‐containing dual‐role hyperbranched platform, which acts simultaneously as reactive tougheners and interfacial coupling agents. Within the matrix, the hyperbranched architecture interpenetrates the linear epoxy network, forming a distinctive dual‐phase “penetration‐locking” topology that reduces free volume and increases effective cross‐link density. At the fiber‐matrix interface, thiol‐terminated hyperbranched molecules enable covalent interphase formation via thiol‐ene click chemistry, enhancing interfacial adhesion and stress transfer. This chemically integrated design enables cost‐effective T300‐based composites to reach a tensile strength of 740 MPa, comparable to conventional T800‐based composites, while T800‐based composites achieve up to 1.1 GPa. Importantly, the incorporation of imide and ester linkages introduces chemically addressable cleavage sites, enabling selective depolymerization under mild alkaline methanolysis, recovery of carbon fibers with retained integrity, and upcycling of oligomeric products as curing agents. This work establishes a molecular design framework that couples network topology, interfacial chemistry, and dynamic covalent functionality, providing a versatile platform for high‐performance thermoset composites with improved lifecycle sustainability.
n5c9079e0db6c: Interfacial assembly of ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) membranes remains a significant challenge. In this study, we report the fabrication of freestanding iCOF membranes by manipulating Hofmeister effect during interfacial polymerization (IP) process. Different kinds of inorganic salts are introduced into the aqueous phase to regulate the dissolution and crystallization dynamics of TpPa‐SO3H. We discover that Li2SO4 provides the optimal ion‐specific regulation by combining a strongly hydrated anion that effectively dehydrates the growing iCOF and a cation that interacts only weakly with the sulfonate framework, enabling TpPa‐SO3H to enrich and stay at the interface. This ion‐specific synergy facilitates the subsequent π–π stacking and ordered assembly into highly crystalline, intact freestanding membranes. The resulting membrane demonstrates a high proton conductivity of 334.7 mS cm−1 at 100°C and 98% RH.
n443f7c4a197f: Achieving triple‐fluorescence from a pure organic compound in solution is nearly impossible, as Kasha's rule only allows single fluorescence from the lowest excited state. In this paper, pyrene‐substituted o‐carboranes, 1a‐c, and 2a, were synthesized within 3–5 steps from commercially available chemicals, and their chemical structures have been confirmed by 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and HRMS. The photophysical properties of these compounds have been studied in detail by UV–vis, steady and transient state fluorescence, temperature‐dependent fluorescence, and femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, as well as TD‐DFT calculations. The results show that while 2a exhibits only local emission, the B,B‐dipyrenyl‐o‐carborane, 1a, shows dual‐emission from locally excited and intramolecular excimer states. Triple‐fluorescence is achieved for 1b and 1c by introducing a small π‐substituent at the carborane carbon vertices, which allows the formation of a charge‐transfer state that is fluorescent in the near‐infrared (NIR) region tailing to 1200 nm. This work provides a new strategy to activate triple‐fluorescence from a single‐component organic compound, opening a new avenue toward multichannel photonic materials and NIR‑II bioimaging.
n9c8bebcb6444: Molecular solar thermal (MOST) systems capable of harnessing sunlight, storing it as chemical energy in the form of a photoisomer, and releasing it as thermal energy on demand represent a promising strategy for renewable solar energy utilization both in liquid‐based devices and the solid state. However, the implementation of MOST materials in the solid state is limited by restricted molecular motion in the condensed phase, which hampers the geometrical requirements for photoisomerization, as well as by inner filter effects which can prevent quantitative photoconversion or necessitate long irradiation times. To address these challenges, three dianthrylnaphthalenes were designed to pre‐organize two anthracene moieties in a face‐to‐face geometry favorable for intramolecular photodimerization. This molecular design increased the forward photoisomerization quantum yield compared to ortho‐dianthrylbenzenes, reaching 32%, while enabling solid‐state switching. In particular, the acenaphthene‐linked derivative underwent quantitative conversion to its higher‐energy photoisomer in both thin films and bulk crystalline powders. Electron diffraction analysis revealed elongated newly formed C─C bonds in the photoisomer, with refined lengths of 1.81(2) and 1.63(2) Å, exceeding the generally observed length of a Csp3─Csp3 bond. These results demonstrate how molecular preorganization can overcome limitations of anthracene‐based MOST systems and expand their potential for solid‐state solar energy storage applications.
n0da1407de57b: Dynamic kinetic resolution (DKR) serves as a fundamental approach in asymmetric synthesis which enables the efficient conversion of racemic starting materials into a single stereoisomer, yet its extension to racemic diastereomers remains a formidable challenge, and reported DKR processes have largely been restricted to substrates bearing a single stereogenic element. Herein, we report an organocatalytic DKR with catalyst‐accelerated racemization and epimerization for the asymmetric construction of significant N–N axially chiral compounds through the merger of a reversible Pudovik addition with an irreversible, stereoselective phospha‐Brook rearrangement. Under bioinspired peptide‐phosphonium salt catalysis, a wide range of N–N axially chiral products were obtained in good yields and high enantioselectivities. Scale‐up synthesis and product derivatization further underscore the synthetic utility of this protocol. Mechanistic studies support a DKR process involving reversible racemization and epimerization through prochiral intermediates, identify the phospha‐Brook rearrangement as the stereodetermining step, and reveal key roles of hydrogen‐bonding and ion‐pairing interactions in catalyst‐controlled stereochemical induction. This work establishes a new paradigm for the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral molecules.
n5ba4b2ba0cc6: Alkali metal cations influence electrochemical interfaces, but their role in regulating urea electrosynthesis remains incompletely understood. Here, we combine constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), classical molecular dynamics (cMD), flow‐cell electrolysis, and in situ infrared spectroscopy to investigate how cations affect urea formation from CO2 and nitrate on Cu. Among Li+, Na+, K+, and Cs+, K+ affords the lowest calculated barrier for direct *CO–*NO coupling and the highest measured urea Faradaic efficiency. Varying the K+ concentration reveals a volcano‐shaped dependence of urea activity and selectivity, with a maximum at a partial current density of 13.62 mA cm−2 and Faradaic efficiency of 24.50% near 1.20 M K+. AIMD calculations identify a minimum coupling barrier at an intermediate nominal K+ concentration and elucidate how K+ concentration regulates precursor geometry and charge redistribution. Complementary cMD simulations reveal concentration‐dependent changes in interfacial reactant distributions and water structure, with infrared spectral features providing experimental evidence of changes in interfacial reaction chemistry. Together, these results establish an optimal K+ concentration window governed by the coupled roles of elementary‐step kinetics and electrolyte organization in urea electrosynthesis.
na0c0942bab36: High-entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) are promising electrocatalysts, yet their ultrasmall size makes them vulnerable to migration-induced coalescence (MIC), a sintering pathway that intrinsic high-entropy effects cannot suppress. Herein, we anchor ultrasmall PtPdIrRuCu HEA NPs on N, O-doped carbon cage fibers (NOCCFs). The N/O anchoring sites inhibit MIC through strong metal–support interactions, which, together with the intrinsic resistance of HEA to Ostwald ripening, synergistically suppress sintering. After 700 °C annealing, the PtPdIrRuCu NPs size increases from 2.8 nm to only 3.8 nm, whereas Pt/C aggregates from 2.3 nm to 21.8 nm. In ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs delivers a mass activity of 7.66 A·mgPt − 1 (7.3‑fold that of Pt/C) and a Faradaic efficiency of 95.8% toward glycolic acid (GA). A membrane electrode assembly (MEA) flow electrolyzer runs stably over 240 h with >90% GA selectivity. Mechanistic studies reveal that the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs enhances *OH adsorption to promote the GA pathway, accelerates COads oxidation via oxophilic Ir/Ru sites to prevent catalyst poisoning, and elevates both C–C cleavage and overoxidation barriers to suppress byproducts.
n2bbbf95bdf17: Chirality‐induced spin selectivity (CISS) has emerged as a frontier research direction in chiral recognition. The CANFs achieved a spin polarization efficiency of up to +94.17% ± 3.72%. Benefiting from their excellent electrical conductivity and spatial‐confinement‐enhanced signal amplification, the CANFs enable dual‐mode enantioselective recognition of kynurenine enantiomers, with a photo‐driven ionic‐current discrimination ratio as high as 10.3. The platform further exhibits outstanding analytical performance, including low limits of detection of 0.024 nM in the photo‐driven mode and 0.012 µM in the electrochemical mode, broad linear response ranges, and good applicability in complex clinical matrices. By integrating CISS‐mediated spin‐polarized transport with nanoconfinement‐enhanced signal transduction, this work establishes a versatile strategy for developing next‐generation real time, high‐performance chiral sensing platforms.
n3f45e905725a: Carbon‐centered radicals have progressively become indispensable tools in modern synthetic chemistry. Visible‐light photochemistry has emerged as a powerful platform for organic transformations, enabling the selective generation of radical species under remarkably mild and sustainable conditions. The controlled generation of unstabilized alkyl radicals, however, remains one of the most challenging and rapidly evolving frontiers in the field. In recent years, substantial efforts have been devoted to the development of novel radical precursors specifically designed to enable the efficient formation of these highly valuable intermediates under photoinduced conditions. This Minireview highlights recent advances in the design of unstabilized carbon‐centered radical precursors, systematically categorizing them according to their structural features. Particular attention is devoted to understanding how precursor design influences redox properties, bond fragmentation pathways, and so forth with the aim of laying the groundwork for the future design of increasingly efficient radical precursors and the discovery of new photochemical reactivity paradigms.
n8afc04c1b0b7: Dearomative hydrofunctionalization of indoles represents an appealing strategy to access C(sp3)‐rich indoline scaffolds for drug discovery; however, such transformations typically require activated substrates, leaving unactivated indoles largely unexplored. Herein, we report a photochemical radical carbonylative dearomatization of unactivated indoles under visible light irradiation. Central to this protocol is the interception of the highly reactive indolenium intermediate—generated in situ via acid‐mediated C3‐protonation—through the formation of an electron donor−acceptor (EDA) complex with 4‐alkyl‐1,4‐dihydropyridines (DHPs). This photoactive EDA complex initiates a mechanistically distinct radical pathway that effectively circumvents the detrimental dimerization typically plaguing indolenium intermediates. Subsequent radical carbonylation and radical cross‐coupling enable the carbonylative dearomatization of a broad range of indoles with diverse alkyl‐DHPs. The method exhibits excellent functional group tolerance and broad substrate scope, furnishing various 2‐acylindolines in generally good yields. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, including control experiments, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, and UV/vis absorption analyses, support a radical‐radical coupling mechanism as the key step in this transformation.
n767834797a36: The efficiency and stability of high‐performance organic solar cells (OSCs) are increasingly determined by the interfacial quality of self‐assembled monolayer (SAM)‐based hole‐selective layers. The strategy also shows broad applicability, enables 18.02% efficiency in 1 cm2 devices, and improves thermal and light stability. These results establish proton‐transfer‐coupled charge‐state regulation as an effective route to simultaneously control molecular assembly, SAM formation uniformity, and interfacial anchoring in phosphonic‐acid SAMs.

n80fcdd851a13: An atomically precise, ligand-capped Cu49 nanocluster is demonstrated to efficiently catalyze the semihydrogenation of alkynes at room temperature. Its unique surface coordination architecture governs substrate adsorption via steric effects; this structural feature, combined with the cluster’s remarkable stability, concurrently facilitates effective alkyne activation and ensures high hydrogenation selectivity. Notably, this work overcomes the conventional dependence on noble metals such as gold and palladium in hydrogenation catalysis, revealing the significant potential of ligand-protected copper nanoclusters for this transformation.
nb91102874037: While polyester waste represents a valuable carbon resource for chemical production, its upcycling typically involves multiple steps for polymer depolymerization, intermediate separation, and subsequent conversion. This work establishes a tandem catalytic method that integrates depolymerization and selective upcycling in a single process, which selectively converts diverse commercial polyesters and mixed waste streams into valuable dicarboxylic acids.
n9a1bfe755e63: This review summarizes the bioinspired design principles, core modules, assembly strategies, unique functions, advances, and bottlenecks of artificial photosynthetic cells, and outlines future opportunities for synthetic photobiological systems.
ne129cee4338d: This review summarizes molecular design strategies for shifting molecular motors from UV to visible and near-infrared operation, with emphasis on recent advances and emerging applications.
naffa31d5ae58: Branched quaternary ammonium chlorides were explored as low-chloride aqueous electrolytes for four-electron Zn–I 2 batteries. 3-Chloro-2-hydroxypropyl trimethylammonium chloride proved optimal for Ah-level pouch cells.

nb8b4a0dda82b: A membrane-defined N-polar InGaN/GaN quantum pyramid photocathode, encapsulated by a selective GO/PLA nano-membrane, enables catalyst-free, long-term stable hydrogen evolution directly in untreated natural seawater.
n7c477b3c2b75: Facing global freshwater scarcity and energy shortages, this work designs a flower-inspired 3D solar evaporator made from modified ramie yarns that simultaneously generates clean water and electricity. Its conical structure traps sunlight to drive rapid evaporation (1.77 kg m−2 h−1) and produce thermoelectric voltage (38 mV) while resisting salt crystallization even in high-salinity brine, offering a sustainable, off-grid solution for water-electricity cogeneration.
n056ae4039b79: High-entropy chalcogenides represent an emerging class of functional materials with immense potential in broad applications. To date, colloidal high-entropy nanocrystals (NCs) have predominantly been accessed via co-nucleation of precursors or simultaneous incorporation of multiple cations. While effective, these approaches lack a mechanistic understanding of NC synthesis. Here, we report the colloidal synthesis of high-entropy Cu–Zn–Sb–Ag–Bi–S NCs in the tetrahedrite phase, employing a sequential, low-temperature cation-exchange strategy, starting from a Cu–Zn–Sb–S tetrahedrite template. Subsequent sequential cation exchanges preserve the crystal phase while enabling precise control over morphology. This bottom-up approach circumvents the need for high-temperature synthesis, while allowing isolation and characterization of intermediate states, providing important mechanistic insight into the evolution of high-entropy NCs. The nanocrystals served as hydrogen evolution reaction electrocatalysts with less negative cathodic potentials. This work introduces the high-entropy tetrahedrite phase, paving the way for entropy-stabilized chalcogenides for energy conversion applications.
nb5b8266bf453: Transition metal dihalides are promising magnetic van der Waals materials because of their structural simplicity, chemical stability, and compatibility with nanofabrication. While magnetic order in these systems is typically associated with bulk-like monolayers, its relation to interfacial phases remains largely unexplored. Here we show that in CoBr2 grown on Au(111), long-range magnetic order already emerges in a structurally distinct interfacial precursor phase, prior to the formation of the bulk-like monolayer.
