During growth, this phase evolves into the monolayer, accompanied by a transition from molecular-like states to semiconducting behavior. Spin-resolved STM reveals an inhomogeneous in-plane magnetic response that is locally suppressed by point defects, whereas macroscopic XMCD demonstrates robust long-range order with pronounced in-plane anisotropy. These results establish that long-range magnetic order in CoBr2 does not require an ideal bulk-like monolayer but can emerge from interfacial phases with distinct electronic and structural properties, enabling magnetism beyond the monolayer limit.
nf891a8c7f84a: Hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) defects are promising building blocks for quantum photonics and sensing, yet their nonlinear optical signatures remain poorly understood. We use first-principles calculations to determine the polarization-resolved linear, second-order, and third-order susceptibilities of multilayer h-BN containing vacancies and carbon-based defect complexes. Defects weakly affect the linear response but strongly enhance nonlinear susceptibilities through symmetry breaking and resonant defect transitions. Carbon complexes produce orders-of-magnitude increases in second-harmonic generation and distinct polarization-dependent spectra that differentiate defects with identical composition but different geometry. Third-harmonic generation is also enhanced, although it is less sensitive to local structure. Measurements on carbon-doped h-BN qualitatively support these trends. These results establish nonlinear spectroscopy as a powerful probe of defect identity and geometry in h-BN and provide a route to defect-engineered nonlinear quantum photonics.
n495d2a1713d2: Multifocal phase holography offers a route to parallel femtosecond laser micro- and nanofabrication, but conventional weighted Gerchberg–Saxton (GSW) phase retrieval requires target-specific iterations and does not jointly optimize the optical quantities governing exposure quality. Here we introduce PhyFlow, a physics-consistent invertible flow model that generates phase-only multifocal holograms from target multifocal patterns in a single inverse pass. A multiscale invertible backbone learns target-to-phase correspondence, while differentiable Fourier optics constraints optimize diffraction efficiency, focal uniformity, and target-shape preservation. Across focal numbers and array scales, PhyFlow matches or surpasses GSW in energy concentration, focal balance, and shape fidelity while reducing per-hologram generation time by 98.8%. Optical-field measurements and femtosecond laser writing further show improved dot-area consistency, narrower line width distributions, and fewer nontarget written features. PhyFlow therefore connects rapid learned hologram generation with physically optimized fields and more uniform parallel fabrication.
n958f5dd3d88f: Chiral nanostructures have attracted considerable attention because of their strong interactions with circularly polarized light (CPL) and their various applications. Although various fabrication methods have been reported, photoelectrochemical approaches using CPL as the chiral source are attractive because of their simplicity, cost-effectiveness, and scalability. However, previous CPL-based methods have required two or more steps, including the preparation of anisotropic precursors. Here, we demonstrate a single-step method for the selective growth of chiral PbO2 nanostructures with handedness dictated by CPL at a chiral yield of 87%, by simply irradiating a transparent electrode with CPL, without using precursor nanoparticles. The obtained structures exhibit well-defined spiral morphologies and high chiroptical activity with maximum dissymmetry factors (g-factors) ranging from 0.006 to 0.010. This conceptual framework, involving symmetry breaking through random nucleation and Mie-resonance-mediated spiral growth under CPL, may be applicable to the template-free fabrication of various chiral nanomaterials.
nac7cf40e3af8: Au nanoparticles (NPs) are inherently thermally unstable at elevated temperatures because their large surface-to-volume ratio promotes melting, migration, and coalescence. Here, we demonstrate that silica (SiO2) nanoconfinement thermodynamically elevates the melting point (Tm) of Au NPs through confinement-induced compressive pressure. Atomic-resolution in situ heating scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) combined with local Fourier crystallinity mapping reveals that bare Au NPs lose crystallinity at 1,000 °C, whereas SiO2-encapsulated Au cores (Au@SiO2) remain crystalline. Accordingly, in situ heating TEM shows bare Au NPs progressively merge while Au@SiO2 remain structurally isolated. Temperature-dependent lattice-parameter measurements reveal significantly suppressed thermal expansion of confined Au cores, corresponding to an estimated compressive stress of 4–5 GPa. Finite-element simulations support this estimate, showing that SiO2 shell shrinkage generates several-GPa core pressure, with thicker shells producing higher pressure and greater Tm elevation. These findings establish nanoconfinement-induced pressure as a general thermomechanical strategy for stabilizing metallic NPs under extreme thermal environments.
n273ad8756d72: Magnesium, a promising alternative for sustainable nanophotonics, crystallizes in a hexagonal close-packed (HCP) system, unlike the face-centered cubic (FCC) structures of gold, silver, copper, and aluminum. We report the high-yield colloidal synthesis of an unexpected shape in an HCP system: cubes. Nanocubes with narrow size distributions were produced from colloidal reduction of a magnesium precursor in the presence of a sodium salt nucleating agent. Electron microscopy and diffraction reveal multiple twinning leading to the formation of six single-crystal units within the nanocubes. A self-limiting, sub-10 nm passivating oxide layer protects the metallic core against further oxidation in air and organic solvents. Strong, multimode plasmonic responses were observed using bulk extinction spectroscopy, single-particle scattering correlated with electron microscopy, and electron energy loss spectroscopy; experimental results were corroborated by numerical simulations. These findings expand the crystallographic boundaries of non-FCC plasmonics and establish magnesium nanocubes as versatile building blocks for nanophotonic applications.
nfc8cd9517c63: Altermagnets have recently gained attention for hosting symmetry-enforced spin-split bands despite zero net magnetization. Angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (ARPES) offers direct access to their electronic structure. However, the intrinsic surface sensitivity of this technique complicates the identification of the observed features: Surface states can be misinterpreted as the spin-split counterpart of bulk bands. This issue becomes particularly relevant for layered intercalated systems, where micrometer-sized domains with distinct terminations often coexist on a cleaved surface. We discuss this scenario for CoNb4Se8, one of the first established layered altermagnets. Supported by density functional theory calculations, we employ micro-ARPES to probe individual domains and reveal two contrasting surface terminations. We identify Co- and Se-terminated domains with characteristic surface states arising from bulk-surface connectivity of the material. Our work shows that termination-dependent surface contributions are essential for the reliable spectroscopic identification of altermagnetism and for assessing its presence across the family of layered materials.
n00630f7656ef: Charge-transfer doping provides a nondestructive route to tune two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), but selectively patterned n-type dopants effective across different TMD channels remain limited. Here, ultrathin bismuth oxide (BiOx) is used as an n-type charge-transfer doping and passivation layer for monolayer MoS2 and WSe2 transistors. In MoS2, 2 nm BiOx preserves the channel structure and yields a TLM-extracted effective contact resistance of 0.71 ± 0.06 kΩ·μm at n2D = 1.8 × 1013 cm–2. Thicker BiOx strengthens n-type modulation but reduces gate controllability. The modulation remains stable after ambient storage and air annealing. BiOx also enhances electron transport in WSe2 and enables homogeneous WSe2 inverters with MoOx-doped p-FETs, achieving a gain of ∼19 and a total normalized noise margin of 0.895 VDD at VDD = 2 V. These results establish BiOx as a cross-TMD n-type charge-transfer dopant for contact, threshold-voltage, and polarity engineering.
n79a1f2802c3b: A bioresorbable, metal-free molecular magnet for wireless deep-tissue sensing is reported that enables continuous cardiac monitoring and injectable organ tracking in vivo before the material safely degrades.
n8f0b777ffd55: Strong coupling between magnons and excitons in CrSBr enables microwave-to-optical transduction, offering a route towards efficient conversion between otherwise disparate frequency regimes.
n8662555b8320: Heteroleptic organosilanes with four different substituents are prepared by a selective and simple method based on the controlled monobromination of multihydrosilanes. This approach avoids the limitations of conventional methods, tolerates diverse functional groups and enables iterative access to highly substituted silanes in excellent yields.
n2f6e6b14dbd3: The stepwise installation of carbon substituents at silicon starting from tetrachlorosilane or tetraalkoxysilanes is burdened by chemoselectivity issues, typically affording product mixtures. Now, monoselective bromination of multihydrosilanes followed by nucleophilic displacement opens the door to the programmable and reliable synthesis of functionalized silicon building blocks.
n617dd9db8a0f: Advances in dynamic covalent chemistry have dramatically broadened its use in polymer research. Cyclic disulfide bonds are a widely used, versatile platform for engineering dynamic polymers. The resulting polymers leverage the dynamic character of exocyclic linkages associated with cyclic disulfide bonds, along with modular, tailorable chain-end functionalities to enable self-healing and chemical recycling. This review summarizes recent advances in dynamic polymer chemistry based on cyclic disulfide bonds that have enabled new design principles for the development and innovation in advanced polymers. We highlight living/controlled polymerization strategies for cyclic disulfide monomers, covering the principal polymerization strategies and mechanisms, and discuss the future challenges and prospective directions of the field in the context of emerging societal and technological demands.
ne513108215db: The discovery of new solid‐state ionic conductors remains challenging because ion transport depends sensitively on both mobile‐ion chemistry and the host crystal framework. Although atomistic calculations can evaluate migration barriers directly, simple descriptors can greatly facilitate screening large materials spaces and gaining mechanistic insight. However, existing descriptors often show limited transferability across mobile‐ion chemistries and material classes. Here, we generate a diverse dataset of ion‐migration barriers spanning Li‐, Na‐, K‐, and Mg‐ion conductors across oxides, sulfides, and halides, and use it to systematically benchmark descriptors. From this analysis, we devise distance contraction, ∆d, a simple local geometric descriptor that measures the largest contraction of mobile‐ion–neighbor distances relative to their equilibrium values along a migration pathway. This quantity captures the dominant short‐range repulsion penalty associated with ion migration and consistently distinguishes low‐ from high‐barrier pathways across chemistries. Using ∆d in a high‐throughput screening workflow, we recover many known fast‐ion conductors and identify previously unexplored candidates, with fast‐ion transport validated by nudged elastic band calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations. Beyond screening, ∆d links diverse ion‐transport mechanisms to a common physical quantity: The largest distance contraction experienced by the migrating ion.
nae7812b9cc52: Glutathione peroxidase (GPX)‐mimetic nanozymes are a promising strategy to restore redox homeostasis, but many existing systems rely on metals and remain limited by cytotoxicity, poor selectivity, and susceptibility to catalytic deactivation. Inspired by the active‐site chemistry of native GPX, we designed dichalcogenide‐hybrid mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) as inorganic–organic nanozymes with tunable sulfur and selenium environments. Structure–activity analysis showed that GPX‐like performance is governed by chalcogen composition, chalcogen density, and spatial proximity of S/Se within the framework, which together regulate reversible disulfide/diselenide redox cycling and substrate access. Among the materials tested, the diselenide–hybrid framework exhibited the highest activity, with improved selectivity and biocompatibility relative to the disulfide‐hybrid analogue, and conventional metal‐based GPX mimics. Mechanistic studies indicated efficient glutathione‐dependent detoxification of peroxides and lipid peroxides through catalytically active chalcogen intermediates. In vivo, the optimized diselenide‐hybrid material protected against acetaminophen‐induced and rifampicin‐induced liver injury, reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, restored antioxidant capacity, and improved survival. It also alleviated steatosis and metabolic dysfunction in metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) models. These findings establish dichalcogenide–hybrid frameworks as effective GPX‐like nanozymes and a promising platform for the treatment of oxidative stress‐associated liver diseases.
n37a06940a90a: As complementary metal‐oxide‐semiconductor (CMOS) technology scales down to the sub‐2 nm node, the dramatic surge in power density has emerged as a fundamental bottleneck. Conventional metal‐oxide‐semiconductor field‐effect transistors (MOSFETs) are constrained by the 60 mV/dec Boltzmann thermal limit, rendering further supply voltage reduction exceedingly challenging. To surmount this fundamental limit, various novel sub‐60 mV/dec steep‐switching devices have been proposed, including tunnel field‐effect transistors (TFETs), negative‐capacitance field‐effect transistors (NCFETs), and cold‐source field‐effect transistors (CSFETs). A comprehensive review of the evolution of sub‑60 mV/dec technologies is presented, with particular emphasis on the three mainstream approaches: TFETs, NCFETs, and CSFETs. The underlying physical principles, recent research advances, optimization strategies, and remaining challenges of these devices are thoroughly analyzed. Finally, prospective directions for future breakthroughs are discussed, encompassing novel materials exploration, the synergistic integration of multiple physical mechanisms, and the experimental verification of integration with advanced CMOS nodes.
n0702537f96da: The discovery that fundamental lattice vibrations can carry angular momentum allows non‐magnetic materials to exhibit properties that until now have only been observable in magnetic materials. However, the role of these specific vibrations, commonly known as chiral phonons, in driving ultrafast spin dynamics has not yet been explored experimentally. Here, using broadband terahertz emission spectroscopy, we demonstrate that the non‐magnetic ferroelectric In2Se3$\mathrm{In}_2\mathrm{Se}_3$ generates signals consistent with a ultrafast spin current after excitation with an ultrafast laser pulse, which we attribute to a chiral phonon–induced spin Seebeck effect. We suggest that the transient heating creates an non‐equilibrium phonon distribution, resulting in a net angular momentum and magnetization perpendicular to the thermal gradient, which is converted into a terahertz electromagnetic pulse via an inverse spin‐Hall effect in a thin metal overlayer. The emitted field reverses sign upon flipping the sample orientation or replacing Pt with W, consistent with spin‐current generation. Polarization‐resolved measurements reveal controllable terahertz ellipticity, indicating an additional polarization‐dependent ultrafast response. Our results establish chiral phonons as a route for generating ultrafast spin currents in non‐magnetic materials as well as providing a pathway toward terahertz sources with switchable handedness.
n48862fe201ad: In highly efficient organic solar cells, the optoelectronic properties of the non‐fullerene acceptor Y6 are governed by the molecular packing of noninteracting and interacting molecules. In this study, steady‐state and transient absorption spectroscopy are employed to disentangle the spectral signatures and excited‐state dynamics of interacting and noninteracting Y6 in solution and thin films. By controlling aggregation in dilute solution, we identify localized Frenkel‐type excitons (LE) on noninteracting Y6 and aggregate excitons (AE) on intermolecular interacting Y6. The AEs exhibit strongly fluence‐dependent lifetimes (30–200 ps) governed by singlet–singlet annihilation, whereas localized excitons decay monoexponentially on a nanosecond timescale. Furthermore, long‐lived polaronic states are observed to form on aggregated Y6 within tens of picoseconds and persist into the nanosecond regime. Comparison with thin‐film measurements reveals similar processes with an additional ultrafast energy transfer from noninteracting chromophores to aggregated domains. These results establish a consistent framework for assigning transient absorption features in Y6 and suggest that, in neat films of Y6, the pairwise formation of polarons arises from an Onsager‐like autoionization process of delocalized excitons in domains of interacting Y6 with moderate yield. This provides central insight into charge‐generation mechanisms in Y6‐based photovoltaic systems.
na43d7b463ecf: Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is a highly recalcitrant fluorinated polymer that is highly resistant to chemical degradation, making its sustainable recycling and upcycling challenging. Despite its widespread use as a binder in the lithium‐ion battery industry, effective strategies for converting PVDF waste into value‐added chemicals remain limited. To resolve this, Fe and Cu dual single atoms incorporated on a new two‐dimensional material nanosheets (In2P3S9 NSs/Fe‐Cu DSAs) were prepared as photocatalysts for direct raw PVDF plastic conversion to high‐value chemicals. The best‐performing photocatalyst (Fe1.0Cu0.5) achieves a total acetic/formic acid generation of ∼1351.8 µmol g−1. Various in situ characterizations such as atomic force microscopy‐kelvin probe force microscopy, x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) demonstrate superior electron extraction from In2P3S9 NSs to Fe and Cu DSAs, after which the electrons are subsequently scavenged by O2 under ambient conditions. Moreover, quenching experiments as well as in situ infrared spectroscopy, and in situ EPR reveal the vital impact of photoexcited electrons and hydroxyl radicals in PVDF upcycling into high‐value products. These findings highlight the significant potential of photocatalysis in transforming one of the most resistant plastic wastes (PVDF) into value‐added products, providing a sustainable remedy for plastic pollution crisis.
na9a3174fe404: The practical deployment of lithium (Li) metal batteries is hindered by not only cycle life but also calendar life. The poor calendar life stems from both the repeated reconstruction of the solid‐electrolyte interphase (SEI) during cycles and, particularly, the continuous growth of SEI during storage. Herein, a durable SEI with high mechanical stability against volume fluctuations and superior passivation capability to suppress electrolyte permeation is demonstrated by integrating inorganics and a cross‐linked polymer into the SEI. Concretely, a cross‐linked polymer with high modulus and low swelling is in‐situ incorporated among the inorganics of an anion‐derived SEI. The elastic modulus of the SEI is significantly increased from 1.63 to 4.37 GPa, and the compactness of the SEI is also improved to suppress electrolyte permeation. Consequently, the cycle life and calendar life of Li metal coin cells are extended by 73% (from 190 to 329 cycles) and 129% (from 1553 to 3561 h), respectively. Furthermore, a prototype pouch cell (506 Wh kg−1) undergoes 124 cycles. This work establishes an effective strategy that concurrently improves the mechanical and passivation performance of the SEI, tackling the critical challenge of calendar life in Li metal batteries.
n9c9bd97195ab: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have transformed RNA therapeutics through their high delivery efficiency, scalable manufacturing, and favorable safety profiles, as demonstrated by COVID‐19 mRNA vaccines and clinically approved small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics. However, extending RNA delivery beyond the liver to extrahepatic tissues, including the spleen, lungs, lymph nodes, brain, and tumors, remains challenging because of the intrinsic hepatotropism of conventional LNPs and their limited cell‐type specificity. Recent advances in lipid chemistry, particle engineering, surface functionalization, protein corona modulation, and route‐specific administration have enabled new strategies to redirect LNPs toward specific tissues and cell populations. This review systematically examines these approaches and highlights key determinants of LNP tropism, including formulation composition, surface properties, endogenous protein adsorption, and administration route. We further discuss the clinical translation of extrahepatic LNP delivery, covering clinically validated products, emerging therapeutic candidates, and gaps between preclinical models and human applications. Major challenges include cell‐resolved biodistribution, long‐term safety, repeated‐dose immunogenicity, cross‐study comparability, and standardized quantitative assessment. Finally, we explore how high‐throughput screening, machine learning, and data‐driven design can accelerate the rational optimization of next‐generation LNPs. These advances may facilitate precise tissue‐ and cell‐selective RNA delivery, expanding the therapeutic potential of RNA medicines beyond the liver.
n56015f46702a: Passive radiative cooling (PRC) technology with zero‐energy uptake is an efficient thermal management strategy for the development of sustainable society. Fabrication of PRC materials with intrinsic extensibility/dimensional stability and efficient healability that can adapt to irregular shapes with prolonged lifetime remains a significant challenge. The present study introduces a design principle for mechanically robust and healable PRC films based on a cross‐linked elastomeric network with combined physical interactions and dynamic covalent bonds, which can be readily modulated by inorganic coating and micro‐/nano‐porous hierarchical architectures while retaining extensibility and healability. Such thermosetting elastomeric PRC films are scalable with strong solar reflectance and long‐wave infrared emittance, realizing excellent cooling performance even after physical damage and healing process. It demonstrates excellent roof cooling ability in summer yet efficient ice‐sculpture preservation function in winter. The scalable synthesis of thermoset elastomeric PRC films opens up new pathways to realize flexible, stable and healable PRC materials, highly promising for practical applications.
nc28d0f2e7727: The anchoring group of self-assembled monolayer (SAM) hole-transporting materials dictates both substrate binding and interfacial passivation, serving as a key lever for high-performance perovskite photovoltaics. Herein, we report a novel SAM molecular material, denoted by XS21, engineered with a multidentate dipicolinic acid (DPA) anchoring core to address conventional adhesion and degradation limitations. From an experimental perspective, the DPA anchor is found to promote molecular chemisorption onto the substrate, potentially originating from the dual-action mechanism of pyridine–Ni coordination coupled with dicarboxylate-metal interaction. Furthermore, XS21 imparts both low acid-dissociation constants (K a) and superior ultraviolet (UV) photostability. Consequently, wide-bandgap (1.79 eV) perovskite solar cells containing XS21 deliver a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.54% with an exceptional open-circuit voltage of 1.372 V. Crucially, integrating XS21 into monolithic all-perovskite tandem solar cells yields a remarkable PCE of 29.62%, alongside an outstanding operational stability (retaining >90% of initial efficiency after 900 h of continuous operation). This work establishes multi-dentate pyridine-carboxylate anchoring as a vital paradigm for next-generation efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics.
n94bdb62805ad: Sodium–metal batteries (SMBs) exhibit high theoretical specific capacity and take advantage of sodium's natural abundance and low cost, showing great promise for broad next‐generation energy‐storage applications. In this review, we summarize the major practical bottlenecks restricting SMB development. The solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) serves as a key mediator to overcome these challenges, and its formation mechanisms are systematically outlined. We comprehensively review diverse electrolyte strategies, including solvent engineering, salt chemistry optimization, additive utilization, high‐concentration, localized high‐concentration, and weakly solvating electrolytes, for modulating Na+ transport and generating mechanically robust, ion‐conductive yet electronically insulating SEI layers. We further discuss advanced in‐situ/operando characterizations combined with multiscale computational modeling and machine‐learning techniques as powerful tools to decipher the dynamic evolution of sodium–metal interfaces. Particular focus is placed on the coupled effects of current density, temperature, electrolyte composition, interfacial layers on sodium nucleation, dendrite growth, dead‐sodium formation, and Coulombic efficiency (CE). Finally, future directions for SEI engineering have been outlook toward high‐performance, practical sodium–metal batteries.
n325862d3ba7d: Altermagnetism defies conventional classifications of collinear magnetic phases, combining compensated magnetization with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting. While altermagnetic band splitting has been established in three-dimensional compounds such as MnTe and CrSb, layered altermagnets remain far less explored spectroscopically. Here, combining termination-resolved micro-ARPES, fine photon-energy mapping, spin-ARPES, and density functional theory, we map the three-dimensional fermiology of the layered g-wave altermagnet CoNb4Se8${\rm CoNb}_4{\rm Se}_8$, obtained by ordered Co intercalation of 2H-NbSe2${\rm NbSe}_2$. We resolve the spin–split branches of the altermagnetic pairs directly in the raw photoemission spectra and, with spin-ARPES at these experimentally identified momenta, show the reversal of the spin polarization at opposite momenta and between two regions of the sample, consistent with opposite time-reversal domains, and its absence along the symmetry-protected nodal Γ$\Gamma$–K direction. We further report a weak low-temperature anomaly near T 0 ≈ 50–60 K, detected by magnetometry, temperature-dependent micro-ARPES, and ultrafast reflectivity, whose microscopic origin remains open. These results provide a momentum-resolved benchmark of the electronic structure of a layered altermagnet.
n21397002b415: Lyophilization offers an attractive route for ambient-temperature storage of biological systems by eliminating cold-chain dependence and suppressing solution-phase degradation. However, lyophilizing mammalian cells remains challenging due to their vulnerability to coupled stresses, including ice-induced mechanical injury and membrane destabilization during freezing and dehydration. In nature, stress-resistant plant cells survive extreme conditions through multifunctional cell walls. Inspired by their natural survival strategies, we engineer an artificial membrane armor (AMA) that enables efficient lyophilization of red blood cells (RBCs). This biomimetic AMA integrates a nanoporous zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF-8) for mechanical support, a water-retentive polymer matrix for hydration retention and colloidal stabilization, and Zn2 + coordination preserves membrane fluidity and suppresses freeze- and dehydration-driven membrane phase transitions. Through synergistic interfacial protection, the AMA effectively buffers coupled stresses associated with lyophilization, enabling ∼95% post-rehydration recovery of RBCs using an ultra-low protectant content (<5 wt%) together with an ambient shelf-life of at least 3 months, unachievable with previous methods. Furthermore, the rehydrated RBCs preserve their native morphology, membrane mechanics, metabolic activity, oxygen transport capability, and in vivo circulation behavior. This work establishes a bioinspired interfacial engineering strategy for transferring desiccation tolerance from plants to mammalian cells, advancing ambient-temperature biostorage of sensitive living systems.
nb764427468d0: Intercalation‐type metal oxides are promising anodes for fast‐charging sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, viable electrode candidates remain scarce, constituting a major bottleneck and motivating intensive research into diverse structural frameworks. Here, we report a synchronic multilevel assembly strategy for synthesizing mesoporous intercalation‐type metal oxide framework anodes. Atomic‐scale assembly of cations, combined with in situ formation of conductive carbon networks, enables the synthesis of structurally tunable nanosized sodium titanate and overcomes the challenges of preparing multimetal oxide nanocrystals under high temperatures. The M‐Na4Ti5O12/C composite delivers superior rate capability (∼115 mAh g−1 at 10 A g−1) and cycling stability (<0.023% capacity fade per cycle over 1000 cycles at 0.2 A g−1) for sodium storage. Its outstanding kinetics arise from ultrafast Na+ diffusion through interconnected mesoporous channels and low‐barrier, nanoscale ion‐conduction pathways. A pouch cell delivers a power density of ∼4.7 kW kg−1 and cycles stably for 1200 cycles, outperforming hard carbon at high rates. This work establishes a rational design framework for developing high‐rate battery materials.
nb67843be428e: The limited exposure of active sites and moderate intrinsic activity of conventional NiFe layered double hydroxides (LDHs) remain major obstacles for their application in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Here,...
nc5a607337783: Rational molecular engineering of the perovskite/hole transport layer interface offers a promising route to simultaneously address inefficient charge extraction, defect-mediated recombination, and lead leakage in CsPbI3–xBrx perovskite solar cells. Herein, we introduce 2,2′-dinitro-9,9′-spirobifluorene (DN-SBF) as an interfacial molecular bridge to tackle these challenges. DN-SBF optimizes energy level alignment, establishes π–π interactions, and forms exciplexes with Spiro-OMeTAD, thereby facilitating interfacial charge transport. Meanwhile, DN-SBF passivates undercoordinated Pb2+ through multiple coordination modes, including robust bidentate chelation formed by adjacent nitro groups, effectively passivating defects and suppressing non-radiative recombination. Importantly, multipoint coordination immobilizes leachable Pb2+, substantially mitigating lead leakage and improving film biocompatibility. As a result, DN-SBF-engineered CsPbI3–xBrx devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 22.40% along with significantly enhanced operational and environmental stability. This work highlights the potential of versatile molecular bridges to concurrently enhance performance, stability, and eco-friendliness, which may contribute to the development of more sustainable perovskite photovoltaics.
n246b6f2bc25e: The vertical integration of heterogeneous dies in three-dimensional integrated circuits demands materials with extreme thermal anisotropy to dissipate heat in-plane while suppressing cross-plane leakage. Randomly twisted van der Waals stacks can enhance anisotropy, but their stochastic nature lacks precise control. Here, we report flipping engineering in Janus MoSSe stacks, exploiting the intrinsic asymmetry between the S–Mo–Se and Se–Mo–S terminations as a programmable structural degree of freedom orthogonal to twisting. By integrating machine-learned potential molecular dynamics with Bayesian optimization for a 14-layer MoSSe stack, we identify a structure with strongly suppressed effective cross-plane thermal conductivity of 0.082 ± 0.002 W m–1 K–1 at 300 K while maintaining robust in-plane conduction, yielding an anisotropy ratio of about 760 and 35% higher than the crystalline reference. This effect arises from flipping-induced breaking of stacking periodicity, which perturbs midfrequency phonons (2–8 THz) and leads to band splitting and nearly flat, layer-localized modes. These changes reduce the cross-plane propagating channels and thus weaken their contribution to thermal transport, while their impact on in-plane transport dominated by low-frequency acoustic phonons is negligible. Flipping engineering thus provides programmable stacking-sequence strategy and a versatile route for designing anisotropic properties in layered materials.
n9d9b0283c1f2: The literature on graphene oxide (GO) comprises hundreds of thousands of publications spanning synthesis, characterization, and applications in diverse domains. Advancing GO materials requires a structured knowledge map derived from systematic mining of this extensive corpus. However, extracting meaningful insights from this vast, heterogeneous, sparse, and unstructured data remains a challenge. To address this challenge, Natural Language Processing techniques, including topic modeling, community discovery, and parameter extraction, are here employed to establish a framework. Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) was applied to the full text of more than 120,000 articles, enabling the identification of eight macro-domains within the GO literature, and neural topic modeling was subsequently employed to characterize the granularity and heterogeneity of these domains. Parameter extraction was performed using Large Language Models (LLMs) on a subset of 8000 full-text articles, with a proto-ontology incorporated into the extraction prompt. Even with a broad prompt, an F1 score of 94% was achieved against manual validation. The extracted parameters were then clustered through community modeling and compared with the LDA-derived topics. At this intermediate resolution of the literature, we demonstrate the application of a recommendation system for relevant parameters according to the material family and application domain. The applicability of the framework at higher resolutions was further demonstrated through the construction of a data set of CO2 adsorption for graphene- and GO-based materials. This data set was subsequently employed in a downstream predictive case study using an Extremely Randomized Trees Regressor, with different training-test splitting strategies evaluated to assess in-domain and out-of-domain generalization at article-level resolution.
nbaa1db6d3112: Polysaccharides in nature possess profound biological significance, and their structural complexity renders them of great research value. However, the structural heterogeneity of complex polysaccharides has long posed a great challenge for analysis. Here, a nanopore profiling strategy was developed for polysaccharide characterization. Experimentally, polysaccharides are hydrolyzed into informative fragments, and the distribution of their resulting nanopore events forms a unique profile that serves as a reliable molecular signature. Seven distinct polysaccharides, including xanthan gum, gum arabic, agarose, sodium alginate, gellan gum, heparin, and chondroitin sulfate A, were successfully identified and discriminated. A profile-based machine learning classifier was also developed, which utilizes the overall distribution profile of fragment events as training input, yielding 100% validation accuracy. Further application of the fully constrained least-squares (FCLS) algorithm enabled accurate quantification of polysaccharide mixture composition, allowing for unambiguous analysis of mixtures of polysaccharides in the same assay. Collectively, this work establishes a universal, label-free, and high-resolution framework for decoding the structural complexity of polysaccharides.
n049029ae9640: Understanding the formation, transformation, and stabilization of metastable polymorphs in functional compounds is a central challenge in materials science and has a profound impact on phase engineering and property control. Ga2O3 is an ultrawide bandgap semiconductor whose rich polymorphism underpins diverse electronic and optoelectronic functionalities, motivating continued exploration of its metastable phases. Among the known Ga2O3 polymorphs, the P1̅-phase has been predicted to have the closest energy to the thermodynamically stable β-phase; however, its existence has not been definitively identified experimentally, and feasible preparation routes remain unclear up to now. Here, combining large-scale molecular dynamics simulations with a high-accuracy machine learning potential, we reveal a reversible strain-induced ferroelastic β–P1̅ phase transition in Ga2O3 and further investigate the origin of instability of P1̅-Ga2O3. Our work not only explains the absence of experimental observations of P1̅-Ga2O3 from the perspectives of mechanical stability and crystallization kinetics but also extends the application of strain engineering in phase transitions of wide-bandgap semiconductor single-crystal materials.
nfd447e35b277: Organic mixed ionic‐electronic conductors (OMIECs) with exclusive electrochemical modulation and coupling between ions and electrons have exhibited intriguing efficiencies in bioelectronics, logic circuits, and wearable devices. However, OMIECs are typically linear polymers whose excessive structural swelling and morphological disorder during electrochemical doping led to low performance and instability. Here, we report n‐type 2D covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) as novel OMIECs (BTID‐BFDO COF and BTDD‐BFDO COF). The rigid π‐conjugated scaffold functions as both a charge transport pathway and an ion‐electron coupling plane, whilst the nanochannels serve as directional conduits for rapid ion transport. 2D OMIECs‐based OECTs exhibit favorable threshold voltages (< 0.5 V), Ion/Ioff ratios (103) and high stability (modulation current retention rate of 91.3% during continuous operation) compared with the linear counterpart (< 10%). More importantly, we elucidate the mechanism underlying in situ ion transport and doping within the rigid porous architectures of 2D OMIECs, establishing a novel design paradigm for robust n‐type organic semiconductors.
nab876de7f754: Overcoming the intrinsic trade‐off between high‐voltage compatibility, thermal stability, and low‐temperature ionic conductivity in halide solid electrolytes remains a critical challenge for advancing all‐solid‐state lithium batteries (ASSLBs). Here, we propose a chemical symbiosis strategy to design a dual‐phase halide electrolyte integrating nanocrystalline LiAlCl4 with amorphous Li‐M‐O‐Cl (M = Ta/Al) phases. This innovative architecture synergistically combines the ultra‐high‐voltage stability (up to 4.8 V) of the crystalline phase with the low‐energy‐barrier ion transport pathways in the amorphous matrix. The designed electrolyte exhibits exceptional electrochemical performance under extreme conditions. It enables the ASSLBs to achieve a 90.5% capacity retention after 100 cycles at 4.8 V, maintain a specific capacity of 133 mA h g−1 over 500 cycles at 55 °C and 3 C, and deliver unprecedented low‐temperature performance with a capacity of 109.6 mA h g−1 and 1800‐h stability under dual extreme conditions of −60°C and 4.8 V. Comprehensive characterization reveals the amorphous phase facilitates facile percolation networks for rapid Li+ conduction, while the nanocrystalline domains maintain structural integrity against high‐voltage degradation. The electrolyte's broad compatibility with diverse cathodes (LiCoO2, LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2) also underscores its versatility for high‐energy ASSLBs.
n643af68f4110: Achieving industrially relevant electrochemical CO2 reduction (CO2RR) to formic acid requires catalyst that simultaneously exhibits high intrinsic activity and surface hydrophobicity. However, high intrinsic activity is considered thermodynamically contradictory on a hydrophobic surface since high hydrophobicity corresponds to low surface energy, thereby leading to low intrinsic activity. Here we overcome this hydrophobicity‐activity trade‐off via a bidentate chelation strategy that grafts carboxylic acid molecules with tunable alkyl chain lengths on Bi2O2CO3 (XC‐BOC, where X denotes the carbon number). The obtained 10C‐BOC sustains high hydrophobicity without sacrificing activity. This hydrophobicity‐activity balance is achieved by restructuring the interfacial hydrogen‐bond (HB) network to suppress the undesired hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and ensure the timely hydrogenation rate for the key *OCHO intermediate, in conjunction with modulating the Bi site electronic structure via the carboxyl‐O/Bi bidentate chelation to guarantee the high intrinsic activity. Consequently, 10C‐BOC achieves ampere‐level performance with FEHCOO‐ > 90% from 100–1000 mA cm−2, with an optimal FEHCOO‐ of 97.7% at 600 mA cm−2 (vs. 83.2% for bare BOC), and maintains FEHCOO‐ > 93% at 200 mA cm−2 for 200 h. This work offers a general strategy to decouple hydrophobicity from intrinsic activity for advanced CO2RR electrocatalysts.
nb4181ae30f48: Alkali‐metal fluorides enable robust solid‐electrolyte interphases (SEIs) in metal batteries owing to their wide electrochemical stability windows and high mechanical stiffness. However, the complexity and dynamic behavior of SEIs have long hindered direct, chemically resolved visualization of fluoride‐rich domains, which is essential for decoding inorganic interphase dynamics and guiding rational battery formation. Here, tetrakis(4‐carboxyphenyl)ethylene (H4TCPE) is used as a fluorescent probe for convenient, semi‐quantitative visualization of alkali‐metal fluoride‐rich interphases, enabled by a crystalline‐lattice‐specific matrix coordination‐induced emission effect mechanism. Under this mechanism, crystalline NaF exclusively activates H4TCPE fluorescence through strong hydrogen‐bonding and coordination interactions that lock the probe's rotation, whereas the probe remains non‐emissive on other SEI components because these phases fail to impose sufficient steric confinement. This chemical contrast enables ex situ and operando imaging and reveals an unexpected formation–breakdown–regeneration lifecycle of the NaF‐rich framework during cycling. This probe‐enabled semi‐quantitative tracking further identifies 1.0 mA cm−2 as the optimal formation current density, yielding the most continuous NaF‐rich framework, minimizing capacity loss, and ensuring stable cycling. Ultimately, this accessible, chemically selective optical strategy opens new avenues for probing fragile battery interphases and tailoring electrochemical protocols for high‐performance energy storage.
ne75692b72dfd: Efficient separation of xylene isomers remains a significant challenge due to their nearly identical physicochemical properties. Here, we report a dual locking strategy in an aluminum–pyrrolic framework (Al‐PyDC) with V‐shaped ligand featured AlO6 chains and pyrrole dual recognition sites that simultaneously stabilize the V‐shaped meta‐xylene (mX). This dual‐locking effect promotes dense packing of mX within confined channels, resulting in a high adsorption capacity for mX (4.0 mmol g−1), which is much higher than that for ortho‐xylene (oX, 2.5 mmol g−1) and para‐xylene (pX, 2.0 mmol g−1). The simulations and solid‐state NMR spectroscopy further confirmed that mX experienced stronger locking interactions with the AlO6 chains and pyrrolic ligands compared to pX. Notably, the dual locking effect was temperature‐dependent, and elevated temperature accelerated molecular diffusion, thereby weakening the effectiveness of the recognition. Hence, Al‐PyDC achieved an excellent mX/pX selectivity of 8.0 in vapor‐phase breakthrough measurements at ambient temperature (303 K), which outperformed most of the MOF counterparts. Additionally, the isomorphic CAU‐10‐H with V‐shaped AlO6–phenyl–AlO6 dual locking sites was employed as a control material to elucidate the role of active‐site in molecular recognition. This dual locking strategy offered an effective approach for enhancing the adsorption capacity and selectivity for challenging isomer separations.
n1257d33b1ad5: Birefringence, the optical property enabling materials to split light based on polarization and propagation direction, is crucial for many technological fields, spanning from telecommunications to imaging and photonics. Particularly, controlling the birefringence is vital in high‐performance applications such as nonlinear optics, adaptable spectroscopy filters, adaptive imaging, for biomedical, and space applications. Most known switchable birefringent materials suffer from either low birefringence values or narrow tuneable values, thus hindering their use in dynamic optical systems. Here, a novel approach based on a dynamic hydrogen‐bonded organic framework (HOF) capable of reversible single crystal to single crystal transformation, during guest molecule inclusion is reported. Changes in the planar conformation of the π–π stacking between layers during guest inclusion drastically alters the birefringence off–on, from negligible values to 0.73, surpassing all known switchable materials. This approach represents a novel platform for the development of high‐performance optical devices.
nf4b9543ca0e2: Hydrogen‐bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) offer versatile porous architectures, yet predictable pore expansion via tecton extension remains challenging because framework assembly is highly sensitive to solvent‐mediated crystallization. Here, we establish a mechanosynthesis‐enabled modular tecton matrix for constructing large‐pore HOFs. Pairwise combination of complementary tectons systematically generates four micro‐ and mesoporous HOFs, including G4, which is difficult to obtain by solution crystallization. These HOFs exhibit surface areas up to 1824 m2/g, pore apertures up to 2.4 nm, with record CO2 and C2H2 adsorption capacities for HOFs at 195 K. One‐pot incorporation of AgOTf during mechanosynthesis enables programmable pore decoration, enhancing room‐temperature C2H2 uptake through stronger framework‐substrate interactions. This work establishes a modular tecton matrix enabled by mechanosynthesis as a general design and discovery strategy for constructing and functionalizing large‐pore HOFs.
n72d32e661b0d: Li─O2 batteries (LOBs) offer an ultrahigh theoretical energy density but suffer from a large overpotential. Photocathodes can lower this overpotential, but most of them cannot achieve efficient charge separation, sufficient redox capability, and broadband photoresponse at the same time. Here, a plasmonic S‐scheme heterojunction photocathode (W18O49/g‐C3N4, WOCN) is constructed. W18O49 serves as the oxidation semiconductor of the heterojunction and a noble‐metal‐free plasmonic absorber, forming a continuous plasmonic heterointerface with g‐C3N4. The intrinsic localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) of W18O49 originates from periodically arranged lattice‐localized electrons in W5+ clusters. Photogenerated carriers with strong redox capability and LSPR‐generated hot electrons are separated by the S‐scheme carrier transfer pathway. Under AM 1.5G illumination, the WOCN‐based LOBs exhibit an ultralow overpotential of 0.04 V and a round‐trip efficiency of 98.75%. Even under NIR illumination, an overpotential of 0.34 V and a round‐trip efficiency of 90.12% are achieved, demonstrating an effective NIR response in photo‐assisted LOBs for the first time. This work opens a new avenue for designing plasmonic S‐scheme heterojunctions toward next‐generation energy storage systems with full solar spectrum utilization.
nca525101dd78: Rapid detection of toxic trace contaminants is critical for global water security, yet routine monitoring relies on costly, time-consuming laboratory analyses. Microbial sensors offer a promising alternative but suffer from limited specificity, insufficient stability, and slow kinetics. Herein, we report a programmable and printable microbial bioelectronic sensor that overcomes these bottlenecks through multi-scale chemical design. Using 2,4-dinitrotoluene as a model pollutant, we genetically reprogrammed the extracellular electron transfer pathway of Shewanella oneidensis by coupling specific pollutant recognition to inner-membrane cytochrome expression, thereby enabling highly specific bioelectrical detection of target pollutants. For robust deployment, these sensing microbes were encapsulated into a dual-network hydrogel sustained by reversible hydrogen bonding, ensuring structural resilience and biocompatibility. By 3D-printing the biosensor into a biomimetic fractal architecture, we minimized mass transport resistance, achieving a response time of 5 min, a 24-fold acceleration over conventional counterparts. The biosensor also exhibited a low detection limit of 6.75 µg L−1 and a broad dynamic range from 20.4 to 700.0 µg L−1 (R 2 > 0.999). Crucially, the biosensor maintained high accuracy (relative error < 4.2%) in actual wastewaters. This work establishes that the multiscale chemical design of microbial bioelectronic sensors enables real-time, targeted pollutant monitoring.
ned321d7fa465: Solar-driven CO2 reduction offers a route to sustainable carbon recycling, and polymeric carbon nitride (CN) has emerged as a leading photocatalyst for this reaction due to its metal-free composition, and...
ned9501745b95: Transition metal fluorides (TMFs) are promising conversion-type cathode materials for high-energy lithium–metal batteries owing to their exceptionally high theoretical energy density, making them attractive for demanding applications such as electric aviation. However, their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish conversion kinetics, pronounced voltage hysteresis, and poor electrochemical reversibility. Understanding the structural and chemical evolution of TMFs and the electrode–electrolyte interphase formed during cycling is essential for improving their performance. Monodisperse nanocrystalline TMFs are ideal model systems for high-resolution transmission electron microscopy because their uniform size, morphology, and electron transparency enable representative nanoscale characterization. Here, we investigate a reproducible colloidal synthesis of monodisperse, single-crystalline CoF2 nanorods and elucidate the mechanisms governing their formation to achieve precise control over particle size and aspect ratio. By independently varying reaction time, temperature, precursor composition, and ligand chemistry, we identify the key factors controlling precursor decomposition, burst nucleation, phase selection, and anisotropic crystal growth. These insights provide a transferable framework for the controlled synthesis of a broad range of transition metal fluoride nanocrystals.
n8e5d09d9c91c: Activating the exceptionally strong N≡N bond remains a fundamental challenge due to the chemical inertness of molecular nitrogen (N2). Plasmonic nanoclusters offer a promising approach by generating localized electromagnetic fields and energetic hot carriers that can drive bond activation under ambient conditions. Here, we combine real-time time-dependent density functional theory with Ehrenfest molecular dynamics to reveal how plasmonic coupling between tetrahedral Ag20 nanoclusters governs N2 activation and dissociation. Systematic variation of the intercluster separation shows that a 6 Å nanogap maximizes near-field enhancement and hot-electron transfer to the adsorbed N2, accompanied by N–N activation. Consequently, N2 dissociation is achieved at incident field strengths as low as 0.5 V Å–1, whereas larger-gap dimers exhibit substantially lower activity. Similarly, isolated N2 remains intact under comparable conditions. These findings establish nanogap engineering as an effective strategy for optimizing plasmon-driven N2 activation and provide design principles for developing efficient plasmonic catalysts.
n80308568dfd5: Solution-processable quantum dot (QD) lasers are essential for next-generation integrated photonic circuits, ranging, and optical sensing. However, their practical deployment remains hampered by high lasing thresholds. Here, we report AgAuSe QD lasing with a record-low threshold of 0.01 μJ cm–2 at 900 nm, representing a reduction of more than 4 orders of magnitude compared to those of previous near-infrared (NIR) QD lasing reports. This achievement is enabled by a well-designed twisted-lattice photonic crystal (PhC) nanocavity delivering extreme light confinement with an ultrahigh quality (Q) factor. The extended photon lifetime reduces the required gain volume, enabling lasing from a single-layer self-assembled QD superlattice (SL), which minimizes scattering losses. Crucially, the robust system allows us to push the operational regime to quasi-continuous-wave (q-CW) lasing at room temperature. These results establish a new benchmark for solution-processed NIR QD sources and provide a technologically viable pathway for sustained CW operation.
n9d636f098eaa: Despite their potential as building blocks of allenes, alkynylogous enol silanes have rarely been employed in organic synthesis. Herein, we establish their utility as nucleophiles in catalytic asymmetric allylic substitution, which results in skipped enallenes bearing two vicinal stereogenic elements (axial and central chirality). This iridium-catalyzed reaction utilizes α-alkynyl silyl enol ethers as alkynylogous nucleophile for reaction with easily accessible racemic branched allylic alcohols and endows tetrasubstituted axially chiral allenones, bearing a δ-stereocenter exclusively as a single regioisomer in moderate to good diastereoselectivity (up to 11:1 dr) and in most cases with high enantioselectivity (up to >99.5:0.5 er). The densely functionalized γ-allylic allenones can be elaborated into useful building blocks, including a highly substituted chiral 2-allyl furan derivative. Through this work, α-alkynyl enol silanes are introduced as alkynylogous nucleophiles in transition metal catalysis.
n2765627ad6ec: The narrow amine donor scope of imine reductases (IREDs) limits their application in the synthesis of opine compounds. Herein, we report a machine learning (ML)-guided protein engineering strategy to address this limitation. An IRED from an unclassified Ensifer, IRED5, was identified through deep-learning-based screening for its strict enantioselectivity toward methyl glycinate. Subsequent engineering using a few-shot learning for protein fitness prediction approach yielded the M178T/A208L/P241V/A36E/S67Q/Q187N (M6) variant with six mutations across the active site and protein surface. Kinetic analysis showed 156-fold toward methyl pyruvate and 72-fold improvements toward methyl glycinate in catalytic efficiency, respectively, over the wild-type (WT) enzyme. M6 accepted diverse keto esters and amino acid esters, enabling stereoselective formation of opine derivatives bearing two stereocenters. Structural and computational analyses revealed the molecular basis for activity enhancement. In preparative synthesis, M6 achieved complete conversion at a 3 M substrate loading, corresponding to a space time yield of 366 g·L–1·d–1. At a 4 M substrate loading, conversion remained high at 95.4% with a space time yield of 525 g·L–1·d–1, affording 10.5 g of enantiopure methyl N-(2-methoxy-2-oxoethyl)-d-alaninate (1a) in 75.0% isolated yield with > 99.9% ee. This work establishes an efficient biocatalytic route to opine compounds and demonstrates the utility of ML-guided enzyme engineering in expanding IRED synthetic capability.
n1b2f50547d9f: The heterogeneous hydrogenation of aromatic compounds using supported metal catalysts is an efficient strategy to increase the three-dimensionality and molecular complexity of organic molecules. However, most heterogeneous hydrogenation methods lack stereoselectivity or rely upon the steric properties of the substrate for stereocontrol, which limit their predictability and generality for pharmaceutical synthesis applications. In this work, we develop two synthetic methods for the amine- and hydroxyl-directed hydrogenation of benzofused arenes using Rh/C and Pt3Cu/SiO2 as heterogeneous catalysts, respectively. Mechanistic studies on the amine-directed reaction reveal that simultaneous adsorption of the amine and benzene functional groups to the Rh metal surface is extremely strong, outcompeting the adsorption of the benzene or amine individually and enabling good turnover and high diastereoselectivity toward the amine-directed product. A broad scope of benzofused scaffolds are effective substrates, generating up to four stereocenters in a single step. The utility of the method is demonstrated in the synthesis of a pyridine bisoxazoline compound derived from perhydro-cis-aminoindanol.
n37a94272487d: Water oxidation in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) uses IrO2 nanoparticles supported on corrosion-resistant TiO2. However, the low conductivity of TiO2 imposes electronic transport limitations that necessitate high Ir loadings for effective catalysis. Here, we present a catalyst design strategy that couples a heavily V-doped TiO2 support with high-density Ir single atoms, enabling water oxidation at minimal Ir loading. In this design, Ti-site-substituted V provides n-type doping, and selective V leaching creates cation vacancies that anchor Ir as isolated atoms. TEM with convolutional neural network (CNN)-based analysis shows Ir single-atom density increases with V content, accompanied by lower charge-transfer resistance and higher Ir-specific activity. The density functional theory indicates that cation-site Ir introduces a midgap state below V 3d levels and shifts neighboring V 3d orbitals toward the Fermi level. Ir1/V-TiO2 achieves 1480 A gIr–1 at 1.55 V vs RHE (1.3 wt % Ir) and demonstrates device-level PEMWE operation at an Ir loading as low as 0.027 mgIr cm–2.
nc350d618c723: The reductive dispersion of metal oxides into isolated cationic species in zeolites is an important strategy for generating well-defined catalytic sites, yet its kinetics and molecular mechanism remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate the H2-induced redispersion of In2O3 physically mixed with H-CHA using in situ/operando UV–vis spectroscopy, In K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES), SEM-EDS mapping, modulation-excitation spectroscopy, H2-TPR, XRF, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Time-resolved UV–vis spectroscopy quantitatively tracks the consumption of bulk-like In2O3 under H2 and reveals that the redispersion rate depends on temperature, H2 concentration, In2O3 precursor properties, and zeolite framework. Higher temperatures and H2 concentrations accelerate the process, with the highest reliable initial rate observed at 600 °C under 10% H2. In K-edge XANES indicates selective formation of reduced In species assigned to framework-stabilized In+ rather than metallic In0, demonstrating a partial-reduction pathway in CHA. H2-TPR provides quantitative redox evidence consistent with reductive solid-state ion exchange and reversible reduction of isolated oxygen-containing In species. SEM–EDS mapping shows the disappearance of surface In-rich domains after H2 treatment, consistent with indium redistribution, while XANES provides bulk-sensitive evidence for formation of reduced In species. Operando redox-cycling experiments reveal reversible interconversion between In(I) and oxygen-containing In(III) species under H2/O2 switching. DFT calculations using representative 1Al and 2Al CHA models suggest that local Al environments can influence the relative stability of framework-bound reduced In(I) and oxygen/hydroxyl-containing In(III)-type species. Together, these results support a two-step mechanism in which bulk In2O3 is first reduced to mobile In+ species and then anchored at acid sites within the zeolite framework. This work provides mechanistic insight into reductive redispersion and offers design principles for regenerable indium-based zeolite catalysts.
neb2ff219589e: The selective hydrodeoxygenation of lignin as a substitute for fossil resources into aviation fuel-range cycloalkanes faces significant challenges due to its complex structure and diverse reaction pathways. Herein, we introduced MoOx species onto Ni nanoparticles-loaded Beta zeolite (Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta), which catalyzed the complete hydrodeoxygenation of lignin dimers and lignin-derived phenols into the corresponding cycloalkanes under mild conditions (200 °C, 2 MPa H2). Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta also enabled the hydrodeoxygenation of real lignin, achieving a cycloalkanes selectivity of over 83%. Mechanistic studies indicated that the synergistic effect between Ni nanoparticles and MoOx species was key to enhancing the hydrodeoxygenation performance. Ni nanoparticles enabled the adsorption and dissociation of H2, and horizontally adsorbed benzene ring in the oxygen-containing substrate, while adjacent MoOx species with abundant oxygen vacancies facilitated the vertical adsorption of oxygen-containing groups in the ring-saturated intermediates and the activation of C–O bonds. Simultaneously, the strong hydrogen spillover on Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta ensured the benzene ring hydrogenation and the cleavage of C–O bonds. This work provides an approach for designing non-noble metal catalysts for lignin hydrodeoxygenation, holding significant value for advancing the application of lignin-based aviation fuels.
n4598f3ccb9e9: In anode-free Li metal batteries, a bare current collector must be converted into a reversible Li metal anode during the first charge, making Li nucleation decisive for reversibility. However, how current collector microstructure governs Li nucleation and growth remains poorly understood, since prior studies focused on single-crystal surfaces to identify favorable crystallographic orientations, leaving grain boundaries unexplored. Here, we identify grain boundary density and character in copper current collectors as key regulators of Li deposition uniformity. Systematic annealing decouples grain size from surface chemistry, revealing that deposition uniformity improves with copper grain coarsening but saturates as disordered boundaries are eliminated during grain growth, leaving predominantly low-energy configurations. Atomistic simulations show disordered boundaries impose high barriers to Li adatom migration, whereas ordered boundaries and adjacent low-index terraces provide low-barrier pathways for redistribution. Copper foils engineered beyond this threshold sustain uniform Li plating across diverse electrolytes and improve cyclability in anode-free cells.
n9f4039694a62: Light-emitting diodes (LEDs) based on colloidal InAs quantum dots (QDs) have emerged as promising light sources for the short-wave infrared (SWIR) range. However, their development is limited by relatively low photoluminescence quantum yield as well as intrinsic device design challenges. Here, we report LEDs with electroluminescence (EL) in the SWIR based on InAs/ZnSe core/shell colloidal QDs, synthesized via a seedless one-pot approach that enables the rapid growth of relatively large InAs cores. Zirconium-doped indium oxide (InZrO) was used as the bottom transparent electrode owing to its significantly higher infrared transparency compared to the commonly employed tin-doped indium oxide (ITO). These two key innovations pushed the EL beyond 1500 nm, with external quantum efficiencies of 3.0, 1.2, and 0.6% at 1093, 1198, and 1547 nm, respectively.
n677d8e82fc56: Conventional carbonization of semi-coke induces excessive ordering of aromatic skeletons, producing dense graphitic structures that hinder Na+ intercalation and suppress low-potential plateau capacity. Here, we develop a rapid thermomechanical coupling sintering strategy using moderate pressure to drive π–π interactions and topological reconfiguration of aromatic units. This process suppresses excessive graphitization while constructing interconnected, twisted pseudo-graphitic domains with abundant closed nanopores. At 1000 mA g–1, PTR-HC reaches 80% SOC in ≈14.4 min and retains 90.1% of its plateau capacity, enabled by abundant Na+ storage sites and rapid diffusion pathways. Kinetic analyses reveal accelerated Na+ transport and a thin, NaF-rich solid-electrolyte interphase with fewer organic components. In situ XRD and Raman attribute slope capacity to surface/defect adsorption and intercalation and the plateau capacity to quasi-metallic Na clusters in closed pores. This work establishes pressure-driven topological engineering as a promising strategy for upgrading semi-coke into fast-charging hard carbon with high plateau-capacity retention.
nadb66549bf6c: Interfacial losses at the perovskite/C60 and C60/metal contacts limit inverted perovskite solar cell performance. Here, we introduce a vacuum-evaporated molecule with giant spontaneous orientation polarization, 6F-2PI, for simultaneously tailoring both interfaces. Incorporating 6F-2PI increases the work function of perovskite, reducing the conduction band offset at the perovskite/C60 interface, which facilitates electron extraction. Concurrently, its phthalimide moieties passivate defect states, suppressing nonradiative recombination, as evidenced by a 0.03 eV recovery in quasi-Fermi level splitting. At the C60/metal interface, 6F-2PI also delivers efficient charge extraction, improved interfacial contact, and thermal resilience. Moreover, its hydrophobic fluorinated units prevent moisture ingress. Consequently, this dual-interface modulation boosts PCE from 18.5% to 22.5% with exceptional device stability, retaining over 90% of its initial efficiency after 2000 h under ambient conditions. Furthermore, this framework exhibits universal compatibility across both vacuum-deposited and solution-processed devices and simplifies processing for mass production.
ne455ea914345: Precise theranostics requires spatiotemporal control and high specificity to adapt to complex physiological microenvironments. Tetrahedral framework nucleic acids (tFNA), classic 3D DNA nanostructures, offer distinct advantages such as atomic-level structural precision, intrinsic programmability, and excellent biocompatibility. While traditional static tFNA lack dynamic responsiveness to external stimuli─severely limiting their clinical translation potential─the emergence of dynamically responsive tFNA has garnered increasing attention. These smart systems offer substantial advantages, including stimulus-triggered structural reconfiguration, targeted payload release, and real-time signal transduction. Despite rapid design innovations, a systematic summary of dynamic tFNA strategies remains lacking. Accordingly, we synthesize the design principles of responsive tFNA by categorizing their mechanisms into conformational rearrangement, chemical bond cleavage, and toehold-mediated strand displacement logic. We highlight their applications in precision diagnosis, smart therapeutics, and theranostics integration and discuss critical challenges in biological stability, scalable manufacturing, and biosecurity. By mapping current advancements and unresolved hurdles, this work provides a comprehensive reference for the rational design of responsive DNA nanodevices and discusses the challenges associated with the clinical translation of dynamic tFNA.
na915e59a073d: Seawater electrolysis is essential for sustainable green hydrogen production but remains hindered by chloride ions (Cl–)-induced corrosion of electrode catalysts. Herein, we report an “adsorption-guided protection” strategy to achieve the trade-off between corrosion resistance and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity for NiFe layered double hydroxide (NiFe-LDH). Unlike conventional strategies that aim solely to repel Cl–, this strategy incorporates Ti dopants as preferential Cl–-trapping centers. The Cl– dynamically adsorbed on Ti sites shields the OER-active Ni/Fe centers from corrosive attack and concurrently creates a localized electrostatic repulsion that inhibits further Cl– accumulation on the catalyst surface. NiFeTi-LDH exhibits high OER performance in alkaline seawater, achieving ampere-level current density with outstanding stability exceeding 3000 h. In situ spectroscopic analysis combined with theoretical calculations reveals that the Ti–Cl bonding not only lowers the energy barrier of the rate-determining step for OER intermediates but also induces an electrostatic repulsion effect that further excludes additional Cl– from approaching the active surface. This study offers insights into the reasonable design of high-performance and corrosion-resistant non-noble-metal catalysts for practical seawater electrolysis.
ndd2fce142a9b: Intravesical chemotherapy is a standard adjuvant treatment for nonmuscle-invasive bladder cancer after transurethral resection, but its efficacy is limited by drug exposure resulting from urinary dilution and physiological voiding. Most current delivery strategies aim to prolong the intravesical residence through mucoadhesion, depot formation, or sustained release. Although these approaches increase local drug availability, they do not directly address insufficient intracellular drug accumulation during the short instillation window. Here, we report a poly-l-glutamic acid-modified gold nanourchin platform, PGU3@DOX, designed to enhance intravesical chemotherapy by accelerating drug internalization by bladder cancer cells. By optimizing the nanoparticle morphology, we identified long-spiked gold nanourchins as the most effective architecture for rapid cellular uptake. The PLG coating enabled doxorubicin loading and supported pH-facilitated DOX release, while the internalized nanourchins induced lysosomal swelling and lysosomal membrane permeabilization in bladder cancer cells. Under a 1 h pulse exposure that mimics the short intravesical dwell-time window, PGU3@DOX showed greater cytotoxicity against bladder cancer cells after extracellular drug removal while showing lower toxicity toward normal urothelial cells. Furthermore, PGU3@DOX achieved a broader distribution and stronger damage in tumor spheroids than free DOX. In an orthotopic bladder cancer model, a single short-duration intravesical administration of PGU3@DOX significantly suppressed tumor progression without detectable acute hematological, hepatic, renal, or cardiac toxicity under the tested conditions. These findings support rapid cellular internalization as a complementary strategy to improve intravesical chemotherapy and provide a morphology-guided nanocarrier platform for enhancing drug delivery within short therapeutic exposure windows.
n2d926e1616bf: Molecular catalysts have been found to be selective for the CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR), with Faradaic efficiencies approaching 100% for two-electron products such as CO and formic acid. However, translating the intrinsic activity of well-defined molecular active sites into practical high-current-density electrolysis remains challenging due to molecular aggregation, poor electronic coupling with electrodes, and limited stability. In addition, multielectron molecular CO2RR is hampered by complex reaction pathways and insufficient adsorption of intermediates. This perspective discusses how nanostructured molecular architectures, from controlled aggregation and support interactions to reticular frameworks, fundamentally alter catalytic performance beyond what is achievable through conventional coordination chemistry alone. We highlight recent advances demonstrating that molecular dispersion, curvature-induced strain, nanoconfinement, and layered confinement can redirect reaction pathways, enabling multielectron reduction products such as methanol and ethanol. We further discuss emerging opportunities in computation-accelerated molecular discovery, strategies to address high overpotentials, and the integration of CO2 capture with electrochemical conversion. By engineering the microenvironment surrounding molecular active sites, we argue that the next generation of molecular electrocatalysts can achieve the activity, selectivity, and stability required for practical deployment.
na7ebaece2908: Early diagnosis and personalized management of chronic liver disease are critical for preventing disease progression and reducing mortality. However, existing diagnostic methods primarily depend on invasive blood sampling and laboratory‐based analyses, which limit their suitability for continuous, real‐world monitoring. In this study, we developed a skin‐conformal, wearable electrochemical biosensing platform capable of real time monitoring of liver health by continuously analyzing liver‐related metabolic biomarkers (creatine and lactate) in sweat. To improve sensor reliability, we introduced a universal enzyme immobilization strategy based on covalent organic frameworks, which enhances enzymatic stability and maintains catlytic activity under dynamic conditions. The fully integrated system supports efficient passive sweat collection, real time multi‐analyte detection, on‐board signal processing, and digital display. The platform was applied in preliminary human studies to track dynamic changes in sweat creatine and lactate in healthy individuals and participants with chronic liver disease. Overall, this work demonstrates a versatile wearable platform for noninvasive, continuous assisted evaluation of liver metabolic functions, contributing to the advancement of next‐generation personalized healthcare technologies.
n7c077fa20a89: A stable symbiosis within the microbiome‐host axis is essential for human health. However, preventing microbiome dysbiosis using biomaterials remains challenging due to their unpredictable influence on microbiome evolution. Inspired by the defensive niche of symbiotic mucosa, we have developed a biointerface that forms an engineered mucosa‐inspired dynamic niche to prevent pathogenic dysbiosis. This biointerface features a dynamic zwitterionic network that emulates the mucosa's biophysical defensive functions. Notably, by leveraging its dynamic niche, the biointerface restricts microbial attachment and aggregation, thereby preventing biofilm formation. Comprehensive metagenomic analyses reveal that microbial communities adapt to this biofilm‐preventive dynamic biointerface compositionally and functionally. In particular, Gram‐negative bacteria were relatively reduced, along with decreased abundance of pathways associated with virulence and biofilm formation. Consequently, the mucosa‐inspired biointerface intrinsically prevents the development of pathogenic dysbiosis. This study demonstrates the groundbreaking potential of material‐based niche engineering to guide the ecological shifts of microbial communities from the material scale.
n2a9889164d86: Pushing LiCoO2 to ≥4.5 V causes coupled degradation: electrolyte oxidation and cathode structural collapse, especially at high rates. Here, we propose a triphase synergistic gel‐electrolyte to tackle both failure modes. The system, constructed by in situ thermal polymerization, integrates an ether‐rich crosslinked polymer network, surface‐activated AlN fillers with Lewis acid–base sites, and a fluorinated electrolyte. This design regulates Li+ transport, confines free solvent molecules, and reconstructs the solvation sheath. More importantly, it induces a uniform, inorganic‐rich cathode–electrolyte interphase at an early stage. Consequently, LiCoO2‐based quasi‐solid‐state cells deliver exceptional stability: over 1000 cycles at 4.6 V and 5 C with an average decay of only ∼0.03% per cycle, and 85.98% capacity retention after 500 cycles in practical Si–C||LiCoO2 pouch cells. Operando EIS‐DRT analysis reveals that the triphase electrolyte substantially suppresses the growth and fluctuation of interphase‐related polarization at high voltage, making the remaining impedance evolution more governed by transport/contact processes. This work demonstrates that decoupling interfacial and structural degradation through a synergistic electrolyte design is key to realizing high‐voltage, high‐power, long‐life quasi‐solid‐state batteries.
n40e8acacb8e3: Mass transport at three-phase interfaces is a primary bottleneck for industrial gas-evolving electrodes due to severe bubble coverage and suppressed liquid renewal. Here, we establish the interfacial work of adhesion (ΔG ad)—quantified via spherical-tip AFM nanoindentation—as a predictive nanoscale descriptor of surface energetics under ambient conditions. ΔG ad captures the thermodynamic competition between electrolyte wetting and gas adhesion at the solid surface, thereby governing bubble-mediated mass transport. Using model MoS2 electrodes, we show that vertical structuring and phase engineering (Vhetero-MoS2) significantly increase the AFM-quantified ΔG ad. This heightened ΔG ad strengthens the solid-electrolyte affinity, effectively suppressing gas adhesion and reducing bubble blockage. In situ Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) and pseudopotential simulations consistently show that surfaces with higher ΔG ad yield smaller bubbles and enhanced interfacial renewal. Accordingly, the apparent aerophobicity follows from stronger electrolyte affinity via interfacial energy competition. Using hydrogen evolution as a representative gas-evolving reaction, the Vhetero-MoS2 electrode sustains stable hydrogen evolution at 1000 mA cm− 2. This work provides a unified energetic framework for three-phase interface engineering, establishing ΔG ad as a quantifiable, AFM-accessible metric for the rational design of high-performance gas-evolving electrodes.
n23e64d2dc19e: Liquid cell transmission electron microscopy (LCTEM) is a rising technique for probing dynamic processes and structural transformations in liquid environments at the nanoscale. However, its broader application is largely constrained by limited spatial resolution, which arises from electron scattering by the encapsulating membranes and the liquid layer. Recent advances in instrument design, micro‐electro‐mechanical system (MEMS)‐based cells, and ultrathin window materials have substantially improved imaging quality, yet achieving atomic‐scale resolution in liquids remains a formidable challenge. This review provides a comprehensive overview of such strategies developed to enhance the spatial resolution of LCTEM, emphasizing the roles of liquid layer thickness, MEMS design, and cell configuration. We highlight representative approaches, such as reducing liquid and membrane thicknesses, optimizing MEMS architectures, and employing grid‐based liquid cells, and discuss their underlying mechanisms and recent progress.
